source: DMZ Scuba site research: facts cross-checked against the cited agency and archaeological records; summaries written by DMZ Scuba.

lake-michigan.name: Lake Michigan
notes: Summer brings a thermocline: below it, expect 40–45°F water even when the surface is warm.
Invasive quagga and zebra mussels coat most wrecks and keep the water unusually clear.
Fresh water: you need less weight than in the sea.

whs.name: Wisconsin Shipwrecks — Wisconsin Historical Society & Wisconsin Sea Grant

nps.name: National Park Service — Sleeping Bear Dunes shipwrecks

geonames-gilboa-fixture-2564638.name: Gilboa Quarry
geonames-gilboa-fixture-2564638.access: Private quarry; deep side requires certification or an instructor
highlights: Sunken planes and helicopters
Nemo's Garden underwater biosphere
geonames-gilboa-fixture-2564638.summary: A spring-fed former limestone quarry west of Findlay, Ohio, popular for training and deep diving. It has sunken aircraft and vehicles and clear water, with a deep side to about 137-140 ft.

mx-cozumel-c53.name: C-53 Felipe Xicoténcatl Wreck
mx-cozumel-c53.depthNote: Superstructure at 40-50 ft, sand at 80 ft
highlights: Nudibranchs, shrimps, octopus and morays
Engine room can be penetrated with training
hazards: Interior penetration needs wreck training and a light
mx-cozumel-c53.summary: A Mexican navy minesweeper sunk as an artificial reef, sheltered with little current and good visibility. The upper decks suit intermediate divers; entering the engine room requires wreck training.

mx-cozumel-colombia.name: Colombia Reef
highlights: Barrel sponges, black coral, pinnacles

mx-cozumel-maracaibo.name: Maracaibo Reef
highlights: Spotted eagle rays and turtles
Sharks and eagle rays
hazards: Extreme currents, big swells and surf
mx-cozumel-maracaibo.summary: One of Cozumel's deepest, most exposed sites at the island's south end, with a wall starting near 27 m. Strong currents and swell make it advanced-only; eagle rays, turtles and sharks reward the effort.

mx-cozumel-palancar-caves.name: Palancar Caves
highlights: Walls, slopes and swim-throughs
hazards: Caves need solid buoyancy control

mx-cozumel-palancar-gardens.name: Palancar Gardens
highlights: Very clear water
Angelfish, damselfish and octopus

mx-cozumel-punta-tunich.name: Punta Tunich Reef
hazards: Strong, turbulent currents

mx-cozumel-tormentos.name: Tormentos Reef
highlights: Spotted moray eels
Tunnels, overhangs and sea fans
mx-cozumel-tormentos.summary: A mid-depth reef north of the main reef line with tunnels, overhangs and plenty of morays. Current runs faster than at most central reefs, so it suits intermediate divers.

mx-cozumel-yucab.name: Yucab Reef
highlights: Dense schools of blue chromis and queen angelfish
Sand, coral and overhang terrain
mx-cozumel-yucab.summary: A mid-depth reef off Cozumel's west coast with sand, coral heads and small overhangs. Fish numbers are high and the current is usually gentle, so it suits divers with a little experience.

noaa-fknms-adelaide-baker.name: Adelaide Baker
highlights: Iron mast and hull remains with gorgonians and sponges
noaa-fknms-adelaide-baker.summary: The scattered remains of a three-masted sailing ship wrecked in 1889, lying in about 20 feet near Duck Key and covered with sponges, gorgonians and corals.
sources: NOAA Florida Keys National Marine Sanctuary

noaa-fknms-adolphus-busch-wreck.name: Adolphus Busch Wreck
noaa-fknms-adolphus-busch-wreck.summary: A 210-foot freighter standing upright on sand near Looe Key in the Lower Keys, sunk in 1998 as an artificial reef and now part of the Florida Keys shipwreck trail.
sources: Florida Keys & Key West tourism council

noaa-fknms-alligator-reef.name: Alligator Reef
highlights: Historic lighthouse marks the reef
Over 600 reef fish species recorded
noaa-fknms-alligator-reef.summary: A shallow protected bank reef off the Alligator lighthouse, with spur-and-groove coral and a big fish list. Calm depths make it a good fit for newer divers and snorkelers.
sources: NOAA Florida Keys National Marine Sanctuary

noaa-fknms-amesbury-wreck.name: Amesbury Wreck
highlights: Two hull sections 600 ft apart with 5-inch gun mount
sources: NOAA Florida Keys National Marine Sanctuary
NOAA Florida Keys National Marine Sanctuary

noaa-fknms-benwood-wreck.name: Benwood Wreck
highlights: Intact bow rising about 25 ft off the bottom
Resident porkfish, goatfish and schoolmaster snapper
noaa-fknms-benwood-wreck.summary: A freighter lost in 1942 and now a Florida Keys Shipwreck Trail dive off Key Largo, lying in 25-45 ft among low reef and sand. The bow is the most complete section, and schooling snapper and porkfish make it a popular, comfortable wreck dive.
sources: NOAA Florida Keys National Marine Sanctuary

noaa-fknms-bibb-wreck.name: Bibb Wreck
hazards: Current can make the wreck undiveable at times
noaa-fknms-bibb-wreck.summary: The Duane's sister cutter, lying on its side in deeper water off Key Largo. It is a deeper, advanced dive, and current can shut it down on some days.

noaa-fknms-duane-wreck.name: Duane Wreck
noaa-fknms-duane-wreck.depthNote: Mast 60 ft, bridge 70 ft, main deck 100 ft, sand 120 ft
highlights: Intact upright cutter with rails, ladders and props
Multilevel dive from mast down to main deck
hazards: Gulf Stream current can be fierce at times
noaa-fknms-duane-wreck.summary: A 327-foot Coast Guard cutter sitting upright on sand near Molasses Reef, with the mast near 60 feet and decks stepping down to 120. Currents can run hard, but it makes an easy multilevel wreck dive.
sources: NOAA Florida Keys National Marine Sanctuary

noaa-fknms-eagle-wreck.name: Eagle Wreck
noaa-fknms-eagle-wreck.depthNote: Rails 70 ft, prop and rudder 110 ft
highlights: Goliath groupers and bull sharks
Schooling jacks around the hull
Propeller and rudder still intact
hazards: Wreck broken in half by Hurricane Georges
noaa-fknms-eagle-wreck.summary: A 287-foot freighter resting on its starboard side off Islamorada, with rails near 70 feet and propeller at 110. Big groupers, bull sharks and jacks circle the wreck.
sources: NOAA Florida Keys National Marine Sanctuary

noaa-fknms-eastern-dry-rocks.name: Eastern Dry Rocks
highlights: Coral fingers and sand-floored canyons
noaa-fknms-eastern-dry-rocks.summary: A small bank reef near Key West packing several reef habitats into about 90 acres, with rubble, coral ridges and sandy canyons in shallow water.
sources: NOAA Florida Keys National Marine Sanctuary

noaa-fknms-grecian-rocks.name: Grecian Rocks
highlights: Purple fan corals swaying in the current
noaa-fknms-grecian-rocks.summary: A shallow patch reef off Key Largo beside the Christ of the Abyss site, whose crest breaks the surface at high tide. It is sheltered enough to dive or snorkel on breezy days and is rich in fan corals and reef fish.

noaa-fknms-joe-s-tug-wreck.name: Joe's Tug Wreck
highlights: Moray eels and schools of fish in the hull
Resident goliath grouper known as Elvis
noaa-fknms-joe-s-tug-wreck.summary: A 75-foot steel shrimp boat, not a tug, lying in two halves in about 65 feet off Key West. A popular novice wreck with schooling fish, morays and often excellent visibility.

noaa-fknms-looe-key.name: Looe Key
noaa-fknms-looe-key.access: Sanctuary Preservation Area with special regulations; boat only
noaa-fknms-looe-key.summary: A spur-and-groove coral reef about six miles offshore of Ramrod and Big Pine Keys, protected as a sanctuary preservation area. Shallow coral fingers and sand channels hold reef sharks, rays and groupers.
sources: NOAA Florida Keys National Marine Sanctuary

noaa-fknms-molasses-reef.name: Molasses Reef
highlights: Boulder corals on a spur-and-groove outer reef
Ship's winch and old Spanish anchor on the bottom
noaa-fknms-molasses-reef.summary: Key Largo's busiest outer reef, with spur-and-groove coral, big boulder corals and plentiful fish. Water is often clear, and a winch and an old anchor lie off the lighthouse.
sources: NOAA Florida Keys National Marine Sanctuary

noaa-fknms-newfound-harbor.name: Newfound Harbor
highlights: Boulder, star and giant brain corals
noaa-fknms-newfound-harbor.summary: A shallow inshore patch reef off Little Palm Island with large boulder, star and brain corals and reef fish, all within 18 feet of the surface.
sources: NOAA Florida Keys National Marine Sanctuary

noaa-fknms-north-dry-rocks.name: North Dry Rocks
highlights: Coral mounds with abundant tropical fish

noaa-fknms-pickles-reef.name: Pickles Reef
highlights: Juvenile nurse sharks and stingrays in sand channels
Remains of the Pickle Barrel civil-war era wreck
noaa-fknms-pickles-reef.summary: A shallow spur-and-groove reef off Key Largo with barrel-shaped coral heads, easy navigation and sea fans. Gentle depths suit new divers and snorkelers, and small fish make it a good photo site.

noaa-fknms-rock-key.name: Rock Key
highlights: Coral fingers and sand-floored canyons
noaa-fknms-rock-key.summary: A bank reef off Key West made up of a rubble zone, long coral fingers and sandy, coral-lined canyons, in water shallow enough for relaxed dives.
sources: NOAA Florida Keys National Marine Sanctuary

noaa-fknms-san-pedro-wreck.name: San Pedro Wreck
noaa-fknms-san-pedro-wreck.access: State of Florida Underwater Archaeological Preserve
highlights: Ballast pile of a 1733 Spanish fleet wreck
noaa-fknms-san-pedro-wreck.summary: The ballast mound of a Spanish ship lost in the 1733 hurricane, resting in about 18 feet south of Indian Key. It is a protected state archaeological preserve.
sources: NOAA Florida Keys National Marine Sanctuary

noaa-fknms-sand-key-reef.name: Sand Key Reef
highlights: Spur-and-groove reef beside a 1853 iron lighthouse
hazards: Fire coral common on sections of the reef
noaa-fknms-sand-key-reef.summary: A spur-and-groove reef seven miles off Key West, topped by a historic red iron lighthouse. Coral ridges rise in shallow water and the south side slopes off to a deeper ledge; visibility swings widely with wind and tide.
sources: NOAA Florida Keys National Marine Sanctuary

noaa-fknms-snapper-ledge.name: Snapper Ledge
highlights: Huge boulder brain coral
Yellowtail snapper, nurse sharks, morays
noaa-fknms-snapper-ledge.summary: A shallow Key Largo ledge reef suited to open-water divers, known for a very large boulder brain coral and schools of snapper with nurse sharks and morays around.

noaa-fknms-sombrero-reef.name: Sombrero Reef
highlights: Classic spur-and-groove reef formation
noaa-fknms-sombrero-reef.summary: A large spur-and-groove reef in the Middle Keys, shallower than 30 feet inside its protected zone and a favourite for both snorkelers and divers.
sources: NOAA Florida Keys National Marine Sanctuary

noaa-fknms-spiegel-grove-wreck.name: Spiegel Grove Wreck
highlights: Huge wreck: one dive covers only a fraction of it
hazards: Silt-outs inside the hull cause disorientation
Overhead environment beyond ambient light
noaa-fknms-spiegel-grove-wreck.summary: A 510-ft Navy landing ship dock sunk off Key Largo as an artificial reef, with its top deck near 60 ft and hull to about 135 ft. Its sheer size rewards repeat dives, but depth and a silt-prone interior make it an advanced-diver wreck.

noaa-fknms-vandenberg-wreck.name: Vandenberg Wreck
noaa-fknms-vandenberg-wreck.depthNote: Superstructure 45 ft, hull on sand about 145 ft
highlights: About 100 ft of vertical relief
noaa-fknms-vandenberg-wreck.summary: A 523-foot former missile-tracking ship sunk off Key West, one of the largest purpose-sunk wrecks anywhere. Its hull sits at about 145 feet while the top reaches 45 feet, so there is a profile for most divers.
sources: Florida Keys & Key West tourism council

odm-02taid.name: Le Sournois
highlights: Goatfish, surgeonfish, moray eels, eagle rays

odm-04yvg4.name: Acacia Bay
highlights: Cliff faces and a diver-made reference ring
hazards: Silts up easily - good buoyancy needed
sources: Scubago (NZ Dive School / Dive Whakatane listings)

odm-05fscu.name: MV Mikhail Lermontov, wreck
hazards: Silt bottom, limited visibility
odm-05fscu.summary: A 176 m Soviet cruise liner that sank in 1986 in Port Gore and still lies largely intact on her side. The top is an easy dive near 12 m, while the hull, penetration and decompression dives reach about 36-38 m; visibility is often modest.

odm-05nt11.name: Baie Ternay Marine Park
odm-05nt11.access: Marine park permit fee, paid through the dive operator
highlights: Nurse sharks under ledges

odm-065uo7.name: Mwana Wa Mwana
highlights: Coral bommies with glassfish, frogfish

odm-071n8b.name: Windmill Beach
highlights: Large granite outcrops and boulders

odm-0cavlp.name: Eagle Ray Rock
highlights: Cut and ravine on a steep vertical wall
Colourful sponges, coral pillars, rays

odm-0f596l.name: Tian Xiang (Wreck)
odm-0f596l.depthNote: Community depth 36 m is too shallow; operators give 45-46 m
highlights: 44 m longliner sunk 2014 as artificial reef

odm-0go2oo.name: Boulari Plateau Manta
highlights: Manta rays (regular visitors to the pass)

odm-0h8fcy.name: Eagle Ray Pass
highlights: Coral canyon spilling onto the wall
Eagle rays cruising along the wall
Sponges, gorgonians and black coral
odm-0h8fcy.summary: A North Wall dive where a coral canyon cuts through the reef and spills onto a near-vertical wall at about 100 ft, with the wall top only about 45 ft down. Eagle rays are regular visitors along the wall face.

odm-0h9a3p.name: West Wall
highlights: Three sunken galleon cannons

odm-0ijygj.name: Tanjung Sari
highlights: Canyon-like rock formations
odm-0ijygj.summary: Reef next to Padang Bai's Blue Lagoon (the same area is also listed under this name): a reef top near 8 m sloping to roughly 18-20 m, with canyon-like rock formations toward the channel.

odm-0je3fz.name: Police Corner
highlights: Large overhang forming a cave-like cathedral
Whitetip reef sharks and bumphead parrotfish
hazards: Current can pick up mid-dive
odm-0je3fz.summary: A current-swept slope in central Komodo with a large cave-like overhang. Best at slack or mild incoming tide; reef sharks, bumphead parrotfish and fusiliers draw advanced divers.

odm-0k86ko.name: Jardin Japonais
highlights: Butterflyfish, barracuda, lionfish, lobsters

odm-0nrk72.name: West End Wall
highlights: Eagle rays, groupers and turtles
Barracuda and the odd wahoo
odm-0nrk72.summary: A sheer, healthy wall off the western tip of Roatán that is usually dived as a gentle drift toward Texas. Eagle rays, groupers, turtles and passing pelagics are the draw; operators recommend Advanced certification and nitrox.

odm-0ovrq9.name: Kolo-Kolo
highlights: Fan and table corals, caves, overhangs
Macro: scorpion leaf fish, squat lobsters

odm-0p83wz.name: Moc Che Deep
highlights: Sea turtles and giant barracuda

odm-0p9s6f.name: Les 3 Pitons
odm-0p9s6f.depthNote: Pinnacles rise from 40 m to tops at 10 m and 5 m
highlights: Three pinnacles each with a freshwater spring
Turtles, surgeonfish, clownfish

odm-0qx1yw.name: Tatawa Kecil
highlights: Rock formations, swim-throughs and boulders
Eagle rays, giant trevally and sharks
hazards: Very strong current; tidal window needed
odm-0qx1yw.summary: A rocky islet in the Linta Strait between Komodo and Rinca with swim-throughs, boulders and coral gardens. Current is strong to very strong, so it is for experienced divers timing the tide; sharks and rays patrol.

odm-0u40l8.name: Melissa’s Garden
highlights: Vividly coloured coral garden
odm-0u40l8.summary: Coral garden near Piaynemo, rated one of Raja Ampat's most colourful dives. Rated for all levels, with depth from about 5 to 30 m and current that can range from mild to strong.

odm-0y8sua.name: Overheat Reef
highlights: Neck crabs and small critters

odm-0zw3ig.name: La Faille d Arue
odm-0zw3ig.depthNote: Wall starts about 15 ft; most diving 50-80 ft, cave near 80 ft
highlights: Coral wall with a cave/fault at about 80 ft

odm-10qe1n.name: White Hole (62)
highlights: Schools of tarpon
Sea turtles
Eagle rays

odm-11x7oc.name: Kingston Wall
highlights: Eagle rays, Napoleon wrasse, turtles
Small caves and crevices in the wall

odm-12846y.name: 2 Mile Stringer
highlights: Frogfish, paperfish and ghost pipefish
Honeycomb morays hunting; turtles feeding
hazards: Best only with little current and no surge
odm-12846y.summary: Twin rocky outcrops at the south end of Two Mile Reef, shallow at about 9-13 m. Good for Open Water divers on calm days, with frogfish, rays and morays on the rocks.

odm-170szf.name: L’Eveillé
highlights: Small arch and chimney on the drop-off
Nudibranchs, morays, occasional shark
odm-170szf.summary: The southern end of the Flic en Flac drop-off, a wall dive with a small arch and chimney at about 25 m. Expect varied reef fish, nudibranchs and morays; operators rate it advanced.

odm-17xl14.name: Cane Bay
odm-17xl14.depthNote: Wall begins near 26-40 ft and drops past 3,000 ft
highlights: Sand chutes through coral gardens to a wall
odm-17xl14.summary: A wall off Cane Bay Beach on St. Croix's north shore, reached from the beach or by boat. Coral gardens and sand chutes lead to a sheer drop-off that suits divers of all levels.

odm-1c0768.name: Playa Grandi / Playa Piscado
highlights: Sea turtles near the fishermen's pier
odm-1c0768.summary: Fishermen's beach on the west coast where turtles gather near shore. Easily accessible shore dive with a steep wall and good chances of turtles.

odm-1ch1rz.name: Aquarium
highlights: Colourful coral heads with many reef fish
odm-1ch1rz.summary: A very shallow, sheltered coral garden in the Bora Bora lagoon south of Pitiu Uta, popular for beginners and snorkelers. Large coral heads hold a dense variety of reef fish, with the occasional eagle ray passing through.

odm-1d0xn5.name: Stonehenge
highlights: Swim-throughs, holes and overhangs in deeper areas

odm-1f6xn6.name: Babylon, Cayman
odm-1f6xn6.mooring: Mooring buoy; mooring pin at 50 ft
highlights: Freestanding pinnacle beside the wall
Corals and sponges grow across the gap
Black coral and gorgonian fans between pinnacle and wall
odm-1f6xn6.summary: A North Wall classic where a freestanding pinnacle rises from over 100 ft to within 45 ft of the surface, set tight against the main wall. The gap between is full of black coral and gorgonians, and the dive is easy enough for first-time ocean divers.

odm-1gh8ip.name: Bear’s Den
odm-1gh8ip.depthNote: Cavern entrance at about 25 ft; swim-through begins near 50 ft
highlights: Large cavern with light beams and glassy sweepers
Swim-throughs and canyons near the mooring

odm-1ghrli.name: M.V. Alpha Funguo
highlights: 48 m trawler sunk 2002 as artificial reef
odm-1ghrli.summary: A 48 m fishing trawler deliberately sunk off Diani in 2002, the first purpose-sunk wreck on the East African coast. Its deck starts around 17 m and the sand lies near 28 m, and it has become an artificial reef with large fish.

odm-1heita.name: Liberty Coral Garden
odm-1heita.summary: A shallow reef beside the Liberty wreck at Tulamben where the brightest coral and most macro life sit around 5 m, with the site only reaching about 10 m. Suited to beginners and snorkelers.

odm-1j010k.name: The BISTRO - Shark Dive AQUATREK
hazards: Bull and other sharks pass close during the feed

odm-1k1u1e.name: Grand Mal Wall
highlights: S-shaped pillar coral wall with canyons
Southern stingrays, lobster, octopus
odm-1k1u1e.summary: A reef north of St George's harbour in Grand Mal Bay, with an S-shaped pillar-coral wall cut by canyons. Good as a drift dive for experienced divers, though beginners can also enjoy it; rays, lobster and octopus are common.

odm-1lmu41.name: Apollo
highlights: School of hundreds of barracuda
odm-1lmu41.summary: A deep sloping reef off Una Una's south cape, starting around 22 m and running to 40-45 m. The draw is a huge school of barracuda, sometimes over a thousand, that circles curiously around divers.

odm-1pp7rr.name: Saba
highlights: Small sunken tugboat with abundant sea life
odm-1pp7rr.summary: Small sunken tugboat lying in the shallows at only about 5 m, reached by a short boat ride from Mambo Beach. Less visited than the Tugboat Wreck and ringed by plenty of fish.
sources: Bluewater Dive Travel (Scuba Lodge & Ocean Suites)

odm-1qb399.name: Malpelo
odm-1qb399.reason: Whole oceanic island and sanctuary with many separate dive sites

odm-1thj17.name: Ghost Bay
highlights: Ghost pipefish, mimic octopus, stonefish

odm-1urrp8.name: Rainbow Warrior
odm-1urrp8.summary: The former Greenpeace flagship, bombed in 1985 and sunk off the Cavalli Islands as a dive wreck. She rests upright with the top around 15-18 m and the seabed near 27 m, and is covered in jewel anemones; the depth calls for advanced training.

odm-1vehdj.name: Pointe Lezarde
highlights: Wall with lobsters, arrow crabs and seahorses

odm-1vh2op.name: Haapiti
highlights: Blacktip, grey and lemon sharks, napoleon wrasse
odm-1vh2op.summary: An outer-reef dive on Bora Bora's north side along an easy coral slope with tunnels, swim-throughs and canyons. Reef sharks, trigger fish and napoleon wrasse are common, and the depth to about 30 m keeps it manageable for most certified divers.

odm-1vyx35.name: Bonnie's Arch
highlights: Large coral archway
Horse-eye jacks, turtles, tarpon and seahorses
odm-1vyx35.summary: A scenic reef off Northwest Point centred on a curving natural coral arch roughly 50 ft across, with the base of the arch near 70 ft. Ridges and valleys around it hold sponges, angelfish, tarpon, horse-eye jacks and turtles.

odm-1z8mif.name: Big Dipper
hazards: Rated for advanced divers

odm-208u5q.name: Steves Ledge
highlights: Plate coral, clownfish, rays, grouper

odm-20tsqf.name: Aruba
odm-20tsqf.reason: Whole island, not a single dive site

odm-21lc8i.name: Simon’s Reef
highlights: Canyons and big coral bommies
Reef sharks, turtles, schooling fish
odm-21lc8i.summary: A deep mid-channel site north of the Gilis with canyons and large bommies rising from sand. Channel currents funnel in schooling fish, reef sharks and turtles; suited to advanced divers.

odm-23dnf7.name: Sec Pate
odm-23dnf7.depthNote: Summit about 15 m; base drops to about 200 m
highlights: Queen angelfish, triggerfish, morays, turtles

odm-24x4mh.name: North Star
highlights: Danish anchor embedded in the wall at about 60 ft

odm-25k7wh.name: Hopscotch
highlights: Ribbon eels and frogfish in ledges
Schooling coachman and goldies

odm-26x896.name: Watamula
highlights: Pristine hard coral field with barrel sponges
Cleaning stations
hazards: Several currents; dive with a guide
odm-26x896.summary: Boat drift dive at the northwest tip of the island with pristine hard coral and big barrel sponges. Several meeting currents make it a site for experienced divers, ideally with a guide.

odm-299gud.name: Office
highlights: Leopard and whitetip sharks, potato bass
Manta cleaning stations on the ledges
odm-299gud.summary: A classic northern reef of ledges and sandy channels about 15 km offshore, with manta cleaning stations and regular leopard and whitetip sharks. Visibility is often good; current can make it harder.

odm-29qwuq.name: Tapu
highlights: Blacktip and lemon sharks, giant wrasse, eagle rays
odm-29qwuq.summary: Bora Bora's classic shark dive on the outer reef beside the pass and Motu Tapu. Coral begins around 10 m and a drop-off runs to roughly 40 m, with many blacktip and lemon sharks, wrasse and turtles. Depth discipline matters because the wall drops away quickly.

odm-2a5bqo.name: Madrépore Manta Point
highlights: Fan coral field; whitetips, turtles, nurse sharks

odm-2aujtr.name: Riko Riko cave
highlights: Largest sea cave by volume in the southern hemisphere
hazards: Boat traffic - do not surface in mid water

odm-2dvynj.name: Crystal Rock Komodo
highlights: White-tip and grey reef sharks, giant trevally
Giant sea fans, barrel sponges, plate corals
hazards: Strong current; depth reached quickly
odm-2dvynj.summary: North Komodo pinnacle in the lee of Gili Lawa Laut, a little more sheltered than Castle Rock but still current-swept. Sharks, trevally and turtles patrol corals-covered slopes to roughly 25-30 m; advanced divers only.

odm-2eklmp.name: Champagne
highlights: Underwater hot-spring bubbles; seahorses, frogfish, squid
odm-2eklmp.summary: A reef over a submerged hot spring at the northern edge of the Soufrière Scotts Head Marine Reserve, where warm bubbles rise around the dive. Calm and easy for all levels, with seahorses and frogfish.

odm-2etrly.name: Epave Franjack, wreck
odm-2etrly.summary: A 50 m Danish cargo vessel scuttled in 1996 in the Cousteau Reserve and resting upright on its keel at about 23 m. Accessible to Open Water divers, it can be penetrated and has become an artificial reef.

odm-2g6ryp.name: La lengua
highlights: Dozing sharks along a short wall; morays, turtles

odm-2i2luq.name: Ship Wreck Point
highlights: One of the healthiest reefs around Curaçao, aquarium-like fish life
odm-2i2luq.summary: Short boat dive off the Mambo Beach area on a reef described as one of the healthiest around Curaçao, with fish life like an aquarium.
sources: Bluewater Dive Travel (Scuba Lodge & Ocean Suites)

odm-2jdpqo.name: Willy T (Wreck)
odm-2jdpqo.depthNote: Moved from Norman Island; now in Key Bay, Peter Island
highlights: Replica pirates and cannons; on-deck bar to visit
odm-2jdpqo.summary: A former floating bar sunk in 2019 off Peter Island as an artificial reef. Its masts reach roughly 35-38 ft, the hull rests on sand near 65 ft, and divers can enter the decorated wreck.

odm-2kqbro.name: St Leonards Pier
odm-2kqbro.access: No jumping or diving off the pier structures
hazards: Shallow water and submerged obstacles
Strong currents

odm-2l0jei.name: St. Pierre
hazards: Not for beginners when current runs

odm-2m4geb.name: Miracle Waters
highlights: Sunken buses, aeroplane and helicopter
Training platforms at several depths
odm-2m4geb.summary: Freshwater quarry lake near Brits used for training and recreational dives, about 33 m deep. Sunken buses, an aircraft and a helicopter sit at 14-30 m, with visibility of roughly 5-10 m.

odm-2m5kya.name: Veronica L Wreck
highlights: Corals, sponges, shrimp, crabs and eels on the barge
odm-2m5kya.summary: A small freighter or barge wreck resting upright in about 15 m in St George's Harbour, softly colonised by coral and sponge. Gentle currents and shallow depth make it a popular novice and night dive.

odm-2oqc9b.name: Vatu Express
highlights: Soft coral wall with reef fish and pelagics

odm-2q4np6.name: Iglesia
highlights: Rock formations with reef sharks and turtles
odm-2q4np6.summary: A reef of separate rock formations linked by sand in Coiba National Park, dived anywhere from 12 to 30 m. Rock walls and overhangs create cathedral-like passages with reef sharks and turtles, best with a little current.

odm-2ulqus.name: Sec Delgrès
odm-2ulqus.depthNote: Wall continues below 60 m; upper section dived
highlights: Sponges, gorgonians, grunts, turtles, barracuda
odm-2ulqus.summary: A wall below Fort Delgrès off Basse-Terre, dropping beyond 60 m but easily enjoyed in the upper part by Open Water divers. Sponges, gorgonians and schools of grunts decorate the slope, with turtles, resting rays and curious barracuda.

odm-2zfnd1.name: Cod Hole
highlights: Twin bommies with a natural arch, wobbegongs
sources: Mudgee Dive and Travel (Scuba Haven info)

odm-32bf60.name: Puri Jati
odm-32bf60.depthNote: Plateau 5-7 m, slope to about 20 m; average rarely over 12 m
highlights: Ghost pipefish, sea moths, nudibranchs
Cup corals scattered over black sand
odm-32bf60.summary: A black-sand muck site off a beach on Bali's north coast, entered from shore. The bottom is a gentle sandy slope, mostly shallow, with ghost pipefish, sea moths and nudibranchs within the first few metres, so dives can run long.

odm-32gwfy.name: Pierre au préfet
highlights: Large coral head with triggerfish, rays and barracuda

odm-32k2pn.name: Desecheo Island
odm-32k2pn.access: Marine reserve; boat access only, go with professionals
highlights: Rock outcroppings, lobsters and pillar coral
hazards: East or south winds can create offshore currents

odm-334ze5.name: Jardines
highlights: Small coral and sponge wall with morays and trunkfish
Garden-like growth and small overhangs
odm-334ze5.summary: A shallow, sheltered reef off Playa del Carmen with almost no current, a low coral-and-sponge wall and small overhangs. An easy choice for novices and relaxed photography.

odm-33ctmu.name: Frederiksted Pier
highlights: World-class macro life on sponge-covered pilings
hazards: Closed to diving when a cruise ship is in port
odm-33ctmu.summary: Old pier pilings on St. Croix's west coast, dived from the pier or the shore. Mostly shallow, deepening toward the far end, it is encrusted with sponges and coral and suited to every level, including night dives.

odm-35f8d5.name: Gili Tepekong, Candidasa
highlights: Whitetip and blacktip reef sharks
Sweetlips, jacks and grouper; mola-mola
hazards: Strong currents, surge and down-currents
odm-35f8d5.summary: An offshore islet off Candidasa with the Blue Hole and Canyon dive routes. Tough currents and surge restrict it to experienced divers, who may see reef sharks, large fish schools and sometimes mola-mola.

odm-36i3cl.name: Northern Exposure
highlights: Eel garden and azure vase sponges
Large coral structures, crustaceans and turtles
odm-36i3cl.summary: A gently sloping reef off St George's that starts on a sandy patch with conch and an eel garden, then drops to about 22 m. Little current and plenty of fish and sponges make it good for all levels and photography.

odm-37cjg5.name: Eelskins
highlights: Gullies, overhangs and swim-throughs

odm-399vs3.name: Mioskun
highlights: Wobbegong sharks on the reef
Soft-coral bommies and a giant clam
odm-399vs3.summary: A forgiving Dampier Strait reef with a sloping ridge, bommies smothered in soft coral and a mild current. Wobbegong sharks are the signature sighting, plus pygmy seahorses and a giant clam in the shallows.

odm-3ftcdp.name: Hilma Hooker (Wreck) (43)
hazards: Moderate to strong current

odm-3h1iv3.name: Great Blue Hole
odm-3h1iv3.depthNote: Sinkhole is 124 m deep; recreational dives go to about 40 m (130 ft)
highlights: Large stalactites and stalagmites in the sinkhole
odm-3h1iv3.summary: Circular marine sinkhole on Lighthouse Reef, 124 m deep. Advanced divers descend to about 40 m (130 ft) to see big stalactites, with very limited bottom time.

odm-3j8n9y.name: SS President Coolidge (Wreck)
hazards: Serious decompression issues; deep wreck
odm-3j8n9y.summary: A 199 m WWII troopship lying on its side off Luganville, reached from the beach. The bow sits near 20 m and the stern near 70 m, so most of it is deep and involves deco. Holds, jeeps and 'The Lady' statue make it a multi-day wreck.

odm-3k9v51.name: Stella Maris / Ocean Encounters
odm-3k9v51.access: House reef inside the Curaçao Marine Park (LionsDive / Ocean Encounters)
highlights: Coral restoration nurseries on the shallow reef
odm-3k9v51.summary: Fringing reef right off the LionsDive resort beach, inside the Curaçao Marine Park, so divers can simply walk in. Coral-restoration nurseries are rebuilding the shallow reef.

odm-3l2wvd.name: Guacamaya Island
highlights: Small island teeming with fish

odm-3mawy6.name: Maomao Arch
odm-3mawy6.access: Passage through the arch depends on sea conditions
highlights: Relaxing shallow cave dive

odm-3oac87.name: Amazon
highlights: Leopard, whitetip and grey reef sharks
Hammerheads at times; whale song in season
hazards: Difficult drift; descend quickly
odm-3oac87.summary: Tofo's furthest and most demanding reef, an L-shaped ridge with craters and swim-throughs about 20 km offshore. Good visibility and plenty of sharks, rays and pelagics; the drift can be difficult, so it is for experienced divers.

odm-3p0s1i.name: Mwanamochi
highlights: Coral head with small reef fish; turtles

odm-3pwpeo.name: Sweet Dreams (59)
highlights: Sea turtle protected nesting area

odm-3qmw8k.name: Vallée aux Mérous
highlights: Fault edged with gorgonians, groupers and snapper

odm-3r9khb.name: Batu Bolong, Nusa Penida
highlights: Pelagics, sharks, rays and Mola mola
hazards: Strongest, fully exposed current of Nusa Penida sites

odm-3sfhkc.name: Julian Rocks - Split Bommie
highlights: Wobbegongs and grey nurse sharks

odm-3tbzqa.name: MV Shakem, wreck
highlights: Intact freighter with swim-throughs, black coral and gorgonians
hazards: Depth and strong currents

odm-3uiy9m.name: Mangrove Point Lembongan
highlights: Reef fish and turtles on a relaxed drift

odm-3w81yh.name: Canyon Reef
highlights: Network of canyons and swim-throughs
Frogfish, channel crabs, lobster, morays, nurse shark
hazards: Up-and-down profile; needs good buoyancy
odm-3w81yh.summary: A shallow web of reef fingers and canyons dropping to about 60 ft, ideal for practicing buoyancy. Swim-throughs shelter lobster, crabs, morays and frogfish, and open-water divers with decent control can manage it.

odm-3xa6x3.name: Barco Hundido - Wreck Cadete Juan Escutia C-56
highlights: Navy minesweeper scuttled in 2000, covered in coral
Stingrays, eels and barracuda
odm-3xa6x3.summary: A decommissioned Mexican navy minesweeper put on the bottom in 2000 inside the Puerto Morelos reef park. It lies in roughly 25 to 30 m, is rated for experienced divers, and is now crusted in coral with rays, eels and barracuda around it.

odm-3xaadg.name: Long Beach Simons Town
highlights: Small wrecks on a compass navigation route

odm-3y6sgu.name: Duppy Waters
highlights: Large barrel sponges, big grouper and turtles

odm-3ynr20.name: Cape Mansuar
highlights: Fusilier schools and reef sharks
odm-3ynr20.summary: A point on the western tip of Mansuar island where a coral garden, wall and sloping reef meet the Dampier Strait. Currents vary, sometimes giving a drift along the island, and dives suit intermediate divers.

odm-3ztzzl.name: Black Forest (Candi City)
highlights: Unique hard coral formations
Blacktip reef sharks and stingrays
odm-3ztzzl.summary: A signature Una Una site known for strange hard-coral formations, starting over a shallow meadow of lettuce corals and reaching about 20 m. Blacktip reef sharks and stingrays patrol it, and any certified diver can do it.

odm-407ju8.name: Swiss Drop
highlights: Drop-off with an accessible passage near Cathedral

odm-41t0ek.name: Anemone City
highlights: Hundreds of anemones with clownfish

odm-432v0c.name: Green Outhouse
odm-432v0c.mooring: Mooring attached to coral in about 20 ft
highlights: Green morays, soapfish and turtles
One of the largest gorgonians in West End

odm-43fxxc.name: Gordon Rocks, Galapagos
highlights: Schools of hammerhead and Galapagos sharks
hazards: Strong currents and upwellings (the Washing Machine)
odm-43fxxc.summary: A sunken volcanic crater off Santa Cruz ringed by three exposed rocks, with a sandy floor near 30 m. Currents and upwellings are strong, so it is for experienced divers, and they pull in schools of hammerhead and other sharks.

odm-443stb.name: Steve’s Bommie - Ribbon No 3 Reef
highlights: Schooling fish, barracuda, whitetip reef sharks
Soft corals on the pinnacle
odm-443stb.summary: A pinnacle on Ribbon Reef 3 rising from around 30 m to just below the surface, with divers often starting near 25 m. Known for schooling fish, big predators and macro life.

odm-45ch04.name: RMS Rhone (Wreck)
odm-45ch04.summary: A Royal Mail steamer that broke in two off Salt Island in a hurricane; the stern lies in about 30-35 ft and the intact bow in 80-90 ft, with swim-throughs, making it a signature Caribbean wreck dive.

odm-45i94l.name: Cornelius Bay
highlights: Elkhorn coral on the plateau
Seahorses among gorgonians along the wall
odm-45i94l.summary: Short boat dive from Mambo Beach: a coral plateau with elkhorn coral that leads to a wall draped in gorgonians, where seahorses can be found.
sources: Bluewater Dive Travel (Scuba Lodge & Ocean Suites)

odm-48g2vj.name: Half Moon Caye Wall
highlights: Caribbean reef sharks, nurse sharks and rays
Tunnels of neon sponges and canyons
odm-48g2vj.summary: Drift dive along the celebrated wall of Half Moon Caye on Lighthouse Reef, known for vivid sponges, canyons and tunnels plus reef sharks, nurse sharks and rays.

odm-4cedqj.name: Northern Arch
highlights: Huge snapper and kingfish in the current
Stingray gatherings in summer
odm-4cedqj.summary: A short, narrow archway at the northern tip of the Poor Knights whose boulder floor drops to about 40 m and beyond. Current pours through and feeds sponge-covered walls, big schools of maomao, snapper, kingfish and seasonal stingrays.

odm-4dbphk.name: Wondergat
odm-4dbphk.access: Entry fee payable; steps down to the water; no permit needed
highlights: Collapsed dolomite sinkhole with side caverns
odm-4dbphk.summary: Flooded dolomite sinkhole about 75 by 100 m across, with near-vertical walls and caverns off the bottom, to roughly 58 m. It is a freshwater shore dive mostly used by advanced and technical divers.

odm-4ht14c.name: Million Dollar Point
highlights: Bulldozers, trucks and jeeps dumped after WWII
odm-4ht14c.summary: A slope off Luganville where the US military pushed surplus vehicles and machinery into the sea after WWII. Easy from the beach in calm weather; wreckage runs from the shallows to about 35-40 m.

odm-4igq4v.name: suana
highlights: Turtles and blue-water eagle and manta rays

odm-4kkcym.name: Blairgowrie Pier
highlights: Macro life and nudibranchs under the pier
Spider crab aggregations
hazards: Active boat pier with no-go zones
odm-4kkcym.summary: A very shallow pier dive from a purpose-built platform, rich in macro life under the pylons. It can be dived day or night, and spider crabs gather at times. Stay out of the boat no-go zones.

odm-4ndkfq.name: Calf Rock
highlights: Ledges and crevices with green moray and lobster
odm-4ndkfq.summary: A rock formation off St. Thomas's southeast coast, paired with neighbouring Cow Rock. Undercut ledges and crevices hold morays and lobsters; shallow enough for all divers.

odm-4qxxfk.name: Karang Sari
odm-4qxxfk.depthNote: Reef plateau at 10-12 m, deeper wall below
highlights: Large bommies on plateau; sea fans and overhangs on wall

odm-4r1mjd.name: Chicken reef
highlights: Pipefish, pygmy seahorses, nudibranchs
Strong current brings fish action
odm-4r1mjd.summary: Large Dampier Strait reef that splits into four separate dives. Dense coral and rich fish life, with macro such as pygmy seahorses on the quieter parts; current is often strong and brings extra action.

odm-4tco6y.name: Roe Reef
highlights: Swim-throughs and a limestone arch
odm-4tco6y.summary: An easy Rottnest Island reef of small caves around 14 m with tight swim-throughs and a large limestone arch, good for all levels when swell is low.

odm-520ng2.name: Le Remorqueur
odm-520ng2.summary: Tugboat wreck about 18 m long off the Tintamarre islet near Saint-Martin, sitting around 15 m and a little deeper depending on the mooring used that day. A boat dive with a step up in difficulty from the easy reef sites.

odm-52krua.name: Westsider Wreck, Carriacou
highlights: Coral-encrusted tugboat with lobsters and large fish
odm-52krua.summary: A roughly 30 m tugboat intentionally sunk in 2004 off Mabouya Island, lying in about 28 m. It is heavily coral-encrusted and good for photography, but the depth makes it an advanced dive.

odm-54bnjj.name: Scotts Head Drop Off
highlights: Colourful vase and tube sponges; lobster, cleaner shrimp
odm-54bnjj.summary: A sponge-covered wall at Scotts Head Point on the sheltered Soufrière bay side, worth diving anywhere between about 40 and 100 ft. Nooks hide lobsters and cleaner shrimp.

odm-560ets.name: Light House
highlights: Granite topography south of Mahé

odm-569wrp.name: Pemuteran Bio Rock Project
highlights: Critters and small fish; good night dive

odm-57q7xw.name: Sec Jaune
highlights: Eagle rays and turtles; arches and coral heads
odm-57q7xw.summary: A yellow-coral rock off Saint-Leu, behind the Pointe au Sel, with caves, arches and coral heads on a shallow-to-moderate profile. Open to all levels, and eagle rays and turtles are often seen.

odm-57r9m5.name: Secret Garden
highlights: Coral gardens with small reef fish

odm-58559r.name: Mabouya Whirlpool, Carriacou
highlights: Reef, small wreck and volcanic bubbles

odm-587ocx.name: Tikila Beach
highlights: Less crowded than other shore sites

odm-5d1jby.name: The Passage
highlights: Narrow canyon, good macro
hazards: Current can be strong

odm-5hw6pn.name: Merimbula Wharf
highlights: Blue gropers that follow divers
hazards: Tricky rock entry; avoid in southerly swell

odm-5idpdj.name: Sea Venture
highlights: Two large propellers, lobsters, tuna and sharks

odm-5j289m.name: Bio Rocks
highlights: Pipefish, juvenile frogfish, flatworms
Corals growing on bio rock frames
odm-5j289m.summary: A shallow artificial reef of submerged metal frames off east Gili Trawangan, now encrusted with coral. It is a relaxed macro dive with pipefish, juvenile frogfish and flatworms, reaching about 25 m at most.

odm-5l3hwm.name: Aquarium - Grand Cayman
highlights: Coral fingers, garden eels and stingrays in the sand
Dense fish life; sea turtles
odm-5l3hwm.summary: A shallow reef next to the Kittiwake off Seven Mile Beach, with coral fingers, sand patches holding garden eels and stingrays, and thick schools of tropical fish. Easy depths make it a good choice for beginners.

odm-5mci32.name: Mabouya Garden, Carriacou
highlights: Schools of fish, lobsters, turtles, eels, rays and sharks

odm-5mq2cn.name: Pos 1
highlights: Live coral top over coral-covered limestone pinnacles
odm-5mq2cn.summary: A popular first dive at Menjangan Island with a sandy bottom and gentle coral slope. Live coral covers the top and limestone pinnacles lie below; current is minimal and beginners are comfortable here.

odm-5nnrvv.name: Country Garden (14)
highlights: Massive coral boulders to swim between
Limestone formations

odm-5nxka7.name: Cartanza Wreck
highlights: Wreck in three pieces with engines intact

odm-5o09r4.name: Seraya Tulamben
highlights: Harlequin shrimp, frogfish, ghost pipefish
odm-5o09r4.summary: A world-famous black-sand macro slope on the Tulamben coast, with artificial structures in the shallows and sponge and coral further down. Calm to mild current; frogfish, harlequin shrimp and ghost pipefish.

odm-5pfpmp.name: Golden Passage Komodo
highlights: Coral garden along the drift
Turtles and reef sharks
odm-5pfpmp.summary: A narrow channel north of Komodo island dived as a drift from a shallow eastern bay, best on a rising tide. It offers a coral garden, a sandy bottom with garden eels and regular turtles and reef sharks.

odm-5ptebc.name: Black Magic Mountain
highlights: Schools of big-eye jacks, barracuda and fusiliers
Black coral bushes cover the pinnacle
odm-5ptebc.summary: A tall Bligh Water pinnacle dived by experienced divers. It is better known for its crowds of schooling fish than for coral, with sharks and eagle rays often passing.

odm-5r5sae.name: Ricketts Point
highlights: Rays, southern hulafish, zebra fish, morwongs
odm-5r5sae.summary: A shallow marine sanctuary in Port Phillip Bay, mostly under 5 m, suited to snorkelling and scuba with rockpools close to shore and about fifty fish species recorded.

odm-5sp3br.name: Gamat Bay
highlights: Mola mola in season
Soft corals, gorgonians, table coral in the bay
odm-5sp3br.summary: Small, sheltered bay on Penida's west coast with sandy bottom and rich soft coral shallows, opening onto a steep slope with bommies and stronger water. One of the better places to look for sunfish in season.

odm-5vpg6z.name: Rappel (11)
highlights: Steep wall
Underwater cave
Excellent for photography

odm-5wzmsz.name: Flying Fish Cove (Jetty dive)
hazards: Sharp coral and stonefish
odm-5wzmsz.summary: A shore dive from the boat ramp in Flying Fish Cove on Christmas Island, descending a reef slope to a drop-off. It is an easy dive with rich fish and coral variety; wear reef shoes for the sharp coral and stonefish.

odm-60n9za.name: La Cheminée
highlights: Chimney-shaped rock rising from the seabed
hazards: Occasional currents; low tide advised

odm-60swpn.name: Sardine Reef
highlights: Sharks and pygmy seahorses in the fans

odm-61xhk9.name: Old Wharf
odm-61xhk9.access: Entry via the disused old boat ramp behind Fyffe House
hazards: Boats launch from the beach - take care

odm-656fp5.name: Cathedral II
highlights: Black coral formation hanging from the ceiling
hazards: Sometimes strong surge in the overhead area
odm-656fp5.summary: The second of Lanai's lava-tube cathedrals, a large chamber with a black coral formation hanging from its roof. It is an overhead environment with occasional surge, so a guided dive is advised.

odm-6bbhpg.name: Le tombant de colombier
highlights: Abundant barracudas
odm-6bbhpg.summary: Wall dive off Pointe du Colombier on the northwest tip of St Barts, dropping to about 25 m, with a light current at times and plenty of barracudas.

odm-6bs41l.name: Angel City (44)
highlights: Double reef system with sand channel

odm-6ejd9q.name: Mike’s Point
highlights: Colourful hard coral plateaus
hazards: Powerful currents; dive at slack with a guide
odm-6ejd9q.summary: A pinnacle between Gam and Mansuar in the middle of the Dampier Strait, with a south wall past 40 m and a shallow coral plateau. It is current-swept and best on slack tide with an experienced guide.

odm-6jq9c1.name: Lee Breakwater
highlights: Seahorses, nudibranchs, john dory, kingfish
hazards: Busy commercial harbour - keep clear of ships

odm-6ndnc7.name: Cai (63)
highlights: Large tarpon schools
Giant anemones

odm-6oimyk.name: Tarpon Channel
highlights: Hammerhead sharks, eagle rays, tunnels and caves

odm-6ra4qp.name: C-50 Rivapalacios (Wreck)
highlights: Upright wartime navy ship sunk in 2000
Corals and sponges; longnose batfish
odm-6ra4qp.summary: A decommissioned wartime navy vessel scuttled in 2000 as an artificial reef off Isla Verde in the Veracruz reef park. It sits upright on its keel at about 27 m, now covered in coral and sponge, and is recommended for advanced divers.

odm-6ugu35.name: Mawan Komodo
highlights: Manta rays plus macro life

odm-6w01fn.name: P-47 Plane Wreck
highlights: Intact WWII P-47 fighter, upside down
About 15 m long, soft corals and fish
odm-6w01fn.summary: An American WWII P-47 fighter near Wai Island, lying upside down on a sloping reef at roughly 28 m with fuselage and wings intact. A second intact plane lies deeper, and a third is broken up in shallows.

odm-6w05b4.name: Willemstoren Lighthouse
hazards: Strong and unpredictable, caution required current

odm-6y7m68.name: Adelaide (Wreck)
odm-6y7m68.reason: NSW Crown Lands closed the ex-HMAS Adelaide dive site in July 2024 for public safety; public told not to dive it

odm-6zgdzb.name: Crystal Bay, Nusa Penida
highlights: Mola mola (ocean sunfish) in the cooler months
hazards: Currents can be very strong
odm-6zgdzb.summary: A sheltered bay off Nusa Penida with some of Bali's clearest water, divable in the bay or around the small island offshore. Ocean sunfish visit in the cooler months, but currents outside the bay demand experience.

odm-6zoqbj.name: Pyramid Rock
highlights: Small tunnels, caves and overhangs
Plenty of fish among granite boulders

odm-73y97h.name: Lost Anchor
highlights: Lush wall of gorgonians and sea fans
Very long anchor chain overgrown with coral and sponges
odm-73y97h.summary: Colorful wall covered in gorgonians and sea fans, best dived by boat. It is named for an anchor chain at least 90 m long that is now overgrown with coral and sponges.
sources: Bluewater Dive Travel (Scuba Lodge & Ocean Suites)

odm-74t4ss.name: Turtle Heaven
highlights: Turtles swimming and feeding near the surface

odm-78265n.name: Snapper Hole
odm-78265n.mooring: Mooring buoy; mooring pin at 33 ft
highlights: Cavern with tarpon and jacks hunting herring (summer)
Swim-throughs, tunnels and arches
1872 Spanish-style anchor

odm-7ckxbl.name: Cuevitas - Dominican Republic
highlights: Tunnel reef with swim-throughs

odm-7dhkfz.name: Boca Sami
highlights: Sea turtles, eagle rays and mini squids

odm-7gkt3m.name: Manta Sandy
highlights: Manta cleaning station
Turtles, blacktip sharks, Pegasus sea moth
odm-7gkt3m.summary: A shallow sandy-bottomed manta cleaning station near Mioskon in Raja Ampat. Black, reef and oceanic mantas queue up to be cleaned, most reliably October to April, in mild current.

odm-7k7vzx.name: Kevs Ledge
highlights: Hawksbill turtle under the overhang
Nudibranchs along the wall; cleaning station
odm-7k7vzx.summary: A ridge and wall dive in the Ponta area with a big overhang where hawksbill turtles nap. Divers drift across several levels at about 24 m, so drift experience and advanced certification are expected.

odm-7kcrku.name: Japanese Shipwreck (Wreck)
odm-7kcrku.depthNote: Wreck rests at about 5 m; reef slope continues deeper
highlights: Macro life: pygmy seahorses, nudibranchs, ghost pipefish
odm-7kcrku.summary: A small wreck lying in only about 5 m of water on the Amed coast, with a reef slope falling beyond it. Mild current and good macro life, including pygmy seahorses and ghost pipefish.

odm-7mrj9i.name: Playa Kalki / Alice in Wonderland
highlights: Fan, leaf, star and brain corals
Big corals along a wall
odm-7mrj9i.summary: Westpunt shore dive from the beach: a sandy start, first drop-off at about 8 m, then a coral wall sloping beyond 30 m. Fan, leaf, star and brain corals are the main draw.

odm-7pr9ci.name: A World Adrift Underwater Sculpture Park
highlights: Underwater sculpture park by Jason deCaires Taylor

odm-7pzjw9.name: Neptune’s Rhapsody
highlights: Coral bommies with swim-throughs
Whitetip reef sharks, anthias, nudibranchs
odm-7pzjw9.summary: A cluster of soft-coral-topped bommies near Rakiraki with swim-throughs along their bases. Anthias swarm over the tops and whitetip reef sharks and nudibranchs turn up around the formations.

odm-7qsc43.name: Jemeluk Bay
highlights: Macro critters and mid-size marine life

odm-7qzoh0.name: Gili Mimpang, Candidasa
highlights: Whitetip, wobbegong and coral cat sharks
Mola mola August to October
hazards: Strong currents and depth
odm-7qzoh0.summary: A trio of rocks off Candidasa known for sharks below about 25 m and clear water. Currents can be strong even for advanced divers; sunfish appear from August to October.

odm-7sg6wb.name: Doc Poulson (Wreck)
highlights: Former cable-laying ship covered in coral
Young fish on the wreck

odm-7tmcao.name: Gindang
highlights: Macro: wonderpus, ribbon eels, seahorses

odm-7v5tjk.name: The Maze
odm-7v5tjk.mooring: Mooring buoy; mooring pin at 49 ft
highlights: Canyons and buttresses to navigate
Sharks and teeming fish on the wall top

odm-7vxlgx.name: Dolphins Den
highlights: Coral canyons, tunnels and swim-throughs
Much quieter than Mary's Place
odm-7vxlgx.summary: A north-shore site with coral canyons, tunnels and swim-throughs reminiscent of Mary's Place but visited by far fewer boats. Soft and hard corals, snapping shrimp and slipper lobsters fill the nooks.

odm-7xo2eu.name: Sunset House Reef
highlights: Submerged bronze mermaid statue (Amphitrite)
Macro life; good for night dives
Coral, sponges and sea whips
odm-7xo2eu.summary: A shore-entry house reef at Sunset House in George Town, popular for macro photography and night dives. Expect healthy coral, sponge and sea-whip growth, a nine-foot bronze mermaid statue underwater and a small landing-craft wreck nearby.

odm-807lyv.name: Outside Edge, Aliwal Shoal
highlights: Pelagic gamefish, rays and sharks
Hard and soft coral wall with turtles

odm-8094ev.name: Cagarras
highlights: Octopus, lobsters and small reef sharks

odm-84xhpw.name: Eden Park
highlights: Blacktip sharks, rare lemon shark, turtles
odm-84xhpw.summary: A relaxed reef dive just beyond the lagoon off Moorea's north coast, next to the Canyons. Healthy coral and anemones attract turtles, barracuda and blacktip sharks, with the odd shy lemon shark. Suitable for most certified divers.

odm-886kmr.name: Labyrinth
highlights: Rock pillars forming tunnels and passages
hazards: Swell and surge

odm-89ojqs.name: Deep Turbo
highlights: Sea mounds with overhangs on a sandy floor
Spotted eagle rays and reef sharks
hazards: Strong currents; depth to ~30 m
odm-89ojqs.summary: Advanced dive off Gili Trawangan's east side: large sea mounds rise from a sandy floor near 30 m, with overhangs and outcrops. Current draws pelagics such as eagle rays and reef sharks, but it needs depth and drift experience.

odm-8ak1je.name: Menjangan - Eel Garden
highlights: Colony of garden eels on a sandy channel
Wall with schooling fish in the passing current
odm-8ak1je.summary: At the western end of Menjangan, a reef wall drops from a shallow top to well beyond recreational depth, ending in a sandy channel with a colony of garden eels. Current can be moderate to strong.

odm-8c46oc.name: The Caves - Acapulco
highlights: Swim-through tunnels and caves
Eagle rays, stonefish, octopuses, moray eels
hazards: Strong current; best dived early in the morning

odm-8clalj.name: Salt Pier (49)
odm-8clalj.access: Dive only when no ship is at the pier
highlights: Pilings overgrown with marine life
Turtles and seahorses
hazards: Limited to strong current
odm-8clalj.summary: Shore dive under the old salt-loading pier south of Kralendijk. The pilings are encrusted with sponges and coral and shelter turtles and fish schools. Dive it only while no ship is moored; the light shafts suit photographers.

odm-8f764l.name: Albatros, wreck
odm-8f764l.summary: A 27-30 m fishing vessel sunk on purpose in Golfo Nuevo off Puerto Madryn to make a dive site. It rests at roughly 15-24 m, is rated medium difficulty, and is covered in life such as tube anemones and large salmon fish.

odm-8fl24x.name: Playa Funchi (3)
highlights: Washington Plantation remains underwater

odm-8jfcj0.name: Mangel Halto Reef
odm-8jfcj0.summary: A south-coast Aruba shore dive where you can walk out to the reef edge, with an inner reef near 55 feet and an outer reef dropping to around 90 feet or deeper.

odm-8l7hob.name: Alibaba
highlights: Canyon where fish shelter from the current

odm-8lm7ec.name: USS Kittiwake (Wreck)
odm-8lm7ec.access: Wreck certification not required; follow an instructor if not wreck-certified
highlights: Five decks to explore; ex US Navy rescue ship
Open, diver-friendly layout
odm-8lm7ec.summary: A 251 ft former US Navy submarine rescue ship sunk as an artificial reef off Seven Mile Beach in 2011. It lies in roughly 15 to 65 ft of water and was prepared for diving, so it suits recreational divers without wreck training.

odm-8ojgwn.name: Menjangan - Bat Cave
highlights: Reef sharks and trevallies
Crevices and caves at 9-12 m
odm-8ojgwn.summary: A wall on Menjangan with crevices and caves around 9-12 m, named for bats in the surface cave. Currents are strong at times, bringing trevallies and reef sharks.

odm-8pob9n.name: El Chato
highlights: Shoals of fish around large rocks
hazards: Powerful, unpredictable currents

odm-8qupvm.name: Wonder Reef On The Gold Coast
highlights: Nine buoyant spiral reefs floating above the seabed
odm-8qupvm.summary: An artificial dive site off The Spit made of nine large spiral structures that float on chains above the seabed. They start around 8 m and the seabed lies at roughly 25-30 m, so there is something for most levels.

odm-8r7gjo.name: Shark Reef - Grenada
highlights: Nurse sharks, turtles, stingrays
Brain and pillar coral formations
hazards: Strong, sweeping Atlantic-side currents
odm-8r7gjo.summary: An Atlantic-facing reef south of Glover's Island known for nurse sharks, turtles and rays among rugged coral formations. Strong sweeping currents restrict it to experienced divers, often as a drift.

odm-8sck8d.name: Split Rock
odm-8sck8d.mooring: Mooring buoy; mooring pin at 58 ft
highlights: Narrow canyon splitting the reef
Black coral ledges; swim-throughs in wall

odm-8svmu9.name: Playa Largu
odm-8svmu9.access: Entry fee paid at the San Juan country house; no amenities
highlights: Healthy coral reefs
Occasional seahorses
odm-8svmu9.summary: Quiet shore dive at a secluded west-coast beach in the San Juan area. Entry fee at the country house, no facilities, but healthy coral reefs with plenty of fish and the odd seahorse.

odm-8tt5sf.name: Hole in the Wall
highlights: Giant cuttlefish, boxfish, moray eels, wobbegongs
Blue-kneed sea spider (unique to South Coast)
odm-8tt5sf.summary: A hole in the reef on the southern side of Bass Point reserve with plenty of fish, cuttlefish, eels and wobbegongs, and a spider crab species found only on the NSW south coast.

odm-8twofe.name: Jetty, Tanah Ampo
highlights: Pier pillars covered in sea fans
Critters living in dumped debris

odm-8y8n4w.name: Biorocks
highlights: Biorock artificial reefs with dense shallow coral
odm-8y8n4w.summary: Gentle slope off Gili Trawangan's east coast where electrified biorock frames have grown into a reef reaching about 18 m, richest in the shallows. Easy for all levels and good for small marine life.

odm-8yhnxr.name: Mexico Rocks
highlights: Boulder coral heads in shallow water
Good light for underwater photography
odm-8yhnxr.summary: Shallow patch-reef complex off the northern tip of Ambergris Caye, a marine protected area of about 100 boulder-coral clusters in only a few metres of water. Good visibility and light make it popular for photography and snorkeling.

odm-90bmai.name: Tugboat Boris (Wreck)
highlights: Encrusted coral and large fish; good night dive

odm-9275ov.name: Jeff Davis Memorial (18)
highlights: Active cleaning stations between 8-28 meters

odm-9364mm.name: South Sands
highlights: Groups of rays, sand sharks and guitar sharks
Boxfish, pufferfish and leather coral on the reef
odm-9364mm.summary: Another sandy clearing on Aliwal Shoal with patches of reef around it, about 17-18 m deep. Rays, sand sharks and guitar sharks are the draw, with boxfish, crayfish and leather coral on the rock edges.

odm-95g47k.name: Ceningan wall, Nusa Lembongan, Bali, Indonesia
highlights: Soft corals, sponges and nudibranchs on the wall
Mola mola in season
hazards: Strong, sometimes downward, unpredictable currents
Exit often in open blue water; SMB needed
odm-95g47k.summary: A near-vertical wall in the channel by Nusa Ceningan, covered in soft corals and sponges. Strong, sometimes downward currents make it a site for experienced divers with good buoyancy and SMB skills.

odm-96vkf8.name: Three Sisters Komodo
highlights: Three submerged pinnacles with pristine coral
Reef sharks, mobula rays, trevally schools
hazards: Frequent current between pinnacles
odm-96vkf8.summary: Three coral-covered pinnacles in southern Komodo, with tops a few metres below the surface and faces dropping to about 25-30 m. Current is common and makes moving between them hard, so it suits experienced divers.

odm-97tgks.name: Kodiak Queen (Wreck)
highlights: Wire Kraken sculpture on a former Pearl Harbor survivor
odm-97tgks.summary: The former Navy fuel barge Kodiak Queen was sunk in 2017 off Virgin Gorda as an art reef topped by a wire Kraken sculpture. It rests in about 55-57 ft, with open-water divers exploring the outside and penetration left to advanced divers.

odm-99c94w.name: Le Tombant Saint Étienne
highlights: Turtles and paddle perch along the wall
odm-99c94w.summary: A steep reef wall just beyond the barrier reef on Tahiti's west coast, close to the Ta'apuna pass. Turtles and schools of reef fish cruise the upper wall, and gentle current often allows a drift. Better with some experience; wind can make it hard to dive.

odm-99zpxm.name: Director's Bay
highlights: Old shark fence covered in coral and sponges
Yellow pencil coral and giant anemones at the drop-off
odm-99zpxm.summary: Former Shell directors' beach on Curaçao's south coast. A narrow sandy shelf ends at a drop-off about 6 m down, then the reef falls steeply to roughly 40-45 m. The sponge- and coral-covered old shark fence is the landmark.
sources: Bluewater Dive Travel (Scuba Lodge & Ocean Suites)

odm-9ajsvb.name: Cistern Point
highlights: Eels, nurse sharks and tarpon in cistern-like holes

odm-9ccgxl.name: Colombia Shallows
highlights: Seahorses on sea fans

odm-9ci018.name: Paradise Reef - Cozumel
highlights: Octopus and lobster on night dives
Turtles and reef fish
odm-9ci018.summary: A shallow, calm reef just south of Cozumel town that is popular for first dives and as the island's favourite night-dive site. Visibility is good and the current gentle.

odm-9d4r5m.name: Canyons - Moorea (Tahiti)
highlights: Blacktip sharks, green turtles, anemones
hazards: Occasional strong currents
odm-9d4r5m.summary: A reef dive on Moorea's north side near Opunohu Bay, where coral canyons shelter small fish and blacktip sharks cruise past. Mostly calm and open to all levels, but currents can pick up and catch newer divers out.

odm-9ec3vn.name: Golden Rock
highlights: Whip coral slope and large coral fans
odm-9ec3vn.summary: Pinnacle off Amed, east Bali, dived as a drift along a descending slope. Expect 5 to 30+ m, a current that swings from medium to strong, and fan and whip corals; guides take experienced divers only.

odm-9edvy7.name: Napoleon Reef
highlights: Gorgonian-covered pinnacle and shallow corals
Rays and cuttlefish on the deep end

odm-9fd2g8.name: El Natural
hazards: Unmarked entry; go with a local guide

odm-9km2d5.name: Flat Rock - Nursery
highlights: Juvenile fish, coral and macro life
Occasional hammerhead passing through
odm-9km2d5.summary: The shallowest of the Flat Rock dives, on its south-west corner, with coral gardens, juvenile fish and macro life rather than big pelagics. A little current is normal but easy to use, so it works well for beginners.

odm-9lrpt2.name: Joanne’s Sunchi (J)
highlights: Terraced reef wall
Suitable for night diving

odm-9qctkq.name: Odyssey (Wreck)
odm-9qctkq.penetration: Swim-through opportunities; going inside needs Wreck Specialty
odm-9qctkq.summary: A large freighter, about 300 ft long and sunk deliberately in 2002, resting on sand at roughly 100-110 ft in Sandy Bay beside the reef wall. It is an advanced-level wreck dive with swim-through chances.

odm-9rvcv3.name: Mikes Cupboard
highlights: Moray eels, octopus, nudibranchs
Flutefish, crocodilefish, leaf fish
odm-9rvcv3.summary: A shallow, low-profile reef with three large bowls near Tofo, good for beginners and photographers. Morays, rays, batfish and macro life hide in its caves and gullies.

odm-9tk1eh.name: Mahavelona
highlights: Wreck with a thriving reef; morays, octopus

odm-9tlgbr.name: Swansea Bridge
hazards: Strong tidal flow; dive only on still water

odm-9uiyc9.name: Rotui
highlights: Juvenile and adult reef fish, turtles, blacktip sharks

odm-9ul3tk.name: Plantation Pinnacle
highlights: Clownfish and anemone garden on top
Swim-through at the base
odm-9ul3tk.summary: A trio of pinnacles in the Mamanucas topped with an anemone garden full of clownfish, with swim-throughs at depth. Beginners can stay on the shallow top while experienced divers go deeper.

odm-9vyf4g.name: Rasgefanno
highlights: Pelagic thresher sharks; seasonal oceanic mantas

odm-9wqk11.name: Turtle Alley
highlights: Barrel and rope sponges, gorgonians on mid-reef

odm-9zpkd4.name: Coral Gardens
highlights: Hard and soft coral cover
Many nudibranchs

odm-a2779p.name: El Jardin
highlights: Eagle rays, turtles, moray eels, butterfly fish
Hard and soft corals on gentle slope

odm-a333el.name: Sidem
highlights: Frogfish, nudibranchs, seahorses

odm-a38ofd.name: The Gardens
highlights: Juvenile fish, snapper, angelfish, eagle rays

odm-a3dhdw.name: Batu Rufas
highlights: Sheltered lagoon and swim-through lined with sea fans
Giant sponge barrels on steep walls
Napoleon wrasse, bumphead parrotfish, pygmy seahorses

odm-a3hbbh.name: Blackish Point
highlights: Crevices, overhangs and caves along the wall
Large midnight parrotfish

odm-a494ab.name: Close Encounters
highlights: Gentle slopes with coral bommies and schooling fish
Baby sharks under table corals; nooks and sponges on the east side
odm-a494ab.summary: A flat-topped reef off Pemuteran with gentle slopes and scattered coral bommies. Calm, camera-friendly conditions suit any level; turtles, trevally, cuttlefish and baby sharks under table corals.

odm-a5zfrg.name: Bat Island: Big Scare, Gran Susto
highlights: Bull sharks
hazards: Strong currents and rough conditions; no anchor line
odm-a5zfrg.summary: A deep, current-prone dive at the outermost Bat Island, famous as Costa Rica's bull shark site. Descents are fast in rough water without an anchor line, so operators usually restrict it to advanced divers.

odm-a71c3t.name: Flamingo Bay
highlights: Whip corals, sponges, sea fans and seahorses

odm-a81yjh.name: Hunga
highlights: Excellent visibility, large coral bommies
odm-a81yjh.summary: A circular open-sea reef with big coral bommies off northwest Zanzibar, known for clear water. Aimed at certified divers rather than first-timers.

odm-a991zo.name: Sorido Wall
highlights: Sharks and fish schools; overhangs and caves

odm-aan42n.name: Shag Rock
highlights: Hiding places for fish and crayfish
hazards: Rock is awash and covered at high tide

odm-afpeme.name: Breath Taker
odm-afpeme.depthNote: Three coral heads at 25-30 m on a drop-off to about 100 m
highlights: Blacktip, grey reef and whaler sharks
Barracuda and swim-throughs on the wall
odm-afpeme.summary: A deep Bligh Water reef of three coral heads on the edge of a very deep drop-off, famous for shark encounters. Sharks, barracuda and big schooling fish gather around the point.

odm-agt8bu.name: Turtle Pinnacle
highlights: Green turtle cleaning station
odm-agt8bu.summary: A lava pinnacle rising from the seafloor off the Big Island's west coast, north of Kona. Mild current and moderate depths make it an easy dive where turtles gather to be cleaned.

odm-aguq5p.name: Flat Rock - Blue Corner
odm-aguq5p.depthNote: Reef top about 28 m, dropping to 40-45 m on sand
highlights: Large bull sharks and varied reef life
hazards: Prone to current; free ascent skills needed

odm-agvj1d.name: Barcadera Reef
highlights: Brain corals and huge sea fans in the shallows
Variety of coral species
odm-agvj1d.summary: Hard coral reef near the airport that thins at the entrance and gets denser and richer with depth, running from about 6 m to 25-28 m. Brain corals and big sea fans stand out.

odm-ai4341.name: Turtle Heaven Gili
highlights: Turtles swimming and feeding near the surface

odm-alhrfc.name: Nudi Rock Raja Ampat
highlights: Barracuda, giant trevally, grey reef sharks
Pygmy seahorses
odm-alhrfc.summary: A Misool rock with walls, slopes and small pinnacles dropping to about 28 m. Currents run moderate to strong, so a reef hook helps; barracuda, trevally and grey reef sharks patrol and the finish is a shallow soft coral garden.

odm-apiri3.name: Anchor Wreck
odm-apiri3.depthNote: Anchor at ~6 m on the wall; main wreck about 35-50 m
highlights: Large coral-encrusted anchor in the shallows
Wall continuing past 30 m
odm-apiri3.summary: A Menjangan wall dive named for a big rusty anchor resting at about 6 m. The wall drops well past 30 m, and the actual wreck lies deep at roughly 35-50 m, so most guides stay on the reef.

odm-arvs3h.name: Sharkies Hideaway Part 1
highlights: Wall with overhangs, caves and canyons; sharks and eels

odm-avli1i.name: Hole in the Wall
highlights: Steep, narrow reef wall with lots of life
hazards: Current carries divers along the wall to Mangel Halto
odm-avli1i.summary: Shore-accessible drift along a steep, narrow reef wall at Mangel Halto, with the current carrying divers to a sandy channel and a shady beach. Rated suitable for beginners; the reef drops to about 30 m.

odm-axlrus.name: Marie Pampoen
highlights: Porcupinefish, tarpon and moray eels around the car pile

odm-ayijk6.name: Faro
highlights: Big-eye jacks, snappers; mantas and whale sharks
hazards: Frequent currents; good fitness needed

odm-b196uu.name: Bloody Bay Wall
odm-b196uu.depthNote: Wall top about 20 ft; drops thousands of feet
highlights: Sheer wall with sponges, tubes and gorgonian fans
Large fish, rays and sharks
Turtles and Nassau groupers
odm-b196uu.summary: A sheer wall along Little Cayman's north shore that starts at about 20 ft and falls thousands of feet. Coral, sponges and fans cover the face, and turtles, groupers, rays and sharks cruise past in very clear water.
sources: Cayman Islands Department of Tourism (Explore Cayman)

odm-b3cq98.name: La Grotte aux Couleurs
highlights: Collapsed cave plateau with green and hawksbill turtles

odm-b4trti.name: Manta Ray Heaven, Garden Eel Cove
highlights: Night manta ray feeding under dive lights
Garden eels on the sandy bottom
hazards: Exposed to open ocean; boat ride can be choppy
odm-b4trti.summary: A coral shelf in Makako Bay off Kona airport that is a day site for garden eels and, at night, the Big Island's manta ray dive. Operators run boat trips; divers kneel on sand at about 35 feet while mantas feed on plankton.

odm-b5uqxq.name: Museum of Underwater Art, Coral Greenhouse
highlights: 12 m-high, 58-tonne sculpture structure

odm-b76zgw.name: Ave Maria
highlights: Reef sharks, stingrays, batfish
odm-b76zgw.summary: A rocky islet between Praslin and the Sister Islands with granite arches and deeper boulders, reaching about 20 m. Reef sharks, rays and lobsters are regular, and visibility is among the best on the inner islands.

odm-b8irph.name: Atlantic Princess (Wreck)
hazards: Penetration unsafe after storm damage

odm-b8r5n8.name: Oro Verde (Wreck)
highlights: 184 ft steel cargo ship, broken up against the reef
Groupers, barracuda, eagle rays, jacks
odm-b8r5n8.summary: A 184 ft steel freighter sunk in 1980 in about 50 ft of water just off Seven Mile Beach. Now broken up against the reef, it is a shallow wreck with jacks, groupers and eels, often dived together with neighbouring Paradise Reef.

odm-ba4s7o.name: Sponge Reef
highlights: Many colorful sponges: elephant ear, tube and vase
Turtles often seen
odm-ba4s7o.summary: Sloping reef off Druif Beach crowded with colorful sponges, with turtles often passing. Depths run from the shallows down to about 25-28 m; rated beginner-friendly.

odm-baa2eo.name: The Awakening Bull Shark Dive
highlights: Bull sharks fed behind a low reef wall

odm-bcp74p.name: Diamond Cay
highlights: Diverse corals; critters in sand and shallows

odm-bf8jja.name: 7 Miles Reef
highlights: Black-tipped reef sharks and pelagic schools
Ragged-tooth sharks at Mushroom Rocks
odm-bf8jja.summary: Sodwana's best-regarded advanced reef, with a drop-off from about 15 m at the summit to 24 m. Its high ledge, Mushroom Rocks bommies, reef sharks, big morays and turtles make for varied multi-level dives.

odm-bg5rd3.name: Buraco das Cabras
highlights: Rock corridor opening into a crevice
Schools of small fish
odm-bg5rd3.summary: Volcanic rock formations that form a corridor leading into a wide crevice, usually dived as a drift that finishes in the Canal da Rata. Sponges, soft corals and small-fish schools line the walls.

odm-bh3uk7.name: Alamanda
highlights: Huge sponges and table corals
Turtles, morays, bumphead parrotfish
odm-bh3uk7.summary: A coral slope beside the Tulamben drop-off with large sponges and table corals, turtles, morays and bumphead parrotfish. Conditions are calm with little current, and it is dived from a boat.

odm-bjj9wl.name: Tour de Boucan
highlights: Canyons, arches and faults with barracuda and turtles

odm-bnizop.name: Cabeço da Sapata
highlights: Wall with passing fish

odm-bp5jzb.name: North-West Point
highlights: Frogfish, white morays, barracuda, rays and turtles
hazards: Dived depending on the current

odm-bptxts.name: Leon’s Wall
highlights: Soft corals and sponges, lionfish, snapper schools, leaf fish

odm-bq878v.name: Grand coude de Kele
highlights: Grey sharks, jacks, barracuda, groupers, eagle rays

odm-bqfj0q.name: Ransiwor
highlights: Sloping reef with big cleaning stations
odm-bqfj0q.summary: An easy sloping reef off Gam with calm conditions, reaching around 25 m. Several large cleaning stations draw plenty of fish, especially around rising tide.

odm-bqv60e.name: Malibu Point
highlights: Turtles, frogfish, ribbon eels in the creek
Schooling fusiliers and possible mola mola
hazards: Unpredictable currents, even in the creek
odm-bqv60e.summary: A sheltered bay on Nusa Penida's east side that opens to walls dropping into the blue. The bay suits easier dives, but the outer walls are exposed to very strong currents and are for experienced divers.

odm-br373g.name: Front Porche (31)
highlights: Tugboat wreck New York at 28 meters

odm-broe8z.name: Jackson Wall and Reef - Grand Cayman
highlights: Mini-walls with swim-throughs
Turtles, rays, reef sharks and barracuda
Large fish and occasional rays

odm-brsvor.name: Acuario
highlights: Many rays including eagle rays
Good coral cover and abundant fish

odm-btquek.name: Caleta de Chon
highlights: Macro life over boulders and small coral patches

odm-buzjsy.name: Puerto Naos - Playa Chica
odm-buzjsy.depthNote: Wall drops from 18 to 50 m; red gorgonians near 35 m
highlights: Near-vertical wall with red gorgonians at 35 m

odm-bve2c8.name: Hole In The Wall
highlights: Sand chute through the wall exiting at 100 ft
Eagle rays, turtles and shallow swim-throughs
hazards: Strong pull down at the hole; keep buoyancy
Dark silty cavern where divers can get lost
odm-bve2c8.summary: A Roatán classic: a sand chute from about 40 ft drops through a hole in the reef wall to around 100 ft, then the dive climbs the wall to shallow swim-throughs and caverns. Depth control matters; sport divers should stay above about 34 m.

odm-bvz6dt.name: Eagle Nest
highlights: Schooling jacks, trevallies and barracuda
Reef sharks and napoleon wrasse
Oceanic manta rays visit
odm-bvz6dt.summary: A pinnacle off the eastern end of Pulau Warakaraket in Misool, Raja Ampat, dived mainly from liveaboards. It is known for pelagic action: schooling jacks and trevally, reef sharks, napoleon wrasse and sometimes oceanic mantas over healthy reef.

odm-bwt28z.name: Margate Bay (55)
highlights: Black margates (namesake)
Eagle rays
Reef sharks

odm-byg3l9.name: Molokini Crater
odm-byg3l9.depthNote: Interior mostly 20-50 ft; outer wall drops past 300 ft
highlights: Whitetip, blacktip and gray reef sharks
Sheer outer wall plunging past 300 ft
odm-byg3l9.summary: A crescent-shaped volcanic islet off Maui. Most boat dives are shallow and sheltered inside the crater, while experienced divers drift along the steep outer back wall. Water clarity is usually excellent.

odm-bzqvk5.name: Seafan Valley
highlights: Valley of giant gorgonians
Kingfish, rays, tropical fish

odm-c051rt.name: Butterfly Bay “KEYHOLE“
hazards: Tidal currents toward centre of bay

odm-c0hocr.name: Catuan (Wreck)
odm-c0hocr.summary: Small tugboat of about 33 m sunk off Boca Chica in 2006 as an artificial reef, now encrusted with coral and resting around 20 m; suitable for a range of experience levels.

odm-c0ojlf.name: Cedral Wall
highlights: Sea fans, sponges, angelfish, jacks

odm-c1ur1a.name: Sweet Lips
highlights: Diverse fauna, good for photographers

odm-c2fj0s.name: test
odm-c2fj0s.reason: OpenDiveMap test artifact, not a named dive site
odm-c2fj0s.summary: Removed from the Atlas because the source record is explicitly a test entry and contains no evidence of a real dive site.

odm-c6dm2z.name: Vilingili Kandu
highlights: Large numbers of grey reef sharks in the channel
Silvertip sharks
odm-c6dm2z.summary: A channel (kandu) south of Villingili island in the Maldives, best on an incoming current when grey reef sharks patrol the mouth in numbers. The channel floor is at about 30 m and divers are generally expected to be advanced.

odm-c6eevg.name: Boss Reef
highlights: Hawksbill and green turtles, nurse sharks, stingrays
Big hole with barracuda at 14-18 m
odm-c6eevg.summary: A huge reef of rolling rock mounds, sandy valleys and plate coral running several miles off St George's. Depths of about 6-25 m suit all divers, with turtles, morays, nurse sharks and rays along its length.

odm-c6etup.name: Yulliet Kecil
highlights: Swim-throughs and overhangs with soft corals
Reef sharks and barracuda along the wall

odm-c6u8bx.name: Salon
highlights: Cleaner shrimp, rays, resident green turtles
odm-c6u8bx.summary: A small coral outcrop near Tofo beach, used for training, refreshers and night dives. Cleaner shrimp, several ray species, turtles, octopus and lots of macro life sit among its small caves.

odm-c75t0p.name: Busselton Jetty
highlights: Schools of yellowtail, herring and longfin pike
sources: WA Dept of Biodiversity, Conservation and Attractions

odm-ca71qn.name: Severence Wreck - Lady Elliot Island
highlights: Intact yacht with soft corals on the rigging

odm-ca8165.name: Twin Barges
highlights: Macro life and an adjacent reef

odm-caaifg.name: Alice in Wonderland, BVI
highlights: Healthy spur-and-groove reef off Ginger Island

odm-cadn7u.name: Devil’s Grotto North
highlights: Swim-throughs, caverns and chimneys in coral heads
Silverside schools, tarpon and barracuda
odm-cadn7u.summary: A shallow shore dive off George Town built around big coral heads riddled with swim-throughs, caverns and chimneys. It tops out within a few feet of the surface, reaches about 45 to 50 ft, and is popular with beginners and snorkellers.

odm-cb4gnm.name: Menjangan - Eel Garden Joly
highlights: Garden eel colony in sandy channel
Large schools of fish in the passing current
hazards: Moderate to strong, tide-shifting current
odm-cb4gnm.summary: A wall on Menjangan's western tip that drops to about 40 m into a sandy channel with garden eels. Passing current brings fish schools but makes it one of the trickier Menjangan dives, rated advanced.

odm-cbbkn1.name: Baung Penyu Bay / Turtle Neck / The Wall
highlights: Feather stars and seahorses

odm-cda7k5.name: Little Cayman
odm-cda7k5.reason: Whole island, not a single dive site

odm-ch533b.name: Marsa Shagra House Reef
odm-ch533b.access: Guests may dive the house reef any time without a guide
odm-ch533b.summary: A well-preserved house reef at Marsa Shagra village on Egypt's Red Sea coast. Coral starts in very shallow water and slopes gradually to outer walls at 40-50 m. Guests can dive it freely.

odm-chthpo.name: Wai Nilu
highlights: Ribbon eels, mandarin fish, frogfish, nudibranchs
hazards: Silt stirs up easily; needs good buoyancy
odm-chthpo.summary: A muck and macro site near Rinca Island, a sandy slope with little coral that is often called a mini Lembeh. Open-water friendly, but silt stirs easily so buoyancy matters.

odm-chxq1l.name: Lesleen M and Vicky B Wrecks
odm-chxq1l.depthNote: Lesleen M deck 30 ft, sand 65 ft; Vicky B about 80 ft
odm-chxq1l.penetration: Lesleen M interior possible for trained wreck divers
highlights: Coral-covered wreck with juvenile angelfish, hawksbill turtles
odm-chxq1l.summary: Two artificial-reef wrecks in Anse Cochon bay: the 165 ft freighter Lesleen M (sunk 1986) sits upright on sand with its deck near 30 ft and bottom near 65 ft, while the 200 ft Vicky B (sunk 2018) lies deeper, near 80 ft.

odm-cjyvf1.name: Good Heart
highlights: Healthy coral and biorock restoration structures
Frogfish, turtles and reef sharks
odm-cjyvf1.summary: The Gili Trawangan house-reef slope on the east side, dropping toward the Meno channel. Relaxed conditions, coral restoration structures, turtles, frogfish and reef sharks, with octopus on night dives.

odm-ckf6xs.name: Flat Rock - Shark Alley
highlights: Grey nurse sharks in two sand channels, June to October
Rays, turtles and wobbegongs
odm-ckf6xs.summary: The grey nurse shark hotspot on the eastern edge of Flat Rock, where sharks gather over two parallel sand channels in winter. It is rated an advanced dive because it starts deep and can carry current.
