odm-cksqf0.name: First Cathedral
highlights: Two-story lava tube cavern lit by skylights
odm-cksqf0.summary: A large lava-tube cavern off Lanai with an open ceiling that lets sunbeams flood the chamber. Multiple exits and good clarity make it approachable for certified divers of any level.

odm-clc1w7.name: Simons Town / Chimney
highlights: Rock chimneys with holes and gullies
Whale sharks sometimes seen
odm-clc1w7.summary: A shallow reef of large rock chimneys riddled with holes and gullies, suitable for beginners and long relaxed dives. Game fish shoal overhead and whale sharks are occasionally spotted.

odm-cm41u2.name: Fausse Passe de Paea
highlights: Leopard rays, turtles, whitetip sharks

odm-cni042.name: Temple Wall
highlights: Sponges, gorgonians and soft corals on the wall
Crustaceans and large gorgonians on the deep section
odm-cni042.summary: A boat dive in Pemuteran Bay: a wall beneath the underwater temple statues, dropping to around 35 m and covered in sponges, gorgonians and soft corals. Depth and occasional current make it one for experienced divers.

odm-co1h25.name: Passe de l’Ermitage
highlights: Chance of rays and turtles

odm-cpc2xy.name: Blue Bay the Wall
highlights: Fan corals and elkhorn coral
hazards: Easy to drift deeper than planned on the wall
odm-cpc2xy.summary: Wall dive reached straight from Blue Bay Beach: the drop-off starts around 3 m and plunges past 50 m. Fan and elkhorn corals make it popular, but clear water makes it easy to go deeper than planned.

odm-cpclvf.name: Purple Rain
highlights: Schools of purple creole wrasse
Barrel sponges, turtles and stingrays
odm-cpclvf.summary: A sloping south-west Grenada reef named for the clouds of purple creole wrasse that fill the water, with big barrel sponges, soft coral, turtles and rays. Best as a drift dive for divers with some experience.

odm-cq5mwh.name: Gili Gede Slope
highlights: Big bommies, soft and table corals

odm-cs4i1y.name: Three Sisters Cayman
odm-cs4i1y.mooring: Mooring buoy; mooring pin at 69 ft
highlights: Three towering pinnacles; the third leans
Narrow canyon leads to first pinnacle

odm-cuukqo.name: White Sand Beach, Carriacou
highlights: Corals and gorgonians with turtles and rays

odm-cvk89a.name: La Zélée, Tahiti
highlights: Coral-covered WWI gunboat wreck scuttled 1914

odm-cwd061.name: Cenote Maravillas
highlights: Light beam striking a sulfur cloud at 30 m
Small hells bells at the cavern edge

odm-cws0o1.name: Inside Edge - Aliwal Shoal
highlights: Wall with ledges, caves and overhangs
Ragged-tooth sharks, scorpionfish, false stonefish

odm-cz2cbv.name: Manta Alley
highlights: Manta rays at cleaning stations
hazards: Lots of current; boats need calm weather and right tide
odm-cz2cbv.summary: A channel at the southern end of Komodo where manta rays gather at cleaning stations. Divers can shelter from the flow on either side of the alley, but sea state and tide must suit the boats to get here.

odm-cz4pqt.name: Kicker Rock / Léon Dormido, San Cristobal, Galapagos
highlights: Hammerhead sharks, typically around 12-15 m

odm-d34nh7.name: Paradise Reef
highlights: Spur-and-groove reef covered in sponges
Dived with the nearby Oro Verde wreck
odm-d34nh7.summary: A shallow spur-and-groove reef off Seven Mile Beach, covered in sponges and busy with fish. Boats usually pair it with the neighbouring Oro Verde wreck for an easy, shallow dive.

odm-d3a5lc.name: Antons
highlights: Big shoals of snappers
Giant moray and turtles
odm-d3a5lc.summary: High-profile ridge at the southern tip of Two Mile Reef that fills with snapper schools, fed by nutrient-rich north-south currents. About 16 m deep and open to Open Water divers, with morays, turtles and frogfish among the rocks.

odm-d9gw7o.name: Paradise - Dominican Republic
highlights: Nurse sharks

odm-d9mqn4.name: Raggies Cave
highlights: Ragged-tooth sharks in winter
Gullies, overhangs and swim-throughs
hazards: Cave off limits while sharks are resting inside
odm-d9mqn4.summary: Cave, gully and overhang system on the seaward side of Aliwal Shoal, famed as the winter gathering spot of ragged-tooth sharks. Dives reach roughly 18 m and the rock is dotted with hard corals, juvenile fish and well-camouflaged scorpionfish.

odm-d9u2py.name: Fish Den
odm-d9u2py.mooring: On a coral mound in a horseshoe canyon
highlights: Hundreds of fish on the shallow mound
Turtles feeding on sponges
odm-d9u2py.summary: A shallow West End site where most of the action sits in the top 20 ft, around a coral mound and horseshoe canyon with a sponge-covered wall beyond. Good for photographers and long bottom times.

odm-dbci2j.name: El Corsario
highlights: Wreck of a luxury yacht lost in 1950
Rock formations and plenty of fish

odm-dckzea.name: Pengah Kecil
highlights: Coral gardens and schooling fish
Dense reef life
odm-dckzea.summary: A small three-pinnacle rock island in Komodo with walls, plateaus and sloping reef. Currents are manageable, making it a good step-up dive for intermediate divers; whitetip sharks rest under table corals.

odm-dlu0jg.name: Gili Meno Harbour
highlights: Sea turtles, moray eels, fusilier schools

odm-dp2jes.name: Bloodlet (12)
hazards: Moderate to strong current

odm-dp8jb4.name: Taotoi
highlights: Blacktip sharks, eagle rays, turtles, giant morays
odm-dp8jb4.summary: A shallow outer-lagoon dive on Moorea's north shore, close to the Taotoi channel where fish stream between lagoon and ocean. Easy depths suit beginners, with blacktip sharks, eagle rays, turtles and large moray eels.

odm-dpfuw6.name: Booby trap
odm-dpfuw6.access: Inside the Curaçao Marine Park, west edge of the Fuik Bay breakwater
highlights: Slope covered in all types of sponges
odm-dpfuw6.summary: Coral reef on the western end of the Fuik Bay breakwater inside the Marine Park; its slope is blanketed in sponges of many kinds, a good spot for sponge identification.
sources: Bluewater Dive Travel (Scuba Lodge & Ocean Suites)

odm-drnzhu.name: Avion Cessna 188
highlights: Sponge- and coral-covered plane; lobsters under wings
odm-drnzhu.summary: A decommissioned crop-spraying Cessna sunk in 2000 off Port-Louis in Grande-Terre, lying on sand at 23-24 m. Now covered in sponges and coral, with angelfish, jacks and lobsters; best for divers qualified to about 40 m.

odm-drqdsk.name: Fam Slope
highlights: Gorgonian corals on a steep slope
odm-drqdsk.summary: Steep slope that becomes a wall in places, in the Fam Islands. A relaxed drift past gorgonian corals, with little current and a depth from about 2 to 25 m, so it works for most levels.

odm-ds731y.name: Passe de Tiputa
highlights: Grey reef sharks, jacks, barracuda, rays
hazards: Strong tidal current; drift technique needed

odm-dtng4q.name: Andrea II (22)
highlights: Large coral formations in the shallows
Reef Renewal coral trees

odm-dvdm14.name: Calabas Reef
highlights: House reef
Night diving possible
Sea turtles

odm-dvvli4.name: Hanging Rock
highlights: Sun corals under a large rocky overhang
Small moray eels in the crevices

odm-dxw4u7.name: Reggies
highlights: Leopard sharks in the cave
Cleaning stations for mantas and rays
odm-dxw4u7.summary: A northern Tofo reef named for its big cave, usually guarded by a sleeping leopard shark. Green tree corals, cleaning stations and patrolling reef sharks and eagle rays make it a rewarding advanced dive.

odm-e0jttg.name: Playa Daaibooi
highlights: Turtles, parrotfish and occasional stingrays

odm-e3dm1p.name: Paradiso / Air Harbour
highlights: Frogfish, pipefish, seahorses, mandarin fish
Hawksbill turtles and sweetlips
odm-e3dm1p.summary: Shallow muck dive in the harbour at the southern end of Gili Air, suitable for all levels. Macro life dominates, with frogfish, pipefish and seahorses, and mandarin fish at dawn or dusk.

odm-e5n7fr.name: Galu
highlights: Turtles, ghost pipefish, seahorses, frogfish
Turtles, octopus, rays, nudibranchs

odm-e6ark6.name: Punta Deseo
highlights: Sharks resting on sand, turtles; whale sharks with plankton

odm-e6iml8.name: Sakatia
highlights: Popular for macro diving

odm-e6rh8b.name: Cabbage Patch Cocos Keeling
highlights: Cabbage-shaped coral, garden eels, whitetips

odm-eah2pm.name: Anse 3 airs
highlights: Small cargo wreck among coral heads
odm-eah2pm.summary: A shallow, easy dive behind Pointe Dufour at Les Anses-d'Arlet, with coral and rocks above a small cargo wreck that hosts reef fish and cuttlefish. A good first site for new divers.

odm-ealdvw.name: Poito
highlights: Napoleon wrasse, trevally, jacks and barracuda

odm-ec1vun.name: rocher creole
odm-ec1vun.access: Inside the Saint-Martin nature reserve; boats under 50 ft

odm-ech2jp.name: Flamingo Bay Wall
highlights: Fringing reef and wall with whip corals and sea fans
Seahorses and flamingo tongue snails

odm-eeggd1.name: Double Reef
highlights: Brain corals and sun anemones in the shallows
Two reefs separated by a wide sandy area
hazards: Rocky entry and surf; dive shoes needed
odm-eeggd1.summary: Two parallel reefs separated by a big sandy area, west of Santa Ana Bay. Shallows carry small brain corals and sun anemones, with fan and pencil coral beyond. Entry over a rocky beach with some surf.
sources: Bluewater Dive Travel (Scuba Lodge & Ocean Suites)

odm-ei5cjf.name: Parcel das Ancoras - Laje de Santos
highlights: Lost fishing anchors among the rocks
hazards: Depth and possible current

odm-el05cp.name: Corveta Ipiranga V17
highlights: Cannon on the stern; well preserved
hazards: Long decompression time
odm-el05cp.summary: A Brazilian Navy corvette sunk in 1983 off Noronha, rated one of the country's best wrecks. It sits around 54-64 m, so it is a technical or deep-experienced dive with long decompression.

odm-el1850.name: Blue MaoMao Arch
highlights: Shafts of sunlight through the arch
Thousands of blue maomao
odm-el1850.summary: The most photographed arch at the Poor Knights: a shallow, low-lying arch where light beams stream in through gaps in the rock above dense schools of blue maomao. Suits snorkellers and relaxed dives.

odm-elsamu.name: Rosario
highlights: Fan corals and gorgonians
Whale sharks in Oct-Nov
odm-elsamu.summary: A coral plateau off Nosy Be at roughly 14-22 m covered in fan corals and gorgonians, with leaf fish, stonefish and nudibranchs. Often a gentle drift dive, and a good place for whale sharks in October and November.

odm-ennl4r.name: White Hole
highlights: Round white sand patch at 35 ft

odm-eo6dba.name: Aquarium
highlights: Hawksbill and green turtles, white-tip reef sharks
odm-eo6dba.summary: A scenic Mnemba reef with sand patches close to the coral, where turtles, groupers and white-tip sharks are commonly seen. Current runs from slight to quite strong depending on the tide, so it is usually dived as a drift.

odm-eoy29e.name: Boga Wreck
highlights: Batfish, trevally, barracuda, morays, lionfish
Wreck props: wheel, statues, cars
odm-eoy29e.summary: A purpose-sunk wreck at Kubu, just north of Tulamben, reached from the beach. It lies at roughly 14-40 m depending on the part and the guide, so it is rated advanced; fish and coral now cover the hull.

odm-ep4tmk.name: Wairterang Wreck
highlights: Groupers, trevally, lionfish on the wreck
Critters in the surrounding sand
odm-ep4tmk.summary: A Second World War ship lying off Wairterang beach in Maumere Bay at roughly 12-33 m, largely coral-covered. It can be dived from shore, has no penetration, and the nearby sand is good for muck-style critters.

odm-ephvfj.name: Banc des gorgones
highlights: Abundant gorgonians near the coast
Ghost pipefish, seahorses, nudibranchs

odm-es5k8g.name: Epave du Gustavia (Wreck)
odm-es5k8g.summary: A 48 m cargo ship sunk in 1991 near the Pigeon islets, sitting upright at about 40 m. Reserved for Advanced divers with deep training; it is often visited by barracuda and counted among Guadeloupe's best dives.

odm-euklpv.name: Rocher du Diamant
highlights: Submerged cliffs, caves and the 15 m-high Diamant fault
odm-euklpv.summary: The remains of a volcanic dome off Martinique's south coast, with drop-offs, caves and a swim-through fault, diveable from the surface down to about 60 m. Exposed to current, so it suits divers with some experience.

odm-eveds9.name: Pura Mas Gading
highlights: Barrel sponges and coral bommies
Mola mola cleaning in season
odm-eveds9.summary: A sloping reef on the north coast of Nusa Penida, found by a small temple in the shallows. Usually an easy drift over soft corals, barrel sponges and bommies, with a chance of sunfish cleaning in season.

odm-eyqsdu.name: Cheynes III (Wreck)
highlights: Leafy seadragons in kelp near the wreck
odm-eyqsdu.summary: A former whale chaser scuttled in the early 1980s off Michaelmas Island, King George Sound, as a recreational dive site. The hull has since split in two; the dive is moderate in depth and leafy seadragons live in nearby kelp.

odm-f4k304.name: Invisibles (51)
highlights: Double reef split by sand chutes
Eagle rays frequent

odm-f4rbpv.name: Secret Bay
highlights: Frogfish, ghost pipefish, dragonets, seahorses
hazards: Visibility drops at low tide or if silt is kicked up
odm-f4rbpv.summary: A very shallow muck site beside Gilimanuk harbour on Bali's west tip. Fine black volcanic sand and rubble, not coral, hold frogfish, ghost pipefish and dragonets; best at high tide when visibility is better.

odm-fardja.name: Pointe Borgnèse
odm-fardja.summary: A reef-wall dive in Sainte-Luce Bay, close to shore and sheltered from wind and swell. The shallow, reassuring conditions make it a favourite for beginners, with clear water over two drop-offs down to roughly 25 m.

odm-fc03rs.name: San Benedicto Canyon
highlights: Schooling scalloped hammerheads
Giant Pacific manta rays, silky and Galapagos sharks
odm-fc03rs.summary: An exposed open-ocean site off the south end of San Benedicto in the Revillagigedo archipelago, reachable only by liveaboard. It is rated advanced to expert and is among the best shark dives in the archipelago, with hammerhead schools, mantas and several shark species.

odm-fcf2uh.name: Warahnus
highlights: Big coral structures, fusiliers at 12-15 m

odm-fcgong.name: Seaview, Carriacou
highlights: Eels, octopus, schools of fish, seahorses

odm-fcnrsd.name: Tapor Tamiyam, Cape Kri, Raja Ampat
highlights: Record fish counts on a single dive
Sharks, tuna, trevally, bumphead parrotfish
hazards: Mild to strong current; reef drops past 40 m
odm-fcnrsd.summary: Raja Ampat's best-known reef: a steep slope from the shallows into very deep water, thick with hard and soft coral and big predators. Famous for fish counts; current ranges from mild to strong, so it suits intermediate to advanced divers.

odm-fd73c0.name: Sandy’s Plateau
highlights: Lobsters under overhangs, crabs in barrel sponges
Gorgonians and hard corals on a wall below a shallow plateau
odm-fd73c0.summary: Shallow plateau north of Jan Thiel that drops into a coral-covered wall rich in gorgonians, hard coral and barrel sponges, with lobsters and crabs. Reached by boat or by a swim from Jan Thiel Bay.
sources: Bluewater Dive Travel (Scuba Lodge & Ocean Suites)

odm-fem74k.name: Banc des Licornes
highlights: Many stonefish, stingrays and rhinopias
Eagle and manta rays pass through

odm-fh5tkf.name: Tombant d Ohotu
odm-fh5tkf.depthNote: Reef flat at 40 ft sloping to about 100 ft before the wall
highlights: Grey and whitetip sharks, tuna, manta rays on the wall

odm-fh70c9.name: Tug 2, Wreck
highlights: Lionfish and leaf fish on the wreck
Garden eels on surrounding sand
odm-fh70c9.summary: A small tug on a sandy bottom close to Snake Reef, about 18-20 m down. It has no interior access, shelters lionfish and leaf fish, and is a popular first wreck for newly qualified divers.

odm-fhcq1i.name: MV Produce, wreck
highlights: Brindle bass and harlequin goldies
Bow and stern largely intact
hazards: Wreck breaking up; penetration not advised
odm-fhcq1i.summary: Norwegian molasses carrier that hit the Northern Pinnacles in 1974 and lies on her starboard side at about 32 m. The bow and stern are still recognisable, resident brindle bass and goldies shelter on her, but the midship has collapsed and penetration is discouraged.

odm-fhuqtd.name: Pedras Secas
highlights: Tunnels, crevices and natural arches
Thresher and sand sharks, barracuda, rays
hazards: Currents
odm-fhuqtd.summary: Rocks breaking the surface, undercut by canyons, tunnels and arches covered in sponges and coral. Expect barracuda, rays, turtles and sharks, and watch for moderate current.

odm-fihm2r.name: Nebo Wreck, Aliwal Shoal
highlights: Stern, propeller and boiler remain
Swim-through at the propeller
odm-fihm2r.summary: A steamship that capsized in 1884 and now rests upside down on sand near 27 m. The stern, propeller and boiler are the recognisable parts, and the area teems with small fish such as kingfish and goldies.

odm-fil9uf.name: Kinasi Pass
highlights: Barracuda, reef fish shoals, occasional turtles
odm-fil9uf.summary: A famous drift through a channel with two walls, a deeper shelf and a shallower wall. Strong tidal flow draws barracuda and reef fish past the divers, so it suits experienced divers.

odm-fjxuoq.name: Shark Alley
highlights: Cowsharks often seen
Big granite boulders with sand patches

odm-fkpgl2.name: Sherwood
highlights: Large cleaning station with mantas and rays
Green tree coral and snapper schools
odm-fkpgl2.summary: A small deep site on the north side of Tofo Bay, built around a cleaning station on top of a rock dome covered in green tree corals. Mantas, rays and tight snapper schools visit; it can only be dived in mild current.

odm-flfloo.name: Biodiversity House Reef
highlights: Table corals in the shallows, night-dive critters
odm-flfloo.summary: Gentle fringe house reef off the Biodiversity jetty, sloping from about 2 m to 20 m with little current. Soft and table corals fill the shallows, and it is popular for night dives and snorkelling.

odm-fofl2t.name: Heron Island
odm-fofl2t.reason: A whole coral cay with many named dive sites

odm-fotccx.name: Escambrón
highlights: Artificial reef of columns and statues

odm-fpn5jz.name: Airport Caves
highlights: Swim-through caverns with glassy sweepers
Seahorses and toadfish on the reef
odm-fpn5jz.summary: A south-side reef wall off the old airstrip with a U-shaped swim-through cave around 15 ft and a sandy floor sloping to roughly 70 ft. Glassy sweepers shelter inside, and seahorses, stingrays and eagle rays are common.

odm-fu2sk5.name: Eel Valley
odm-fu2sk5.access: Inside the Curaçao Marine Park, west edge of the Fuik Bay breakwater

odm-fvwors.name: Kubu Reef
highlights: Corals against black sand

odm-fytywz.name: Playa Shon Mosa
highlights: Vibrant corals, tropical fish and occasional seahorses

odm-fz3c5w.name: Shallow Wrecks at Butler Bay
highlights: Coral-encrusted wrecks with schooling reef fish
odm-fz3c5w.summary: Three wrecks (trawler Suffolk Maid, tug Northwind, oil barge Virgin Islander) lying close together in Butler Bay at about 55-70 ft. Best by boat; slight current, good visibility and heavy coral growth.

odm-g27w5i.name: Punt Canon
highlights: Intact coral reefs full of fish

odm-g730ni.name: Ted's Point
odm-g730ni.depthNote: Wall to about 40 ft; sailboat wreck at about 60 ft
highlights: Small sunken sailboat at about 60 ft
Groupers, blue tang, morays, eagle rays

odm-gagwk8.name: Brightledge
highlights: Hawksbill turtles, colourful sponges, excellent visibility
odm-gagwk8.summary: A popular Barbados west-coast reef ranging from about 65 ft to beyond 125 ft, rated intermediate to advanced. Known for visibility, colourful corals and sponges and hawksbill turtles.

odm-gaxxgd.name: Renco
highlights: Leaf fish, octopus, mantis shrimp

odm-gb9px6.name: Deep Sponge - 2 Mile Reef
highlights: Vase-shaped sponges
Frequent game fish sightings

odm-gbencc.name: West Side Story (Mele 2)
highlights: Large staghorn coral field
odm-gbencc.summary: A big staghorn coral field near Hideaway Island off Efate, with the reef beginning about 6 m below the surface and falling away past 30 m. Damselfish and anemones live among the branches.

odm-gbewqb.name: Big Rock Market
highlights: Excellent visibility in calm weather
hazards: Exposed to Atlantic swell; dived less often

odm-ge2y4k.name: Table Top
highlights: Cleaning stations; large groupers
Stingrays and honeycomb whiprays on sand

odm-genvyc.name: Blue Corner
highlights: Mola mola and pelagic encounters
hazards: Extreme currents
odm-genvyc.summary: A deep drop-off off the north-west corner of Nusa Lembongan with some of the strongest conditions around the islands. Advanced to expert only; pelagics such as mola mola and bull rays can appear.

odm-geqk6i.name: Motu Nuhi-Nuhi (l’aquarium)
highlights: Coral garden with many colourful fish

odm-gfpa66.name: Catalina The Wall
odm-gfpa66.summary: Drop-off on the east side of Catalina Island, reached by boat from La Romana or Bayahibe, where the wall falls away in steps into deep Caribbean water. Divers choose their depth to match certification.

odm-gh34dj.name: Artemis
highlights: Large coral formations; octopus, eagle ray

odm-ghgjjv.name: Cannibal Rock Komodo
highlights: Frogfish, pygmy seahorses, nudibranchs
Giant trevallies and nurse sharks
Encrusting sponges and macro life
odm-ghgjjv.summary: A sheltered bay in the south of Komodo National Park near Rinca, loved for dense sponge-covered reef with both macro subjects such as frogfish and pygmy seahorses and larger visitors like giant trevally. Conditions are usually calm and suit a wide range of divers.

odm-gj4ixy.name: Pinnicles Ponta Malongane
highlights: Bull, hammerhead and dusky sharks in season

odm-gls0jd.name: Roman Rock
highlights: Large granite reef around a lighthouse

odm-grm8yk.name: Nurse Rock
highlights: Grey nurse sharks, July to October

odm-gsnev4.name: Bonaire
odm-gsnev4.reason: The whole island of Bonaire, not a single dive site

odm-gt3nsj.name: The Gutter
highlights: Weedy seadragons, pygmy pipehorses, blue devilfish
odm-gt3nsj.summary: Shore dive at Bass Point entered down a rocky gutter at the water edge, dropping to an underwater amphitheatre near 20 m. Rated suitable for a range of experience levels; watch swell at the exit and no-deco limits.

odm-gu8odc.name: Batu Belah
highlights: Sponge and gorgonian reef
Reef sharks; occasional threshers and eagle rays

odm-gweonh.name: Le piton aux gorgones
odm-gweonh.depthNote: Pinnacle rises from deep water to about 42 m (per operator)
highlights: Gorgonian-covered pinnacle, whitetip sharks, turtles

odm-h44ua4.name: CJ’s Dropoff
highlights: Steep wall dropping below 140 ft
Eagle rays, barracuda, morays and turtles

odm-h53xft.name: Manta Bommie
highlights: Manta rays cleaned atop the bommies

odm-h5jnsd.name: Mbwangawa
highlights: Lobsters under plate corals, cuttlefish, turtles
odm-h5jnsd.summary: An extensive reef of hard and soft corals with plate-coral patches off northeast Zanzibar. A mild current allows a relaxed drift, with lobsters, cuttlefish and turtles regularly seen.

odm-h5uvxg.name: Wonderland
odm-h5uvxg.mooring: Anchor sits in about 10 m of water
highlights: Healthy hard and soft corals

odm-hcjsqv.name: Mitsio Wreck
highlights: Snapper and fusilier schools around the hull
Scorpionfish and stonefish on the wreck
odm-hcjsqv.summary: A shrimp trawler deliberately sunk in the mid-2000s on a sandy bottom near Nosy Be, resting around 26-28 m. Dense schools hide the hull, with scorpionfish, stonefish and barracuda around it.

odm-hjhawe.name: Soufreire Pinnacles
highlights: Frogfish and seahorses

odm-hjrv5g.name: Portsea Hole
odm-hjrv5g.access: Inside Port Phillip Heads Marine National Park
highlights: Vertical reef with sponges, soft corals and invertebrates

odm-hkbgje.name: Toopua
highlights: Eagle rays and stingrays over sand, morays, giant clams
odm-hkbgje.summary: A lagoon dive off Motu Toopua with coral walls, small caves and swim-throughs, then a sandy floor where eagle rays and stingrays feed. Suits all levels and sometimes runs as a drift dive depending on weather.

odm-hkh49t.name: Survival Bukabuka Island
highlights: Yellow-tailed fusiliers and pyramid butterflyfish
Occasional green turtle

odm-hl3i9n.name: Yenbuba Jetty
highlights: Schools of batfish and sweetlips
hazards: Boat traffic around the jetty

odm-hof2ng.name: HMAS Swan (Wreck)
odm-hof2ng.access: Boat only; private boats need a permit from Dunsborough Visitor Centre
highlights: Schools of bullseyes inside the hull
odm-hof2ng.summary: Former navy destroyer scuttled in 1997 off Dunsborough, upright in roughly 30-35 m with parts of the superstructure intact and bullseyes filling the rooms.

odm-hpj90l.name: The Halliburton (Wreck)
odm-hpj90l.penetration: Several areas can be entered and explored
highlights: Upright wreck with many nooks and crannies
odm-hpj90l.summary: A deliberately sunk ship standing upright on sand near the mouth of Utila harbour, with the bridge top near 65 ft and the seabed around 100 ft. Several compartments can be explored and it is full of small marine life.

odm-hs4okz.name: Clown Reef
highlights: Clownfish and anemones
Tiny sexy shrimp for macro hunters

odm-hse7cc.name: Abu Helal
odm-hse7cc.depthNote: Lagoon 7-12 m; canyon 40-60 m is technical
highlights: Coral garden and canyon with swim-throughs

odm-hutguf.name: Black Rock Reef
odm-hutguf.mooring: Mooring buoy; mooring pin at 30 ft
highlights: Coral gardens and freestanding coral heads
Resident school of reef squid

odm-hx4fuu.name: Simio Bipolar
highlights: Spotted eagle rays
Coral islands on flat sand with many reef fish

odm-hx8xos.name: Airplane Wreck (Santa Martha)
odm-hx8xos.depthNote: Remains of a light aircraft at about 7 m

odm-hxdyvm.name: San Francisco Wall
highlights: Spotted eagle rays
Slope that drops off into deep blue
odm-hxdyvm.summary: A slope covered in coral between roughly 40 and 70 ft that then falls away as a vertical wall. Gentle to moderate current and good visibility make it workable for all levels, with eagle rays a regular sight.

odm-hz0xou.name: Mini Wall
highlights: Eagle rays, turtles, batfish and sweetlips
odm-hz0xou.summary: Easy central Komodo dive: a reef plateau teeming with fish that drops into a wall past 30 m. Little current makes it a popular check-out dive, with turtles, eagle rays and plenty of macro.

odm-hz36jx.name: Black Rock - Hawaii
highlights: Green sea turtles and night-time eels, lobsters, reef squid
odm-hz36jx.summary: Black Rock (Pu'u Keka'a) at Ka'anapali is an easy beach-entry dive along a rocky ledge reaching about 30 feet. Suited to beginners, with turtles by day and octopus, eels and squid at night.

odm-i6b1f2.name: Ashos Gap (Shark Cleaning Station)
highlights: Grey reef shark cleaning station

odm-i6vqpz.name: Jane Sea (Wreck)
highlights: Gorgonians and orange cup coral cover the wreck
Sits upright next to a coral reef
hazards: Wreck is collapsing; one operator bars penetration
odm-i6vqpz.summary: Cement freighter sunk in 1988 as an artificial reef, upright on sand beside Barcadera Reef with the bow near 18 m and the propeller around 28 m. Covered in gorgonians and cup coral; boat access only.

odm-i769u2.name: Jardines
highlights: Coral fingers; schools of porkfish and grunts

odm-icj8ng.name: Tupitipiti
odm-icj8ng.depthNote: Guides give 10-30 m and 20-150 ft; not reconciled
odm-icj8ng.access: About 40 min boat ride to the southern outer reef
highlights: Coral caves, canyons and swim-throughs; sponges
hazards: Only dived in calm weather

odm-ieffng.name: La Pointe au Sel
highlights: Jacks, dogtooth tuna, marlin on the big wall
odm-ieffng.summary: Réunion's big-wall dive off Saint-Leu: a platform near the island edge ends in a sheer drop beyond 70 m. Schools of jacks, dogtooth tuna and the occasional marlin pass by, and current means it suits experienced divers.

odm-igz53k.name: Les trois Pointes
highlights: Lava flow with barracuda and many reef fish
odm-igz53k.summary: An easy dive beside the Vieux-Fort lighthouse in southern Basse-Terre, where volcanic rock mixes with pale sand. Shallow enough for introductory dives, with a lava flow that attracts barracuda and plenty of reef fish.

odm-ihxhcd.name: New Reef (Dom Te Te)
highlights: Coral bommies, many fish schools

odm-ik6p0u.name: Checkers
highlights: Potato bass, frogfish, snapper clouds
odm-ik6p0u.summary: A horseshoe-shaped ridge in Ponta Bay at 15-18 m, easy enough for open water divers. Clouds of snappers and fusiliers hang over it, with potato bass, morays, turtles and the odd frogfish.

odm-imm1om.name: Diamond Reef
highlights: Small 200-yard reef wall, ideal for all levels

odm-in2iu5.name: Elphinstone South
highlights: Oceanic whitetip sharks with pilot fish
hazards: Strong current; risk of being swept off the reef
odm-in2iu5.summary: An open-ocean reef off Marsa Alam whose southern plateau sits at roughly 20-40 m. Currents can run hard along the walls, so it is a drift dive for advanced divers, famed for oceanic whitetip sharks.

odm-ip9fzp.name: El Aguila (Wreck)
odm-ip9fzp.penetration: Wreck is in open sections; penetration possible
highlights: Intact mast, large groupers and green morays
hazards: Storm-broken into three sections
odm-ip9fzp.summary: A large cargo ship lying on sand at roughly 30-33 m beside the reef wall, split into three pieces by a hurricane. It is an advanced-level dive with an upright mast, open sections to explore and big groupers and moray eels.

odm-ipf01g.name: The Cathedral
highlights: Chimney to the surface beyond the pulpit
odm-ipf01g.summary: A tall, narrow cavern a short boat ride from Port Vila, with a wide entrance on a sandy floor around 22-28 m and a chimney that lets divers surface inside.

odm-ipgz98.name: POINTE FERRY
highlights: Coral band forming a wall several metres high

odm-iql4qk.name: Anchor Point
odm-iql4qk.mooring: Mooring buoy; mooring pin at 58 ft
highlights: Swim-through leading onto the wall
Hawksbill and green turtles on the north wall

odm-irb7xj.name: Aquarium
highlights: Many reef fish and moray eels
Eagle rays seen up close
odm-irb7xj.summary: A gentle reef off Flic en Flac that operators use as the starting dive for newer divers and mixed-ability groups, packed with reef fish and morays, with eagle rays often passing close by.

odm-irng2g.name: Puerto Morelos The Aquarium
highlights: Coral fingers; schools of porkfish and grunts
Eels, rays and occasional turtles
hazards: Good buoyancy control needed among coral fingers

odm-irz11m.name: Mayhem
highlights: Many fusiliers on the north and east sides

odm-it1675.name: Barwon Banks
highlights: Barracuda, trevally and batfish schools

odm-iuizje.name: Toyapakeh
highlights: Schools of triggerfish, batfish and trevally
Coral plateau 5-15 m, drop-off to deep wall
hazards: Strong, unpredictable currents
odm-iuizje.summary: Penida's most praised site, in a bay on the Toyapakeh strait: a shallow coral plateau, terraces and a wall to the south. Fish life is dense, but current can be strong and changeable, so the deeper drift suits experienced divers.

odm-iv7j2q.name: Melasti
highlights: Frogfish, harlequin shrimp, nudibranchs, seahorses
odm-iv7j2q.summary: A sandy, coral-poor muck site on the Amed coast, calm and shallow, great for macro. Frogfish, harlequin shrimp, nudibranchs and seahorses are regular finds.

odm-iye906.name: Gili Selang
highlights: Hammerhead and grey reef sharks

odm-izlgyt.name: Canon
highlights: Old cannon from the 1615 Banda wreck
Macro life on sandbank and slope
odm-izlgyt.summary: A shallow north Flic en Flac reef with a small slope and sandbank, popular for buoyancy practice and macro photography. A cannon from a 1615 Dutch ship lies on the rempart.

odm-j145r3.name: Dial Rock
highlights: Calm shore entry with a 150 m surface swim

odm-j4aqc2.name: Emerald
highlights: Sandy slope with artificial structures
Gorgonian fans, eel gardens, reef sharks
odm-j4aqc2.summary: A quiet Tulamben boat or jukung dive starting in a sandy bay with artificial structures, then a drop-off where sponges and gorgonian fans get richer from about 20-30 m. Reef sharks are a good sighting.

odm-j6a3by.name: Bossy’s Canyon
odm-j6a3by.summary: A deep fault and wall off Saint-Leu on Réunion's west coast. The drop starts shallow, around 6 m, and falls away into a 60-70 m abyss, giving a dramatic wall dive.

odm-j7nwns.name: M.V. Mataora
highlights: Anemonefish, groupers, Moorish idols on wreck

odm-j8kmck.name: Sampalan (Nusa Penida, Bali)
highlights: Rich corals, schooling batfish, tuna, turtles

odm-j9hupi.name: Atlantis
highlights: Square boulders like a sunken city
hazards: Very unpredictable current; far offshore

odm-jaommq.name: Bunutan
highlights: Garden eels, barrel sponges, stingrays, reef sharks
odm-jaommq.summary: A drift dive along the Amed coast with garden eels, barrel sponges, stingrays and reef sharks. Current is moderate and usually runs parallel to shore; advanced open water is suggested.

odm-jdujxv.name: Barracuda - Cozumel
highlights: Reef sharks, eagle rays, barracuda
hazards: Extreme, unpredictable current; trips often restricted
odm-jdujxv.summary: An exposed reef on Cozumel's northern tip with a strong, unpredictable current. Operators run it selectively; it rewards expert divers with reef sharks and eagle rays.

odm-jfh9x5.name: Pinnacles
odm-jfh9x5.depthNote: Two pinnacles from 24 m sand; tops at 16 m and 14 m
highlights: Massive blue anemone on one pinnacle

odm-jg7nht.name: Sea Fan City
highlights: Wall covered in large sea fans
Pygmy seahorses can hide in the fans
odm-jg7nht.summary: A coral wall off Kuata abundant with sea fans, with a shallow hard-coral garden above and nooks for macro life. Most of the best of it lies above about 20 m.

odm-jkprqh.name: Bounty Wreck, Gili Tarawang
highlights: Groupers and sweetlips among the wreckage

odm-jkqahr.name: Julian Rocks - Needles
highlights: Big bommies with rays and leopard sharks
odm-jkqahr.summary: Large bommies at the southern end of Julian Rocks off Byron Bay, in roughly 10-15 m. Currents bring schools of fish, and rays and leopard sharks are regular visitors.

odm-jm764d.name: Waynes World
highlights: Turtle cave
Raggies in the gullies in summer
Colourful soft corals
odm-jm764d.summary: Flat, slightly deeper section of Two Mile Reef (14-16 m) that suits drift dives. Soft corals and a turtle cave are the highlights, and ragged-tooth sharks gather in its gullies in summer.

odm-jmjjur.name: Jack Point
highlights: Big green soft corals; overhangs and crevasses

odm-jmm5r5.name: FRIWEN WALL
highlights: Macro life and many nudibranchs
Two small caves at the start

odm-jnr43p.name: Key Hole
highlights: Colourful boulders and walls

odm-jqxl2g.name: Stragglers' Reef
highlights: Canyons with eels, octopus, lobster, eagle rays

odm-jtxrfl.name: Segara
odm-jtxrfl.depthNote: Artificial reef structures at about 9 m
highlights: Coral-covered artificial reef (2008)

odm-jx25hx.name: Mayan Princess House Reef
highlights: Large sponges, sea fans and gorgonians on the wall
Nurse sharks and reef sharks

odm-jyr761.name: Double Cove Marine Reserve
odm-jyr761.access: No-fishing area (prohibited fishing in the whole cove)
highlights: Tame fish between the two arms
Koi wreck inside the no-fish area
hazards: West arm exposed in southerly winds

odm-jyu5ko.name: Catedrales
highlights: Coral formations off Isla Verde

odm-k0t74c.name: Flinders Reef
highlights: Hawksbill and green turtles; cleaning station
sources: Nigel Marsh Photography (Scuba Diver magazine article)

odm-k3bpys.name: Seaquest Shallow
highlights: Southern stingrays, pipefish and flounders on sand
odm-k3bpys.summary: A gentle sandy flat dotted with coral heads, regarded as a good beginner and photography dive. Stingrays hide in the sand and small species such as pipefish and flounders can be found by going slowly.

odm-k3y8dx.name: Les Arches de Sakatia
highlights: Rock with three small arches

odm-k4xrg7.name: Gotham, Sodwana Bay
hazards: Deep dive; narcosis risk at 35-40 m
odm-k4xrg7.summary: The deepest of the Five Mile Reef sites, a ledge dropping to about 40 m toward the 5 Mile Canyon. Deep-specialty certification is needed, and dives are capped at 40 m.

odm-k56p3v.name: THE HOLE
highlights: Only safe swim-through on the Mooloolaba reefs
Wobbegongs and groupers live in the bowl below

odm-k6duzw.name: Shark Point, Gili Trawangan
highlights: Turtles feeding on seagrass at about 5 m
odm-k6duzw.summary: Popular slope off the northwest of Gili Trawangan, falling toward the Lombok Strait. Turtles graze the shallows and reef sharks are common, while experienced divers can drop to about 30 m.

odm-k7oyid.name: Meno Slope
highlights: Green and hawksbill turtles
Sandy slope with coral blocks
odm-k7oyid.summary: Sandy slope off Gili Meno's west side, running from about 5 m to 28-30 m with scattered coral blocks. The shallow part suits beginners, and green and hawksbill turtles are regularly seen.

odm-kbvbu3.name: Terrigal Haven
highlights: Giant cuttlefish in winter, blue gropers
Port Jackson sharks in breeding season
odm-kbvbu3.summary: A sheltered harbour dive beside the Terrigal boat ramp, shielded from southerly swell with minimal tide and a gentle sandy slope. Good for beginners, refreshers and macro photography, with cuttlefish, gropers and nudibranchs.

odm-kdbd4e.name: Tackle Box
highlights: Canyons, caverns and tunnels
Caribbean reef sharks, nurse sharks and eagle rays
odm-kdbd4e.summary: Canyon-and-groove reef about a mile off San Pedro with vertical walls, caverns and tunnels, dropping to around 30 m. Reef and nurse sharks and eagle rays are regularly seen; rated intermediate.

odm-khsln4.name: Roonies
highlights: Resident seahorse and longnose hawkfish
odm-khsln4.summary: Compact deeper site off Two Mile Reef at roughly 27-32 m, requiring Advanced Open Water. Small and busy, it is known for a resident seahorse and longnose hawkfish.

odm-kjk9bq.name: Dan’s Reef
hazards: Strong currents during tidal changes

odm-kl72f8.name: La Poza, Xcalak
highlights: Schools of tarpon sheltering in the reef gaps
Eagle rays, groupers and barracuda
odm-kl72f8.summary: A trench-like formation just inside Xcalak's barrier reef, famous for resident tarpon that shelter there from currents offshore. The dive suits a range of levels, with depths from about 9 to 24 m and a chance of eagle rays, groupers and manatees.

odm-klqqza.name: Danglebens Pinnacles
highlights: Winter jack and cero feeding frenzy at south pinnacle

odm-kt4ja2.name: Giants Castle
highlights: Potato groupers, manta cleaning stations
Tornado schools of giant trevally
odm-kt4ja2.summary: Tofo's closest deep site: a long ridge and wall just outside the bay, dived as a drift along the current. Several manta cleaning stations, big groupers and trevally schools make it a favourite, and it is the fallback when currents run strong.

odm-kxx9fl.name: Castle Rock
highlights: Large bommie with temperate reef life

odm-kyqz2y.name: Ressurreta
highlights: Parrotfish, turtles and brain corals
odm-kyqz2y.summary: A calm reef beside the Canal da Rata that works as an easy second dive for newer divers or as a gentle drift. Depths run roughly 8-15 m, with turtles and reef fish on the coral.

odm-kzhn0d.name: tinderbox
highlights: Bigbelly seahorses, rock lobsters, weedy seadragons
odm-kzhn0d.summary: South of Hobart marine reserve with rocky reef, kelp and sand, suited to beginners and photographers, with calm clear water and seahorses and seadragons.

odm-kziqt1.name: Playa Cas Abao
odm-kziqt1.access: Beach entrance fee (about 10 Nafl, higher on Sundays)
highlights: Mushroom-like coral formations, barracuda and eagle rays
odm-kziqt1.summary: Walk-in shore dive from a pretty beach on the west coast: a sandy start leads to a drop-off around 6 m and a coral-covered wall. Easy navigation makes it a good beginner site.

odm-kzu4s9.name: Small Wall
highlights: Overhangs sheltering soldierfish, grunts and damselfish
Shallow, lively reef next to Director's Bay
odm-kzu4s9.summary: A small wall just past Director's Bay toward the open sea, relatively shallow, with overhangs and nooks that shelter schools of soldierfish, grunts and damselfish.
sources: Bluewater Dive Travel (Scuba Lodge & Ocean Suites)

odm-l0o08p.name: Marble Arch
highlights: Three connected arch swim-throughs

odm-l1c8eu.name: KeiSei 113, Wreck
hazards: Cracked, fragile hull; risky to penetrate
odm-l1c8eu.summary: An old boat sunk in 1987 as an artificial reef off Flic en Flac, lying on a 36 m bottom and usually dived together with the rich reef at Park. Deep-diver level; the concrete-coated hull is fragile.

odm-l1hlm5.name: Amazing Maze
highlights: Channels, swim-throughs and canyons
Reef fish sheltering in coral formations
odm-l1hlm5.summary: A maze of channels, swim-throughs and canyons on the outer reef by Nananu-i-Ra. Depth is modest so buoyancy control matters more than the numbers, and the coral nooks suit photography.

odm-l33iy8.name: Maggie’s Maze
odm-l33iy8.mooring: Mooring buoy; mooring pin at 40 ft
highlights: Winding canyon ending in a swim-through
Nurse sharks under the overhangs
Horse-eyed jacks around the arches

odm-l5vvgi.name: Scotts Head Pinnacle
highlights: Swim-through full of soldierfish; deepwater sea fans
odm-l5vvgi.summary: A volcanic pinnacle in the Soufrière Scotts Head Marine Reserve, pierced by a swim-through at about 35 ft that leads to a crater wall falling past 120 ft. Soldierfish fill the passage and the wall is covered in sea fans.

odm-l6ih8k.name: Kinondo
highlights: Very large moray eels on the southern reef
Gentle slopes and steep walls

odm-l8izat.name: Cenote Angelita
highlights: Hydrogen sulfide cloud hovering above the floor
odm-l8izat.summary: A deep cenote in Quintana Roo where a layer of hydrogen sulfide forms a misty cloud over the bottom. Reserved for advanced or deep-certified divers because of the depths involved.

odm-l9b75t.name: Yellow Submarine
highlights: Eagle rays, frogfish and turtles
Octopus on night dives

odm-lae2rt.name: Starship
odm-lae2rt.depthNote: Operator range 0-60 m; guide max 30 m
highlights: Schools of fusiliers, turtles and eagle rays
odm-lae2rt.summary: A drift dive along a ridge and wall at Wakatobi's Tomia area, rated beginner. A gentle current carries divers over healthy reef with fusilier schools, turtles and the odd eagle ray.

odm-laph2r.name: MV Captain Keith Tibbetts (Wreck)
highlights: 330 ft ex-Cuban Navy frigate with intact guns
Sponge-covered hull; turtles, barracuda, groupers
hazards: Mid-section and stern storm-damaged: tangled structure
odm-laph2r.summary: A 330 ft former Soviet-built frigate sunk in 1996 off Cayman Brac as an artificial reef. It sits between about 20 and 90 ft, is covered in sponges, and storm damage has opened the structure up while leaving guns and the bow's red star.
sources: Cayman Islands Department of Tourism (Explore Cayman)

odm-lbgwxc.name: Le Jardin de Corail
highlights: Bronze bust of Commandant Cousteau at 12 m
odm-lbgwxc.summary: A shallow coral massif on the east face of the Pigeon islets in the Cousteau Reserve, down to about 20 m. Home to dense tropical fish and the bronze Cousteau bust lying at 12 m.

odm-lct3ve.name: Passe de Tikehau - Tuheiava
highlights: Barracuda, hammerheads, mantas, big fish schools
odm-lct3ve.summary: Tikehau's only pass, a narrow channel dived as a drift with the incoming tide. Shoals of barracuda, tuna and sharks, with hammerheads and mantas possible, make it the atoll's top dive; the tide must be timed with a local guide.

odm-leiaze.name: Blue Lagoon
highlights: Frogfish, ribbon eels, nudibranchs
Cleaning stations below 20 m
odm-leiaze.summary: Padang Bai's classic macro site: a sandy bay with coral at its edge, then a slope with coral blocks and a wall. Expect frogfish, ribbon eels and nudibranchs, and cleaning stations deeper than about 20 m.

odm-lfhela.name: San Pedro - Belize
odm-lfhela.reason: A town on Ambergris Caye, not a dive site

odm-li53tn.name: Pasir Timbul
highlights: Fish and shark action on a coral slope

odm-litzbk.name: Atlantic Princess Wreck (Bayahibe)
hazards: Penetration unsafe after storm damage

odm-ljhjbc.name: Stratmann Wreck
highlights: Tug with garden eels, moray and lobster; night dive
odm-ljhjbc.summary: A sunken tug off Bequia lying on sand at about 18 m, with the mooring on top near 5 m. Portholes, propeller and cargo hold hold eels and lobsters, and the dive finishes over the Devil's Table reef.

odm-lla5v7.name: Cuatro piedras, Catalina Islands
hazards: Currents can make it hard to stay on the sand patch

odm-lq2cgt.name: La Crique Abricot
highlights: Sergeant majors, parrotfish and turtles on seagrass
odm-lq2cgt.summary: A sheltered cove at Grande Anse d'Arlet, down to about 20-25 m, with rock heads, faults and seagrass beds. Calm and protected from current, it suits introductory dives and beginners and is rich in turtles and reef fish.

odm-lrma5s.name: Chankanaab
highlights: Stingrays, snappers, morays, lionfish
Night dives with octopus in the south
odm-lrma5s.summary: A shallow, sheltered reef off Chankanaab park with calm, predictable conditions. It suits every level and is good for stingrays, morays and night-time octopus.

odm-lssxra.name: Mirko's Reef
highlights: Healthy coral, green turtles, schooling fish

odm-lu2f3k.name: Anina (Wreck)
highlights: Freighter with orange coral and tropical fish

odm-lvwhas.name: Jack-A-Dan, Carriacou
highlights: Reef and sandy bottom frequented by rays

odm-lwskfo.name: Fam Wall (Keruwo Channel)
highlights: Reliable drift along a long wall
Manta rays, giant trevally, pygmy seahorses, turtles
odm-lwskfo.summary: A drift dive along one long wall with steep slopes on the east side of Keruo Island, Raja Ampat. Currents through the channel can be strong; mantas, trevally, turtles and pygmy seahorses are seen.

odm-ly6st9.name: Skillion Cave
highlights: Enormous colony of jewel anemones
Blue gropers inside the crack
hazards: East or north-east swell breaks on entry and exit
odm-ly6st9.summary: A shore dive from the rock platform north of Terrigal Haven that follows a wall down to a crack in the reef with a boulder roof. It reaches about 20 m, and jewel anemones and gropers live inside. Swell from the east makes entry and exit unsafe.
sources: Michael McFadyen's Scuba Diving Web Site

odm-lyi1v1.name: Partridge Point
highlights: Very large granite boulders and outcrops

odm-m0gqmq.name: Alma Bay
highlights: Granite boulders, corals, rays and nudibranchs
Green turtles cruise through
odm-m0gqmq.summary: A sheltered, patrolled beach on Magnetic Island that slopes gently to about 5-8 m, used heavily for teaching new divers. Granite boulders, corals, rays, nudibranchs and the odd turtle make it a relaxed shore dive.

odm-m2rc1k.name: Gold Coast Seaway
highlights: North Wall: pelagic fish, wobbegongs, whaler sharks
hazards: Tidal current; dive at high-tide slack
odm-m2rc1k.summary: An estuary-mouth shore dive at the end of The Spit, split into the South Wall, North Wall and pipes. Tide drives everything: go at high-tide slack for the clearest water, then expect wobbegongs, pelagics and rays along the walls.

odm-m4t4qn.name: White Reef
odm-m4t4qn.access: Within a rahui (no-take area) protecting the reef

odm-m7fvrx.name: Fish Bowl
highlights: Swim-through arch with barracuda; reef sharks
hazards: Can become dangerous in rough seas
odm-m7fvrx.summary: A fish-rich reef in 40-60 ft near the harbour entrance off Great Bay, reached by boat. A swim-through arch often holds barracuda and reef sharks are common; suitable for all levels but rough seas make it hazardous.

odm-m9skky.name: Thousand Steps (16)
highlights: Steep drop-off from 9 m

odm-mdiggk.name: Snake Bay
highlights: Many moray eels
Jacks chasing bait balls, creole wrasse, rays, turtles
hazards: Steep, slippery slope at the entry by the pier
odm-mdiggk.summary: Busy reef off a small pier on the west coast where the drop-off starts around 9 m and falls to about 40 m. Known for moray eels and heavy fish traffic including jacks, rays and turtles.
sources: Bluewater Dive Travel (Scuba Lodge & Ocean Suites)

odm-mdu6m8.name: Kisima Mungu (Nomads)
highlights: Walls, overhangs and sea fans
Trevally, barracuda, eagle rays

odm-mez7ia.name: Baxter’s Reef
hazards: Outer reef is more exposed to swell and wind

odm-mfzns3.name: HMNZS Canterbury (Wreck)
odm-mfzns3.summary: Former navy frigate scuttled in 2007 as an artificial reef near Cape Brett. She sits upright with the superstructure at roughly 12-14 m and the bow and stern on sand at 32-38 m, so most divers explore the upper decks; interior access is for experienced wreck divers.

odm-mg6pfp.name: Flat Rock - Turtle Cave
highlights: Grey nurse sharks in winter
Batfish schools, barracuda and turtles
Eagle ray fevers and humpback whales in winter

odm-mk24wj.name: Batu Ringit
highlights: Rubble slope with rare macro critters

odm-mkqnp7.name: Addu Manta Point
highlights: Reef mantas, up to 30 on one dive

odm-mlf81p.name: Jungle
highlights: Dense corals; wall running around north side

odm-mnljsp.name: Windmill Shallows
highlights: Sloped reef with drop-off, gorgonians, anchors and sharks

odm-moy4h9.name: Mama Viña (Wreck)
odm-moy4h9.depthNote: Deck about 15 m, deepest parts about 28 m
highlights: Groupers, barracuda and turtles
Fast coral growth on the artificial reef
odm-moy4h9.summary: A scuttled vessel off Playa del Carmen lying across the current, with its deck near 15 m and deepest parts near 28 m. Corals have grown quickly and groupers, barracuda and turtles visit.

odm-mp98lo.name: Antilla (Wreck)
highlights: Largest shipwreck in the Caribbean
Bow and stern intact with coral and sponge growth
hazards: Old, unstable wreck; penetration not advised
odm-mp98lo.summary: German freighter scuttled by its own crew in 1940, resting on sand in about 17 m off Palm Beach. Bow and stern are fairly intact and covered in coral and sponges; the wreck is too fragile to enter.

odm-mpzfzz.name: Lighthouse Wall
odm-mpzfzz.mooring: Mooring buoy; mooring pin at 64 ft
highlights: Rocky points and sand channels down the wall
Star corals in horizontal plates at depth

odm-mrh0xr.name: Carl’s Hill (V)
highlights: Coral wall
Seahorses
Underwater photography

odm-mt5owc.name: Kinasi Wall
highlights: Giant clams, large groupers, Napoleon wrasse, hawksbill turtles
odm-mt5owc.summary: A sheltered bank reef about 800 m long that slopes steeply rather than dropping sheer. Best at slack water or a gentle incoming tide, with groupers, giant clams and hawksbill turtles among the corals.

odm-mvsyus.name: Coral Gardens - Dominican Republic
highlights: Coral patches with sea fans and whips

odm-mxbx4d.name: HMAS Brisbane (Wreck)
odm-mxbx4d.depthNote: Upper decks about 15-16 m; seabed about 28 m
odm-mxbx4d.access: Queensland Parks permit or written authority required (booked through licensed operators)
odm-mxbx4d.penetration: Large openings cut in the hull; interior only for suitably trained divers
highlights: Eight-storey ex-navy destroyer
odm-mxbx4d.summary: A former navy destroyer deliberately sunk in 2005 off Mudjimba to serve as an artificial reef. The upper decks sit around 15 m with the seabed near 28 m, so exterior sections suit certified divers while the interior needs wreck training. A park permit is required.

odm-mxupd7.name: Olaf Sakatia
highlights: Small fish, leaf fish, nudibranchs

odm-myap9v.name: Bushrangers Bay
highlights: Grey nurse sharks

odm-n0h9g3.name: Turtle Reef / Macabuca - Grand Cayman
highlights: Mini-wall dropping to about 60 ft

odm-n0pe90.name: Pillarsteen
highlights: Fusilier schools over soft-coral slope
Caves and swim-throughs
Sharks and the odd turtle
hazards: Surge in southwest swell
odm-n0pe90.summary: A Komodo reef slope off Padar with boulders, caves and swim-throughs, carpeted in soft corals and patrolled by fusiliers, sharks and turtles. Useful when other sites run hard current, but can surge in swell.

odm-n0q7sc.name: Toho II, wreck
highlights: Fish-rich wreck inside the lagoon
hazards: Visibility often poor

odm-n34qxb.name: La Cathedrale
highlights: Large arches sheltering lobsters and spider crabs

odm-n3gs21.name: Mellow Yellow, Sodwana Bay
highlights: Shoals of yellow fish
Shrimps, nudibranchs and paperfish
odm-n3gs21.summary: Narrow reef strip at the southern end of Bikini, about 16-20 m deep and open to Open Water divers. Named for its yellow-fish schools, it also offers gullies, overhangs and plenty of shrimp and nudibranch macro subjects.

odm-n3yn07.name: Cenote El Pit
highlights: Descent past ancient dead trees
hazards: Hydrogen sulfide cloud near 30 m

odm-n4hdea.name: Orange Canyon
highlights: Two canyons lined with orange elephant-ear sponges
Gorgonians and sea fans
hazards: Prone to current; cannot always be dived
odm-n4hdea.summary: A spectacular wall site toward Northwest Point named for its big orange elephant-ear sponges, with two canyons split by a large coral head at about 60 ft. Current often makes it undiveable, so it is only done when conditions allow.

odm-n4t0w6.name: Raggedy Cay
highlights: Nurse sharks, turtles, morays and eagle rays

odm-n6yiw8.name: Mi Dushi (T)
highlights: Seahorses spotted at this location

odm-n7qdz1.name: Ilha do Frade
highlights: Turtles, corals and sponges

odm-n9itut.name: Papa Whisky, Tahiti
highlights: Whitetip, blacktip and grey reef sharks
Sea fans at 40 m
odm-n9itut.summary: An amphitheatre-shaped reef on the west coast away from any pass, known for pelagic sightings. Reef sharks and turtles patrol a small drop-off, with lively coral from around 20 m and a steeper wall deeper down for advanced divers.

odm-nbavyc.name: EN1
highlights: Honeycomb whiprays; crocodilefish, stonefish
hazards: Strong tidal current; slack high tide only

odm-ncb5d0.name: Kichafi
highlights: Healthy reef with extensive plate corals
odm-ncb5d0.summary: A healthy coral reef with broad plate-coral fields, suited to mixed-experience groups. A sandy area next to the reef makes it popular for training dives.

odm-ne42tn.name: Goat Island
odm-ne42tn.access: Marine reserve - no fishing or taking marine life
hazards: Unsafe in E/NE winds over 20 kn or swells over 1 m

odm-nee0ck.name: Blue Channel
highlights: Swim-throughs and a shallow "bowl of fish"
Silverside shoals mid-June to early August
odm-nee0ck.summary: A popular, easy channel dive on the West End that runs from the inner reef out to the coral ridge, with swim-throughs, a sandy shallow bowl full of fish and canyons that fill with silversides in summer. Suits both divers and snorkelers.

odm-nfdhek.name: Promenade Point
hazards: Boat and waterski traffic - use a dive flag

odm-ngl7iv.name: Rye Pier
odm-ngl7iv.access: Long walk from car park to purpose-built diver platform
highlights: Large stingrays and seahorses

odm-nl5z98.name: Ilha de Buzios - Costao dos Aquarios
highlights: Abundant fish, turtles and butterfly rays
hazards: Current; only in very calm seas

odm-nm62sc.name: Hands Off (M)
highlights: Cleaning stations
Drop-off with coral formations

odm-nnhxmz.name: Conception Rocks
odm-nnhxmz.access: Long boat ride (40+ min); not run by all operators
highlights: Common hawksbill turtles
hazards: Exposed to swell in the Southeast Monsoon

odm-noomi2.name: Jemeluk Wall
highlights: Barrel sponges, big sea fans, table coral
Nudibranchs along the wall
odm-noomi2.summary: A coral-covered wall that starts a short swim from the Jemeluk shoreline at Amed, reaching about 20 m. Calm, easy entry makes it a gentle first wall dive, with sponges, fans and table corals along the slope-to-wall transition.

odm-np813v.name: Batu Kelebit
highlights: Big pelagics, groupers and sharks
Bumphead parrotfish in the morning
odm-np813v.summary: A coral pinnacle with patch-reef shoulders off Tulamben that falls past 60 m, with most diving around 25 m. Currents are usually small, though when it runs groupers, sharks and other big fish turn up.

odm-nrsscs.name: Texas (The Point)
highlights: Giant barrel sponges and soft corals on a drift
Sargassum triggerfish and barracuda
hazards: Wall top is deep; hard to ascend against the current
odm-nrsscs.summary: A current-swept drift at the western tip of Roatán, where two ocean currents meet over huge barrel sponges and coral plains at around 90 ft. Conditions vary and it is recommended for advanced divers.

odm-nsm535.name: Batu Lima
highlights: Black and white tip reef sharks
Epaulette (walking) sharks on night dives
odm-nsm535.summary: Five adjacent rocks near Gam where reef sharks patrol and the reef is rich in fish and macro. Currents run from mild to strong, and the shallows come alive with walking sharks and invertebrates on night dives.

odm-nul5dj.name: THE COLOSSEUM Coral Coast Divers private shark sanctuary
odm-nul5dj.access: Open Water certification required; minimum 4 guests

odm-nve7tv.name: Tomajiko, Hiri Island
highlights: Sea fans and soft corals along the wall
Moray eels, nudibranchs, turtles, napoleon wrasse

odm-nvh4dd.name: The Maze
highlights: Maze-like channels with scorpionfish and lobster
Cave at 70 ft with lionfish

odm-nx25iu.name: Toyapakeh Wall
highlights: Wall swept by current with abundant fish
Mola mola possible
hazards: Constant current along the wall
odm-nx25iu.summary: A current-swept wall on the Toyapakeh strait off Nusa Penida, rated advanced. The constant flow brings plenty of tropical fish, healthy hard and soft corals and, with luck, mola mola.

odm-ny3tvx.name: Roca Partida
highlights: Giant Pacific mantas and schooling hammerheads
Whitetip reef sharks on the wall
hazards: Strong currents and surge around the pinnacle
odm-ny3tvx.summary: A remote guano-covered pinnacle in the Revillagigedo archipelago that drops into very deep water and is only dived from liveaboards. Currents can be strong, with one side usually sheltered; expect mantas, hammerheads, whale sharks and whitetips on the ledges.

odm-nya70b.name: Sandy Slope
highlights: Soft corals
odm-nya70b.summary: A wide shallow sandy flat at Menjangan Island that slopes away into deeper water with soft corals. Currents are minimal and the site suits beginners and buoyancy practice.

odm-nyv6fe.name: Sanur Beach
highlights: Sand with coral patches

odm-o0cx8v.name: Pura Ped
highlights: Turtles and big fish in the blue

odm-o1jb8q.name: Catalinas Island, Clásico
highlights: Fish schools, seasonal mantas, white-tip reef sharks

odm-o208bl.name: Caverna da Sapata
hazards: Currents change with the season
odm-o208bl.summary: A cave at the tip of Sapata with its entrance near 24 m and sunbeams cutting through, rated for experienced divers. Orange corals and sponges cover the walls, and current varies with season.

odm-o2327j.name: Crystal Palace, Rottnest Island
highlights: Caverns, swim-throughs and nudibranchs
odm-o2327j.summary: A shallow limestone cave and swim-through site off the south of Rottnest Island, suitable for most divers, with nudibranchs and plenty of fish in the caverns.

odm-o24h8d.name: The Ozone Shipwreck
highlights: Paddle wheels break the surface
odm-o24h8d.summary: Wreck of a 1886 paddle steamer scuttled as a breakwater off Indented Head in 1925, lying in about 3-4 m so the paddles show. An easy shallow dive or snorkel close to shore.

odm-o2hcyp.name: Cod Hole - Ribbon No 10 Reef - GBR
highlights: Habituated giant potato cod (up to 2 m)
odm-o2hcyp.summary: Ribbon Reef 10 coral garden at about 16-18 m, famous for the giant potato cod that approach divers. Reached only by multi-day liveaboard from Cairns.

odm-o3h2px.name: French Cap Pinnacle
hazards: Unprotected; dive only in calm seas

odm-o3yqxj.name: Sebayur Kecil Komodo
highlights: Bumphead parrotfish schools

odm-o5ssz0.name: Bari’s Reef (30)
highlights: #1 biodiversity in the Caribbean (300+ fish species)

odm-o6nrem.name: Batumulapan
highlights: Fan corals and giant sponges

odm-o7hans.name: Anau
odm-o7hans.access: Protected site; dive times may be limited
highlights: Manta rays at a cleaning station
odm-o7hans.summary: Bora Bora's best-known manta site, a calm lagoon channel on the east side with two coral formations and a sand alley between them. Mantas come to be cleaned here and are regularly seen; the site is protected and diving time can be restricted.

odm-o7j7wm.name: Twin Peaks, Saxon Reef
highlights: Two coral-covered peaks with a sandy reef wall nearby
hazards: Navigation can challenge novices; guide recommended

odm-o7jvu9.name: Popes Eye
odm-o7jvu9.access: Port Phillip Heads Marine National Park; boat access
highlights: Snorkel and shallow dive inside the ring
Australasian gannet colony on the rock
hazards: Outside wall needs more diving experience
odm-o7jvu9.summary: A man-made basalt ring in the Port Phillip Heads Marine National Park with a sheltered, 2 m deep centre and a wall dropping to about 12 m outside. The inside suits snorkellers and new divers, while the outside needs more experience.

odm-o90ivo.name: Astron, wreck
hazards: Strong current; dive in calm weather

odm-o96x2j.name: Packet Rock (Wreck)
highlights: Many barracuda around the rocks

odm-o9sjtx.name: Laje Dois Irmãos
odm-o9sjtx.summary: A submerged slab beside the Dois Irmãos hill, with rock, sand and plenty of fish at roughly 23-24 m. Reef sharks may pass, and with favourable current it turns into a drift.

odm-ocp3us.name: Epave Augustin Fresnel (Wreck)
odm-ocp3us.summary: A 53 m former lighthouse tender lying at roughly 27-33 m. Divers can swim along the hull and enter the wheelhouse and living spaces; Advanced Open Water level is required.

odm-od7t8z.name: KT Mawar
highlights: Massive propeller; giant frogfish
Soft pink corals on the wreck

odm-ofy6zu.name: Star Gerren
odm-ofy6zu.summary: German coaster sunk in 2000 off Palm Beach in roughly 14-21 m. Holes were cut in the hull so divers can enter and exit the wreck; reached by boat and rated intermediate.

odm-omkwux.name: Spooky Channel
highlights: Narrow channel with light filtering from above
Swim-throughs, lobster and starfish
odm-omkwux.summary: A channel through the barrier reef linking the lagoon with the outer reef, entered through a small opening that widens into a cavernous gorge to about 90 ft. Light filters down from above, making it an atmospheric dive for photographers.

odm-onem9e.name: Hole in the Corner
highlights: Excellent visibility in calm weather
hazards: Exposed to Atlantic swell; dived less often

odm-oo4t1k.name: La Petite Sirène
highlights: Turtles, green morays and platax

odm-ooe1lv.name: SAIL ROCK - GMI
highlights: Weed-covered boulders with crayfish
hazards: Exposed to swell and strong winds

odm-oq58xy.name: MKVI
highlights: Ledge running east-west makes navigation easy
Anemones, clownfish and Christmas tree worms
Mini cave with wobbegongs and slipper lobsters

odm-or7svt.name: Putahataha Island
highlights: Underwater cavern about 5 m wide at entrance
Kelpy rocky reef circumnavigation

odm-ot5oqj.name: Tugboat
odm-ot5oqj.summary: A small tugboat wreck resting upright in shallow water just off the Caracas Bay shore on Curacao. Easy to reach from the beach, popular with snorkelers and divers, and a good night-dive spot.

odm-otnxdi.name: East Chute
highlights: Deep sandy valley cutting the wall
Storm-flattened Cayman Mariner tug wreck
Green tube and orange elephant-ear sponges

odm-oxxlfi.name: Les Grottes du Portail
highlights: Overhangs and lava tunnels about 100 m long

odm-oydkpv.name: USAT Liberty Wreck
odm-oydkpv.summary: Cargo ship wrecked off Tulamben, lying a short swim from the black-sand beach with its top about 5 m down and the stern reaching roughly 30 m. Easy shore entry and plenty of fish life make it Bali's classic wreck dive.

odm-oz5j2f.name: Shane’s
highlights: Macro life: flying gurnards, frogfish, scorpionfish
odm-oz5j2f.summary: A sand-and-coral reef off northern Zanzibar prized for macro photography, with frogfish, gurnards and scorpionfish. Depths stay moderate, so it works for newer divers.

odm-p19pv4.name: Shark Bank
highlights: Snapper, jack and batfish schools; reef sharks
House-sized granite boulders and arches
hazards: Current can be punishing
odm-p19pv4.summary: An offshore granite seamount about 8 km from Mahé, rising from deep water to roughly 18 m. Big schools, turtles and reef sharks gather around boulders and arches; currents range from glassy to strong, so it suits advanced divers.

odm-p3mcx9.name: Flagstaff
highlights: Grey nurse sharks visit in winter
Rays on sand, nudibranchs in weed gardens

odm-p5eqac.name: Trinity Caves
highlights: Three long swim-throughs exiting onto the wall
Moray eels and nudibranchs in side chambers
odm-p5eqac.summary: A West Wall favourite where three long swim-throughs wind through the reef and emerge on the wall around 80 ft. The dive tops out near 100 ft and finishes on the wall top, with sponges, gorgonians, crustaceans and moray eels along the way.

odm-p5qkpt.name: AUT Millennium Centre
odm-p5qkpt.reason: Public swimming pool used for confined-water training sessions

odm-pbc3nu.name: Amity Point
highlights: Wobbegongs, schooling fish, occasional dolphin
hazards: Fishing lines and boat traffic
Very tidal; dive about an hour before high tide
Stonefish on the bottom

odm-pc39s3.name: Coral Gardens
highlights: Dense coral bommies, high fish diversity, good for photography
odm-pc39s3.summary: A broad area of coral outcrops behind the Kinasi and Chole walls, shallow enough for bright light and clear water. It is a favourite for photography and is often used as the easy final stage of a wall dive.

odm-pcm5sm.name: Srikandi Speedboat (Wreck)
highlights: Intact speedboat wreck

odm-pdjwy0.name: Four Buoy, Sodwana Bay
highlights: Overhang cleaning station with honeycomb morays
Swim-throughs around a sand patch

odm-pehu3s.name: Rottnest Island
odm-pehu3s.reason: A whole 19 km2 island with dozens of separate dive sites

odm-pew820.name: Tiki
highlights: Grey reef sharks and lemon sharks
Underwater sculptures by a local artist
odm-pew820.summary: An outer-reef dive on Moorea's northwest coast, near the pass and the oceanic slope. Grey and lemon sharks gather around a submerged tiki statue and sculptures. Calm, clear water and gentle current make it accessible, though it is a short boat ride out.

odm-pie5k2.name: Cap Salomon
odm-pie5k2.depthNote: Reef slopes to about 30-40 m per guides
highlights: Rocky blocks and coral heads; turtles, parrotfish

odm-pj2jcz.name: Cathedral
highlights: Ragged-tooth sharks in season
Crater-like amphitheatre with archway and swim-through
odm-pj2jcz.summary: Amphitheatre-shaped rock formation on the outer shoal, reached by a front archway, a roof opening or a side swim-through. It sits near 27 m, so it suits experienced divers, and ragged-tooth sharks often patrol it.

odm-pjexlr.name: Coral Garden, Menjangan
highlights: Hard and soft coral, big fans, reef fish
odm-pjexlr.summary: A shallow, calm coral garden on Menjangan, suitable for beginners and snorkellers. Hard and soft coral colonies, big fans and plenty of reef fish.

odm-pkrjya.name: Santa Rosa Wall
highlights: Spotted eagle rays
Barracudas, turtles and giant sponges
hazards: Strong, unpredictable drift current
odm-pkrjya.summary: Cozumel's classic wall drift, dropping well past recreational depths. Eagle rays, barracuda and big sponges are the draw, and the steady current calls for solid buoyancy and air management.

odm-pl77wq.name: Le Nahoon
odm-pl77wq.penetration: Deck, holds and cabins can be visited
highlights: Intact three-masted ship sunk as an artificial reef
odm-pl77wq.summary: A deliberately sunk sailing ship standing upright on sand off Les Anses-d'Arlet, a flagship wreck dive for Martinique. Deck, holds and cabins are in good shape and covered in colourful growth; a certified deeper-diving level and some current are to be expected.

odm-pplaug.name: Tres Cocos Canyons
highlights: Sea turtles during mating season
Deep, narrow canyons cutting across the reef

odm-pqyql0.name: Hong Kong
highlights: Turtles and tube-sponge skyline

odm-prcp5b.name: Cenote Chikin Ha
highlights: Two cavern lines past rock formations
hazards: Halocline on the cavern lines

odm-ps4trz.name: Gili Biaha, Candidasa
highlights: Shark cave with resting reef sharks
Pelagics and seasonal mola mola
hazards: Surge and unpredictable up and down currents
odm-ps4trz.summary: An island off Padang Bai and Candidasa with swim-throughs, sharks and pelagics. Strong, unpredictable currents and surge make it a site for experienced divers with good buoyancy.

odm-psp771.name: Colombia Deep
highlights: Pinnacles and coral formations
Nurse sharks under ledges
hazards: Strong currents possible
odm-psp771.summary: A deep wall at Cozumel's south end with pinnacles and rich coral. Nurse sharks rest under ledges, and currents can be strong, so it is best left to experienced divers.

odm-pw9xwu.name: Hydravion et Goelett
odm-pw9xwu.penetration: The Catalina seaplane can be entered
highlights: Catalina seaplane wreck, schooner and a third boat

odm-pxbwwa.name: Peters Place
highlights: Big groupers, creole wrasse and dog snapper
Free-swimming morays and eagle rays

odm-pzxov9.name: Klein Curaçao
highlights: Stunning, healthy coral reef
Good chance of turtles
hazards: Strong current in places; dive in calm weather
odm-pzxov9.summary: Uninhabited island about 10 km off the south coast, reached by boat day trip. The reef is in excellent condition with turtles, but some areas have strong current, so it suits experienced divers in calm weather.
sources: Bluewater Dive Travel (Scuba Lodge & Ocean Suites)

odm-q0vowe.name: Cenote Chac Mool
odm-q0vowe.access: Just south of Puerto Aventuras; cave-certified divers for the long cave system
highlights: Air dome under a partly collapsed ceiling
hazards: Sunken branches and trunks at the entrance

odm-q275ju.name: La Vallée blanche, Tahiti
odm-q275ju.depthNote: Around 20 m typical; deeper (40 m) for experienced divers
highlights: Several shark species incl. blacktip, lemon
Good drift dive along a white-sand strip
odm-q275ju.summary: Tahiti's best-known shark dive, just off the airport reef on the northwest coast. Currents carry divers past grey, blacktip, whitetip and lemon sharks, plus jacks and barracuda, over a pale sand channel. A drift dive best suited to divers with some experience.

odm-q3z86d.name: Lighthouse Reef - Grenada
highlights: Large fish, rays and sharks

odm-q54ks6.name: Cenote Dream Gate
odm-q54ks6.access: Reached by a dirt road through the jungle
highlights: Stalactites and tree roots to the water
hazards: Tight spaces demand good buoyancy

odm-q6k903.name: Wrong Entry
highlights: Drop-off wall with overhangs

odm-q7bpxl.name: Bat Cave
highlights: 200 m cave ending in open chamber with bats

odm-q7no2l.name: Jardin del Eden Cenote (Ponderosa)
odm-q7no2l.access: Large open pool south of Playa del Carmen, shared with snorkelers
highlights: Mayan gobies and tunnel-like cavern

odm-q8en5g.name: Five Mile Bay
hazards: Some silt on the drop-off
sources: Scubago (NZ Dive School / Dive Whakatane listings)

odm-q9qgu7.name: Mellow Yellow
highlights: Yellow soft corals cover the current-facing side
Thick schools of anthias and crimson sea fans
odm-q9qgu7.summary: A Bligh Water pinnacle named for the yellow soft corals that smother its current-facing side. Anthias swarm around the rock and sea fans add colour, so it is best dived with some water movement.

odm-qan8ns.name: Something Special (32)
hazards: Limited, sometimes strong current

odm-qbcmhl.name: Palmitas
highlights: Eagle rays, mottled moray eels, butterfly fish
Small coral formations on sand

odm-qcjnla.name: POINTE AUX FOUS
highlights: Coral strip below the cliff, very rich coral fauna

odm-qdluhw.name: Airplanes (Wreck)
highlights: Two sunken airliners: an intact YS-11 and a broken-up Convair
odm-qdluhw.summary: Two airliners, a YS-11 and a Convair, deliberately sunk on sand south of Renaissance Island at roughly 15-26 m. The YS-11 is largely intact and the planes can be partly penetrated.

odm-qglmyr.name: Le jardin des kiosques
highlights: Angelfish and groupers; dolphins often pass
odm-qglmyr.summary: A coral plateau off Saint-Leu cut by faults, arches and small caves between about 3 and 18 m. Suited to beginners and experienced divers alike, with angelfish and groupers on the reef and dolphins sometimes passing.

odm-qkgonx.name: Red Slave (60)
hazards: Strong currents

odm-ql33uq.name: Seahorse Bay
highlights: Seahorses, hairy frogfish, flamboyant cuttlefish
Popular night dive
odm-ql33uq.summary: A black-sand muck site on the Lombok side of the Gilis, good for macro photographers. Seahorses, hairy frogfish and flamboyant cuttlefish turn up, and it comes alive at dusk for night dives.

odm-qm7gg2.name: Banc 06
highlights: Shoals of fish over a shallow plateau
Big moray; occasional manta or eagle ray

odm-qmjree.name: Pink Beach Komodo
highlights: Pygmy seahorses on sea fans
Hawksbill turtles feeding on sponges
odm-qmjree.summary: A calm, sheltered coral slope on Komodo's coast, shallow and gentle enough for newly certified divers. It makes a relaxed break between Komodo's current-swept dives, with good macro life and turtles.

odm-qmyylt.name: Tori’s Reef (52)
highlights: 70-meter sandy flat
Salt pond outlet channel

odm-qr1ved.name: Fingers
highlights: Boxer shrimp, leaf fish, nudibranchs, frogfish

odm-qtgep7.name: Banc des Fusiliers
odm-qtgep7.access: About 10 km behind Nosy Sakatia; boat only
highlights: Macro life plus snapper, grouper, barracuda schools

odm-qujo9q.name: Friwen Wall, Raja Ampat
highlights: Many nudibranch species and macro life
Whip corals, gorgonians, sponges on the wall
Pygmy seahorses, blacktip sharks, fusiliers
odm-qujo9q.summary: A coral-covered wall in the Dampier Strait with small caves and overhangs, mild to medium current and suitable for all levels. Known for macro life such as nudibranchs and pygmy seahorses.

odm-qwqf0f.name: Blue Magic
highlights: Reef and oceanic mantas at cleaning stations
Sharks, dog-toothed tuna, giant trevally
hazards: Strong current may need reef hooking
odm-qwqf0f.summary: A pelagic hotspot off Mansuar: a reef top at 7-8 m sloping to 25-30 m. Mantas visit cleaning stations and sharks, tuna and trevally pass through. Current is medium to strong.

odm-qxwl7v.name: Tatawa Besar
highlights: Soft corals, turtles and swim-throughs

odm-qzlnah.name: Calhaus
highlights: U-shaped tunnel with an arch
hazards: Current and surge at the tunnel entrance

odm-qzpqfh.name: Henley on Klip - Bass Lake
highlights: Sunken car, bus and helicopter
Spring-fed training lake
odm-qzpqfh.summary: Spring-fed flooded mine lake south of Johannesburg, shelving from a walk-in slope to about 22-23 m. It is a mainstay training venue with sunken vehicles to visit, though visibility is often only a few metres.

odm-r0t2qz.name: Blue Bay Garden
highlights: Box crabs, octopus and baby brain and star corals
Gorgonians and cleaning stations on the slope
odm-r0t2qz.summary: Shore dive from Blue Bay Beach over a coral slope that begins at about 5 m and drops gently to roughly 50 m. Known for small critters such as box crabs and octopus, plus cleaning stations.
sources: Bluewater Dive Travel (Scuba Lodge & Ocean Suites)

odm-r2ga9f.name: Nine Mile Reef
highlights: Grey nurse sharks in winter, leopard sharks in summer
Wobbegongs year-round; bull sharks drop in
hazards: Strong current, up to about three knots
Often a drift dive with blue-water safety stops
odm-r2ga9f.summary: An offshore reef off Tweed Heads with a rocky ridge, ledges and bommies from about 10 m to 30 m. It is a shark site, with grey nurse sharks in winter and wobbegongs all year, but strong current and the need for calm seas make it for experienced divers.

odm-r5zlib.name: Boboss lalina
highlights: Macro, crocodilefish, scorpionfish, stonefish

odm-r6dqy8.name: Los Mogotes
highlights: Schooling tarpon and circling reef sharks

odm-r6t59f.name: Cap la Houssaye
highlights: Cannon at 5 m, turtle seagrass, caves with lobsters
odm-r6t59f.summary: A shallow marine-reserve site at the mouth of Saint-Paul bay, 2-18 m deep, with small caves, rock "patates" and a seagrass bed where turtles feed. Open to all levels and a popular first-dive and macro-life site.

odm-r7hped.name: Jack Iron Point, Carriacou
highlights: Lobsters, octopus, eels and sharks

odm-r82tnc.name: Pontal do Norte
highlights: Large submerged rock with big fish

odm-rbc6lv.name: Dragon Bay
highlights: Sand channels, coral fingers, sponges, lobsters and eels

odm-rbuddo.name: Wahoo
highlights: Reef sharks, moray eels, turtles; plankton draws whale sharks
hazards: Strong currents on an exposed seamount
odm-rbuddo.summary: An exposed offshore rock in Coiba National Park known for strong current and pelagic action. Reef sharks, morays and turtles gather along steep faces, and plankton can pull in bigger visitors; advanced divers only.

odm-rccztl.name: Bare Island East
odm-rccztl.access: Bare Island precinct closed for bridge restoration from 24 Aug 2026; reopening expected late 2027
hazards: Surge around the point; tricky in southerly swell
odm-rccztl.summary: The eastern face of Bare Island in Botany Bay, entered from the south-east point and slippery to exit, so it suits divers who know the site. Max depth is about 12 m with soft corals and macro life; southerly swell makes it tricky. The precinct is currently closed.

odm-rcoq14.name: L' Aquarium, Tahiti
highlights: Cessna plane and two small boat wrecks
odm-rcoq14.summary: A sheltered lagoon dive off Faa'a built around a small plane wreck and two boats. Shallow and nearly current-free, it is a go-to spot for training dives and first-timers, with lionfish and plenty of reef fish around the wrecks.

odm-rcylum.name: Craters Edge
highlights: Jacks, tuna and cero hunting baitfish; giant barracuda
odm-rcylum.summary: A pinnacle at the end of a volcanic ridge northwest of Scotts Head Pinnacle that can be circled in one dive. Pelagic hunters work schools of baitfish beside a wall of barrel sponges.

odm-rcz97f.name: Kelly’s Caverns
odm-rcz97f.mooring: Mooring buoy; mooring pin at 31 ft
highlights: Canyons and tunnels under the boat
Macro life on rubble field at 45-50 ft

odm-rf10xu.name: Haji
highlights: Submerged coral ridge, crocodilefish, nudibranchs

odm-rg2x9v.name: Pillar Coral
highlights: Coral pillar rising from the blue
Shallow swim-through cavern beside the mooring

odm-rg88gy.name: Barracuda Point, Carriacou
highlights: Sloping black coral reef with turtles and sharks

odm-rgj8cc.name: Old Issac’s
odm-rgj8cc.mooring: Mooring buoy; mooring pin at 29 ft
highlights: Ledge from 25 to 50 ft with rubble bottom
Yellow-headed jawfish and pike blennies
Coral outplanting site at eastern edge

odm-rjvf7w.name: Wakatobi House Reef
odm-rjvf7w.depthNote: Crest ~2 m; wall past 40 m (Wakatobi) to 70+ m (DIVER)
highlights: Wall with overhangs, turtles, hard and soft corals
Shallow macro: frogfish, pipefish, stonefish
odm-rjvf7w.summary: A shore-accessible fringing reef in front of the Wakatobi resort: shallow coral flats about 70 m wide, then a wall falling past 40 m. Mild currents along the slope make drift dives easy, and critters fill the shallows.

odm-rmjtbf.name: Nurses Quarters
highlights: Grey nurse sharks resting in the cave

odm-ro3ng5.name: Hogwarts / Outback
highlights: Very large resident green turtle
Frogfish, leaf fish, nudibranchs
hazards: Odd currents; negative entry needed
odm-ro3ng5.summary: A northern wall dive that starts on a pinnacle, with swim-throughs, overhangs and two cleaning stations for mantas. Currents can be tricky, so a negative entry is used.

odm-roej1n.name: SS Maori, wreck
odm-roej1n.depthNote: Top of engine about 6 m; deepest wreckage 21 m near the bow
hazards: Strong surge and ragged wreckage
Cold water

odm-rotsc5.name: La Source, Tahiti
highlights: Green and hawksbill turtles
Freshwater spring emerging at about 8 m
