odm-rotsc5.summary: A gentle west-coast reef dive off Puna'auia, popular for turtle sightings and a freshwater spring bubbling up from the seabed. Shallow, current-free and clear, so it suits newer divers, with deeper sections for experienced ones.

odm-rrjx30.name: Canyon
highlights: Coral growing on old lava flows, colourful fish
odm-rrjx30.summary: A reef of old lava channels off Saint-Gilles-les-Bains, dived between the surface and about 20 m. Coral has colonised the lava flows, and the site is open to all certification levels.

odm-rt2fk3.name: Car Pile - Marie Pampoen (Wreck)
highlights: Lionfish hiding in the metal scrap
hazards: Debris continues well below 40 m
odm-rt2fk3.summary: Artificial reef of sunken cars, beams and a small barge off Marie Pampoen. The debris starts around 15 m and keeps dropping well below 40 m, so it is a deep or technical dive.

odm-rtoxod.name: Maharani
highlights: Coral plateau at 6 m, faults and caves over white sand
odm-rtoxod.summary: A shallow site off Boucan Canot beach, 3-15 m deep, with a coral plateau at about 6 m and fissures and caves above white sand. Suitable for every level and for introductory dives.

odm-ru9kx4.name: White Slave
hazards: Moderate to strong current

odm-rwk52x.name: Dr. Grooms Garden
highlights: Corals, gorgonians, eels and sharks

odm-rxj6pm.name: Corporal Meiss (37)
highlights: Natural amphitheater at 25 meter depth

odm-rxxjas.name: Cenote Zapote (Hells Bells)
highlights: Hells Bells bell-shaped formations
Sulfide cloud and a 4500-year-old tree
Halocline
odm-rxxjas.summary: A deep sinkhole in the Ruta de los Cenotes known for its Hells Bells, bell-shaped formations hanging below a hydrogen sulfide cloud. Guided dives go to about 30 m through clear water with a halocline, so good buoyancy matters.

odm-rz4m8e.name: Deep Blue, Carriacou
highlights: Coral wall with drop-off, sharks and big fish
hazards: Depth and strong currents

odm-rzixho.name: Pablo’s Place
highlights: Dense soft corals on a vertical wall
Barrel sponges and large coral columns
odm-rzixho.summary: A vertical wall just around the northern tip of West End, noted for dense soft corals, barrel sponges and big coral columns. Conditions swing with weather and current, from a calm drift to a stronger one, so it is rated for advanced divers.

odm-rzove1.name: Taket Malang
highlights: Barrel sponges, bommies and sea fans on the plateau
odm-rzove1.summary: A seamount-style dive north of the Gilis with a plateau at about 10-12 m covered in barrel sponges and sea fans, dropping to 40 m between pinnacles and canyons. Turtles are the star attraction.

odm-s019h6.name: Magic Wall
highlights: Macro life: many nudibranch species
Moray eels draped over sponges and kelp

odm-s0jhoy.name: Butcher’s Bank
highlights: Pipefish, flounder, tube anemones on sand
Turtles and rays
odm-s0jhoy.summary: A relaxed sand-and-coral-platform dive on the West End that rewards slow, close-up looking. Expect pipefish, flounder and tube anemones on the sand, plus turtles and rays near the coral formations.

odm-s4k62e.name: Aldebaran Wreck
highlights: Morays, lionfish, sweetlips, batfish
hazards: Strong currents

odm-s586n0.name: El Canal - Acapulco
highlights: Schools of fish among rock formations

odm-s5ni7r.name: L’Ilot
highlights: Granite boulders with morays and lionfish

odm-s7tsqu.name: Julian Rocks - Hugos Trench
highlights: Macro life, wobbegongs and turtles
hazards: Trench swim-through only in perfect conditions
odm-s7tsqu.summary: A trench between sheer walls at Julian Rocks, about 12-18 m deep, good for macro life and wobbegongs. Swimming through it is only attempted when conditions are right.

odm-sahdzj.name: SS Yongala Wreck
odm-sahdzj.summary: The 1911 steamer Yongala lies on a sandy seabed about 30 m deep off Townsville, its upper hull near 16 m. The superstructure is gone but the hull is intact and heavily colonised by marine life.

odm-savpub.name: North Sands
highlights: Round ribbontail rays on the sand patch
Guitar sharks in summer
odm-savpub.summary: A large sand patch on the northern part of Aliwal Shoal ringed by reef. Reaching about 17 m, it is a place to look for ribbontail rays buried in the sand, summer guitar sharks, and old shark teeth lying among the shells.

odm-sc9zmm.name: Snake Reef, Mauritius
highlights: Scorpionfish, morays, lionfish and stonefish
Prime macro photography site
odm-sc9zmm.summary: A boulder reef on sand at the north end of Flic en Flac, around 25 m. Famed for scorpionfish, morays and other critters, so it is a photographers' favourite; operators prefer Nitrox and little current.

odm-se3mg9.name: Forest (N)
highlights: Black coral formations
Nurse sharks near cave at 30 m

odm-set79c.name: Playa Manzaliña
highlights: Vibrant corals, tropical fish and occasional seahorses

odm-sf8l6t.name: Koi island
highlights: Many sharks and fish schools

odm-sfc36u.name: Pink Beach (53)
highlights: Stingray sightings
Cleaning stations, eagle rays possible

odm-sgrfif.name: Middle Arch
highlights: Blue maomao and demoiselle schools
Air-pocket cave (Bernie's Cave)
hazards: Bay beside the arch drops to about 80 m

odm-si7jbj.name: Batu niti
highlights: Frogfish, ghost pipefish, flamboyant cuttlefish
Seafans and elephant ear sponges
odm-si7jbj.summary: A coral slope off Tulamben that blends into muck, producing frogfish, ghost pipefish, nudibranchs and cuttlefish. Most of the diving is in the 15-30 m range with small to variable current.

odm-siylcm.name: No Name (A)
highlights: Unique granite blocks of volcanic origin

odm-sjk4dg.name: Barracuda - Playa del Carmen
highlights: Giant morays, lobsters and crabs
Five finger-like reef outcrops
odm-sjk4dg.summary: A shallow Playa del Carmen reef shaped like a hand with five finger-like outcrops, close to Tortugas and often dived second. Look for large morays, lobsters and the barracuda it is named for.

odm-sky7x5.name: Sauwandarek
highlights: Fusilier schools beyond the jetty

odm-sm85fu.name: Atlantis
highlights: Reef
Sand bottom
Open ocean in one dive

odm-smeeg8.name: Half Moon Wall
highlights: Eagle rays, eels, turtles and healthy coral
Tunnel opening onto the wall at about 70 ft
odm-smeeg8.summary: A pretty West End wall right off Half Moon Bay, with a shallow reef top that drops past 150 ft. Healthy coral, eels, turtles and eagle rays are the draw, and open-water divers can enjoy the upper section.

odm-smqesc.name: Shacks Beach
highlights: Underwater cave and coral ecosystem
hazards: Only diveable on calm days

odm-snbzx0.name: Jack-A-Dan West, Carriacou
highlights: Shallow reef with eels and schools of fish
hazards: Potential strong currents

odm-sp9o5y.name: Fish Rock Cave
hazards: Pitch-black shaft section; torch essential
odm-sp9o5y.summary: A roughly 120-125 m ocean cave through Fish Rock off South West Rocks, between a deep entrance near 24 m and a shallow one near 12 m, with grey nurse sharks and big schools of fish.

odm-sqi4hu.name: La Piscine
highlights: Coral valleys with moray eels in cavities
odm-sqi4hu.summary: A sheltered, shallow stretch between the two Pigeon islets in the Cousteau Reserve, reaching about 25 m at most. Calm and clear, it is a favourite for first dives and discovery sessions, with iron coral and moray eels.

odm-sss193.name: Gravel Loader
highlights: Grey nurse sharks at the loader end
Giant cuttlefish and blue gropers
odm-sss193.summary: A shore dive from the boat ramp at Bass Point: a short surface swim to a disused loader jetty whose pylons shelter fish and invertebrates, with grey nurse sharks often passing and cuttlefish and gropers around.

odm-suuch3.name: Cenote Nicte Ha
highlights: Lily pad garden at the surface
hazards: Some current and tight maneuvering

odm-t030bt.name: Superior Producer (Wreck)
highlights: Upright cargo freighter; wheelhouse and holds to explore
hazards: No diving when a cruise ship is in port
Depth and strong currents
odm-t030bt.summary: Cargo freighter sunk in 1977 that sits upright near the Willemstad main pier, from about 17 m on the superstructure to 34 m on the sand. Strong currents make it an advanced dive, and it is closed whenever a cruise ship is in port.
sources: Bluewater Dive Travel (Scuba Lodge & Ocean Suites)

odm-t0ka4w.name: Cow Rock
highlights: Swim-throughs with lobsters and spotted drum

odm-t103n9.name: Menjangan - Pos 2
highlights: Gorgonian fans between 20 and 25 m
Triggerfish, fusiliers, trevally
hazards: Aggressive nesting triggerfish
odm-t103n9.summary: A craggy wall on Menjangan starting at around 12 m and falling to about 40 m, with big gorgonian fans at 20-25 m. Light to moderate current; watch for territorial triggerfish.

odm-t2pp2u.name: Coral Basket
highlights: Small shallow wall, deeper coral ridges

odm-t3bvru.name: Arashi (Wreck)
highlights: Airplane wreckage covered in coral
odm-t3bvru.summary: A beginner-friendly Aruba site where airplane wreckage lies around 35 feet down, overgrown with coral formations.

odm-t4wh2d.name: Sental
highlights: Big puffer fish, turtles and reef sharks
odm-t4wh2d.summary: Drift dive along Nusa Penida's north coast where the reef falls away to its richest coral and fish zone at 15-20 m. Turtles, reef sharks and large pufferfish are regular sightings.

odm-t7ejkj.name: Miralles, Wreck
highlights: Large interior spaces allow safe penetration to bridge
odm-t7ejkj.summary: The Antonio Miralles was sunk in March 2004 in Golfo Nuevo off Puerto Madryn as an artificial dive site. It lies about 20-30 m deep depending on tide, is rated medium to hard, and its roomy interior allows penetration.

odm-t94fn0.name: Broughton Island The Looking Glass
highlights: Swim-through gap with grey nurse sharks
hazards: Surge; undiveable in even moderate seas
odm-t94fn0.summary: A trench or arch cutting through the rock at Broughton Island, shallowest inside the gap, where grey nurse sharks gather. Dives only when seas are calm as surge builds quickly.

odm-tb91a5.name: Ulua Beach Park
highlights: Turtle cleaning station on the second reef
odm-tb91a5.summary: A beach-entry reef dive in Wailea, South Maui, used for scuba instruction thanks to gentle conditions and a gradual slope. Turtles visit a cleaning station on the second reef; swells can ruin visibility.

odm-tbcncs.name: Taharoa Domain (Kai Iwi Lakes)
highlights: Freshwater crayfish (koura) and trout

odm-tbkm6n.name: Big Rock, Mauritius
highlights: Eagle rays when a current runs
Resident turtle shelters here
odm-tbkm6n.summary: A drift-style dive along a steep wall that open water divers can handle. Its quality depends on a slight current, when eagle rays and other fish gather along the edge; without current it is only an average dive.

odm-tfj1el.name: Oswaldo’s Drop Off
highlights: Shallow terrace good for snorkeling

odm-tfxcq1.name: Manta Point , Makassar Reef
highlights: Likely manta encounters at bommie cleaning stations

odm-tgt8d9.name: Taurus e Virgo
odm-tgt8d9.summary: Two tugs sunk on one reef site 20 m apart off Recife (Taurus in 2006, Virgo in 2017), both resting around 25 m. A popular pair that can be dived together on a single dive.

odm-thwrq9.name: Whibbles Reef
highlights: Spotted eagle rays and schools of horse-eye jacks
Drop-off with brain coral, turtles and rays
odm-thwrq9.summary: A deep offshore reef south of St George's with a sloping sand wall and a drop-off, washed by current much of the time. Rated intermediate, it suits drift diving among eagle rays, jacks, barracuda and turtles.

odm-tiz29k.name: Pipeline
highlights: Old sewer pipe with soft corals and sponges
odm-tiz29k.summary: Nelson Bay night-dive favourite at the marina end: a rock entry then a roughly 250 m disused pipe running out into the bay, covered in macro life.

odm-tk8hjo.name: Coral Nursery
odm-tk8hjo.mooring: Dedicated mooring gives access to the nursery
highlights: Elkhorn coral restoration nursery (~800 fragments)

odm-tkdxxx.name: Siaba Kecil
highlights: Small caves with angelfish and batfish
Turtles and mandarin fish in shallow coral garden
hazards: Fast drift current
odm-tkdxxx.summary: Fast drift through canyons and small caves along a reef face in central Komodo, ending in a shallow hard-coral garden. The current can fly, so it suits experienced drift divers.

odm-tlviy1.name: Manta Bay
highlights: Manta rays year-round
Gullies and swim-throughs
hazards: Surge near the cliffs
odm-tlviy1.summary: Shallow coral and sand bay on Penida's south coast, closer and more sheltered than Manta Point. Smaller manta rays feed overhead through the year, and the bottom has gullies and swim-throughs; surge is the main nuisance.

odm-tn1a3u.name: Manta Ridge
highlights: Reef and oceanic mantas at cleaning stations
odm-tn1a3u.summary: A Raja Ampat ridge where reef and oceanic manta rays are cleaned and feed, mostly in 6-17 m. Strong, shifting currents mean divers hook on or hold position, so good buoyancy control matters.

odm-toe59b.name: Komati Springs
odm-toe59b.depthNote: Open water to 53 m; flooded mine cave system to about 186 m
odm-toe59b.access: Cave certification required for overhead areas; no permit needed

odm-tp5tww.name: les canyons de babodi
highlights: Large pelagics and several species of rays
odm-tp5tww.summary: Giant canyons on the north Caribbean coast of Martinique near Saint-Pierre, running from about 12-15 m down past 60 m. The upper canyons suit newer divers while the floor is for deep-certified divers.

odm-tryuql.name: Leonora’s Reef (X)
highlights: Double reef system with tunnels through coral formations

odm-tvjcot.name: Greta’s Place
highlights: Intact soft corals and colourful reef fish
odm-tvjcot.summary: A calm Una Una dive where the wall meets the sloping bottom, down to 30 m or more. Large hard and soft corals support plenty of colourful reef fish, and the neighbouring wall sometimes brings bigger visitors.

odm-twa17f.name: Passe de 3 Bassins
highlights: Many turtles

odm-twmydd.name: Antonio Lorenzo
highlights: Leopard moray, scorpionfish; ex-longliner sunk 1999
odm-twmydd.summary: A former longline fishing vessel scuttled in 1999 on sand off Saint-Leu, resting around 38 m. A deep wreck for advanced divers, with morays and scorpionfish living in the hull and the chance to look inside.

odm-txbukm.name: Wave Break Island
highlights: Small fish on the northern rock wall
Wobbegongs and grey nurse sharks
hazards: Tidal; best dived on and after high tide
odm-txbukm.summary: A man-made breakwater island inside the Gold Coast Seaway that shelters divers from ocean swell. Shallow and protected, it is a standard site for introductory dives and snorkelling, with plenty of small fish, wobbegongs and sometimes grey nurse sharks.

odm-tyk29j.name: Penguin Cove
highlights: Black coral trees
Huge crayfish in the cracks
hazards: Can be a little silty
odm-tyk29j.summary: An easy Milford Sound starter dive over a sloping sandy bottom, regarded as a beginner site. Black coral grows unusually shallow here, and large crayfish crowd the crevices, though silt can reduce visibility.

odm-u4vj7h.name: Tulamben Drop-Off
odm-u4vj7h.summary: A wall just a short swim from the Tulamben shore, beginning at about 3 m and dropping past 70 m. Divers usually stay on the shallower sponge- and gorgonian-covered upper face.

odm-u5ic8m.name: Long Caye Aquarium
highlights: Table-top formation and steep wall
Sea feathers and lace coral
odm-u5ic8m.summary: Wall at Long Caye on Lighthouse Reef with a table-top top and steep drop. An easy drift dive with high visibility, usually the third stop of a Blue Hole day trip.

odm-u6kq63.name: Carib Cargo (Wreck)
highlights: Stingrays, turtles and reef sharks around the wreck
hazards: Wreck is crumbling; penetration not advised
odm-u6kq63.summary: An upright inter-island cargo ship on sand at the edge of the Man of War Shoal Marine Park off Great Bay, in roughly 65-70 ft. Rays, turtles and reef sharks visit; the hull is deteriorating, so stay outside.

odm-u77wua.name: Makena Landing
highlights: Caves, arches, turtles and whitetip sharks

odm-u9tfdf.name: J4 Submarine Wreck
hazards: Surge on the shallow site

odm-ua255x.name: Bare Island West
odm-ua255x.access: Bare Island precinct closed for bridge restoration from 24 Aug 2026; reopening expected late 2027
highlights: Sheltered side, dived in southerly swell
odm-ua255x.summary: The western, sheltered side of Bare Island in Botany Bay, with an easy entry and a boat-ramp exit that suit beginners. Depths reach about 12 m, and it is the side to choose when southerly swell is running. The precinct is currently closed.

odm-uavx82.name: Black Coral Wall
odm-uavx82.depthNote: Black coral from about 25 ft; deep wall on the south side
highlights: Black coral at about 25 ft, unusually shallow
Macro subjects for photographers
odm-uavx82.summary: A south-side wall named for black coral growing unusually shallow, from around 25 ft, with one of the deeper drop-offs on that coast. The sandy reef top is full of juvenile fish and a favourite with macro photographers.

odm-ubje8f.name: Blue Devil Cave
highlights: Tame blue devilfish
Sydney pygmy pipehorse
odm-ubje8f.summary: A well-known Bass Point cave dive near The Gutter, famous for blue devilfish that are used to divers and for sightings of the tiny Sydney pygmy pipehorse.

odm-ubujmh.name: Chimney
highlights: Unusual chimney-like underwater structure

odm-ucnfnf.name: Kichwani
highlights: Schooling reef fish in the shallows, predators in the blue
odm-ucnfnf.summary: A steep coral bank on the Mnemba side, dived as a drift along the wall. Reef fish shoal in the shallow upper slope while bigger predators patrol the open water beyond the drop.

odm-ud1p7g.name: Tombant de Papeari
highlights: Gorgonians, chub and snapper schools, spadefish

odm-udeaxd.name: Mermaid’s Lair
highlights: Green moray eels, lionfish and nurse sharks

odm-uev7fe.name: Cenote Car Wash (Aktun Ha)
highlights: Open lily-pad basin
Room of Tears cave

odm-ui8f3h.name: Manta Point
highlights: Reliable manta ray encounters at cleaning stations
Turtles, eagle rays, bamboo sharks
hazards: Moderate to strong currents
odm-ui8f3h.summary: Makassar Reef in Komodo is a shallow drift over rubble where manta rays gather at cleaning stations, with the main action at roughly 6-18 m. Accessible to open-water divers with good buoyancy.

odm-uib62u.name: SAS Transvaal (Wreck)
odm-uib62u.summary: Former navy Loch-class frigate scuttled in Smitswinkel Bay in August 1978 to form an artificial reef. The wreck sits on sand at about 34 m with its main deck near 29 m.

odm-uk7l5s.name: Mur de corail/Coral Wall
highlights: Blacktip reef sharks and turtles along coral walls
odm-uk7l5s.summary: A sheltered coral-wall dive near Opunohu Bay, split into three sections so it can fill several tanks. Calm water and shallow-to-moderate depths make it comfortable for beginners, with reef sharks, turtles and morays along the walls.

odm-ukbbw2.name: Mr. Bud Wreck
highlights: Jawfish on surrounding sand flats
odm-ukbbw2.summary: A small cargo vessel about 75 ft long resting at around 60 ft on sand, with its cabin roof near 45 ft and bow wedged in the reef. A relaxed wreck dive for most certification levels with jawfish in the sand around it.

odm-utk73d.name: Manta Bommie
highlights: Manta ray cleaning station, November to April
Leopard sharks and guitarfish
hazards: Current and swell can make the dive challenging
odm-utk73d.summary: A group of rocky outcrops a short boat ride off Point Lookout where migrating manta rays visit shallow cleaning stations through the summer. Leopard sharks, rays and turtles also turn up. Depths are shallow, but current and swell can make it demanding.

odm-uubagz.name: Exmouth Navy Pier
odm-uubagz.access: Licensed local operator only; photo ID required; guided

odm-uv6xq3.name: Crossover
highlights: Sharks and fish schools along the wall

odm-uvj8p9.name: Mala Wharf
highlights: Green sea turtles, whitetip sharks, frogfish
hazards: Rip current in the bay when surf is up
odm-uvj8p9.summary: A shore dive around the collapsed remains of an old pier near Lahaina, Maui. Entry is a short wade over rough lava, and the pier remnants shelter turtles, frogfish and whitetip sharks.

odm-uvjxgi.name: Playa Forti
hazards: Car tires and fishing line debris on the seabed

odm-uvkrvv.name: Car Wrecks (Kokomo Beach)
highlights: Field of old car wrecks, with a small wreck just beyond at 45 m
hazards: Deep and far out; plan enough air for the return
odm-uvkrvv.summary: Car pile off Kokomo Beach: many old car wrecks lying roughly 30-50 m deep, with a small wreck just beyond. A long surface swim and depth mean you must plan air carefully.

odm-ux7u7k.name: La Diéppoise, wreck
highlights: Groupers, jacks, perch, nudibranchs on the wreck
odm-ux7u7k.summary: New Caledonia's best-known wreck, deliberately sunk in 1988 between the Boulari pass and Amédée islet. It rests around 26 m and has become a reef for groupers, jacks and nudibranchs.

odm-uzr2a0.name: Francisco Reef
highlights: Anthias and fusiliers from the start
odm-uzr2a0.summary: Easy reef near Biodiversity Resort, 3 to 25 m with little current. The dive starts on a shallow rock alive with anthias and fusiliers.

odm-v2dtgx.name: ÎLe Fourchue
highlights: Rays, barracudas and turtles
odm-v2dtgx.summary: Boat dive around Île Fourchue, a rocky islet northwest of St Barts, shelving to roughly 20 m and known for rays, barracudas and turtles.

odm-v2y1or.name: Divers Leap
odm-v2y1or.depthNote: Most sea life at 8-15 m along the wall edge
highlights: Possible drift dive along the reef
odm-v2y1or.summary: House reef in front of Jan Thiel Beach with easy entry from a small beach; a short shallow stretch leads to a drop-off at about 10 m, and conditions sometimes allow a drift dive.
sources: Bluewater Dive Travel (Scuba Lodge & Ocean Suites)

odm-v321kx.name: 1 / 4 Wreck (Stern Courier)
highlights: Cargo vessel sections on a coral bed with lobsters, eels, rays

odm-v35gpo.name: Pamir, wreck
highlights: Black coral, sea fans, frogfish and squid
odm-v35gpo.summary: A 165-170 ft freighter sunk as an artificial reef in 1985 off Barbados's west coast, resting upright in roughly 40-60 ft. Easy for all levels, with openings to peek inside and plenty of sponges, sea fans and fish.

odm-v3hat4.name: Moon Island
odm-v3hat4.depthNote: The Arch off the south-east side: archway about 17 m, sand about 20 m
highlights: Grey nurse shark visits in winter
The Arch: large boulders with an archway
sources: Michael McFadyen's Scuba Diving Web Site

odm-v4blus.name: Bird Rock
hazards: Surge on the fly-over
sources: Mudgee Dive and Travel (Scuba Haven info)

odm-v6ro3m.name: Chunnel
highlights: Ragged-tooth sharks patrolling the channel
Turtles, sand sharks and ribbontail rays
odm-v6ro3m.summary: A shark-traffic channel close to Raggies Cave on Aliwal Shoal, about 17 m at most. Ragged-tooth sharks pass through constantly, with turtles, sand sharks and rays on the neighbouring sand; coral is sparse because of current.

odm-v6xsbe.name: Casa Cenote
highlights: Mangrove roots overhead, fresh and salt water fish
odm-v6xsbe.summary: A shallow, calm dive along a mangrove-fringed channel that links the cenote to the sea near Tulum. Easy conditions suit beginners, with small fish among the roots and a cave line leading into the dark.

odm-v7lae4.name: Esmeralda Canyon
highlights: Nurse sharks at a long-running feeding site
Groupers, snappers, barracuda and moray eels in deep canyons
hazards: Deep canyons and swim-throughs suit experienced divers
odm-v7lae4.summary: Canyon dive off Ambergris Caye near the Shark Ray Alley area, with deep cuts and swim-throughs best for experienced divers. Nurse sharks, groupers, snappers and morays are the main sights.

odm-vcvvke.name: Manta Point Aliwal
highlights: Swim-through, gullies and rock caves
Leather coral; occasional manta rays

odm-vfgg0r.name: Black Rock
highlights: Lovely wall reached by a descent in clear blue water

odm-vfuigd.name: Mcgregor’s Bay
highlights: Leatherjackets, red moki, goatfish, baby snapper

odm-viijgd.name: Atnam
highlights: Canyon covered in gorgonians
Chance of pelagics, tuna, leopard sharks

odm-vj5eyn.name: Tortugas Reef
highlights: Hawksbill, green and loggerhead turtles
odm-vj5eyn.summary: A gently sloping reef off Playa del Carmen that is among the area's most popular boat dives. Turtles of three species are regularly seen, and a moderate current usually runs along the reef.

odm-vjo3ba.name: Opera House
highlights: Caverns lit by shafts of light
odm-vjo3ba.summary: A deep cave system on a limestone slope off Rottnest, with light shafts through the caverns, overhangs and occasional grey nurse sharks, reaching around 30 m.

odm-vjwek1.name: Batu Tiga
highlights: Giant trevally, barracuda, massive groupers

odm-vl1b69.name: Yenkoranu
highlights: Passing sharks; popular night dive

odm-vlqof5.name: Julian Rocks - Cod Hole
highlights: Grey nurse sharks, moray eels, wobbegongs
odm-vlqof5.summary: A swim-through cave at the northern end of Julian Rocks, sloping from about 15 to 21 m. It suits experienced divers and is known for grey nurse sharks.

odm-vmu5il.name: Punta Sur - Devil’s Throat
highlights: Coral cave descending through an overhead
Cathedral chamber with marine life
hazards: Strong currents and surf
Overhead environment needs buoyancy skill
odm-vmu5il.summary: Cozumel's southern tip site, where a coral cave drops through an overhead section. Currents and surface surf are strong, so it is advanced-only and needs sound buoyancy and gas management.

odm-vodl0q.name: Lean
odm-vodl0q.depthNote: Sandy slope at ~20 m, walls drop below 40 m
highlights: Series of walls south of the river mouth

odm-vr1zwk.name: Buyuk
highlights: Turtles, pufferfish and macro on sandy slope
Napoleon wrasse and barracuda in current
odm-vr1zwk.summary: A sloping, sandy coral reef on Nusa Penida's north coast, dotted with bommies and sponges. Usually gentle enough for easier dives, though stronger current brings big visitors such as Napoleon wrasse and barracuda.

odm-vr4jg0.name: Farikede
highlights: Silvertip, grey reef and thresher sharks

odm-vuifmn.name: HMS Proselyte
highlights: Cannons, anchors and ballast bars under coral growth
odm-vuifmn.summary: The scattered remains of a 1801 Royal Navy frigate on the Man of War Shoal just off Philipsburg. Cannons, anchors and ballast bars lie under heavy coral in about 20-55 ft; surge can be felt.

odm-vv12jt.name: Gerombong
highlights: Small decorated cavern at 13 m
Critter-rich rubble and macro
odm-vv12jt.summary: A gentle coral slope near Tulamben with a small decorated cavern around 13 m (bring a torch) and a rubble area rich in critters. Calm, with little current.

odm-vvg9ls.name: Bias Tugel / White Sand Beach
highlights: Green turtles, pygmy seahorses, nudibranchs
Macro life and schooling fish
odm-vvg9ls.summary: A coral plateau at 6-10 m dropping to 30 m or more on a white-sand bay near Padang Bai. Calm most days but currents can be unpredictable; turtles, nudibranchs and pygmy seahorses.

odm-vypg4d.name: Navarra
highlights: Fishing vessel sunk as an artificial reef in 1996

odm-w2h1ed.name: Instant Replay
highlights: Dense red and yellow soft coral wall
Nudibranchs and pygmy seahorses for macro
odm-w2h1ed.summary: A Rakiraki dive along a wall thick with red and yellow soft corals that sway in the current, with small macro life such as nudibranchs among the coral heads.

odm-w2m98f.name: River Taw Wreck, Saint Kitts
highlights: Upright freighter with turtles, stingrays, octopus, snapper

odm-w3te2u.name: Sandy Island Garden, Carriacou
highlights: Ridge reef with turtles, rays and seahorses

odm-w4fdqb.name: Aquarium de Cook
highlights: Coral heads, anemones, hawksbill turtles, eagle rays

odm-w6m7s2.name: La Baleine
highlights: Morays, barracuda and schools of bécune

odm-w97nby.name: Roches Merveilleuses
hazards: Moderate to strong currents on a drift dive

odm-w9tby5.name: Diamond Rock
hazards: Strong currents around Diamond Rock
sources: Saba Conservation Foundation (Saba National Marine Park)

odm-wagsf8.name: Sculpture Park
highlights: Sculptures acting as an artificial reef with corals and fish
odm-wagsf8.summary: Molinere Bay's underwater sculpture garden lies in shallow water of roughly 4-10 m. The figures now serve as an artificial reef, colonised by corals, sponges and fish, making an easy dive for beginners.

odm-waitdg.name: Castle Rock Komodo
highlights: Hunting grey, white-tip and black-tip reef sharks
Trevally, tuna, mackerel above the rock
hazards: Strong current, negative entry needed
odm-waitdg.summary: Submerged seamount in north Komodo topping out a few metres below the surface and falling to deep water. Current is strong, so divers drop in fast and often hook on while reef sharks and trevally hunt nearby; advanced divers only.

odm-wbxdda.name: Sunset Reef
highlights: Hard and soft corals with snapper and sweetlips
Turtles; occasional manta at the cleaning station
odm-wbxdda.summary: A gently sloping reef off the south-west of Gili Trawangan, suitable for all levels. Most of the interest lies around 10 m, with turtles, snapper and sweetlips, and the odd manta stopping at the cleaning station.

odm-week61.name: Aquarium
highlights: Reef fish, nudibranchs, turtles, stonefish
odm-week61.summary: A sheltered, fish-rich reef off Beau Vallon on Mahé's north tip with little or no current. It is the usual first dive for newly certified divers, with nudibranchs, turtles and scorpionfish among the rocks.

odm-wf0g5p.name: The Cauldron
highlights: Manta rays often seen
hazards: Shotgun channel current up to five knots
odm-wf0g5p.summary: Komodo's tidal drift through a rocky channel into a coral bowl, finishing over a coral garden. Currents are fierce and tide-dependent, so it is for experienced divers; reef sharks and mantas are the draw.

odm-wfrwm9.name: Lighthouse Bommie - Lady Elliot Island
odm-wfrwm9.mooring: Mooring line; descend and drift onto the bommies
highlights: Manta cleaning station
Turtle cleaning station nearby
odm-wfrwm9.summary: A group of small bommies off the west side of Lady Elliot Island, reached by a mooring line, famed for manta rays being cleaned by wrasse, with turtles also cleaned nearby.

odm-wgguee.name: Les Jardins de Salomon
highlights: Feather gorgonians and barrel sponges
odm-wgguee.summary: Gentle coral gardens below Cap Salomon near Grande Anse d'Arlet, with feather gorgonians and barrel sponges colouring slopes that run to about 25 m. A calm, easy boat dive suited to newer divers.

odm-whjar3.name: Little House on the Prairie
odm-whjar3.mooring: Mooring buoy; mooring pin at 29 ft
highlights: Interconnected tunnels under the boat
Star corals; coral spawning night dives

odm-wi7r27.name: Igloo
highlights: Sweetlips, octopus, ghost pipefish
Remains of an abandoned underwater habitat

odm-wkqen6.name: Manta Point, Sekar Kuning
highlights: Mantas with wingspans over three metres
hazards: Strong surge and waves on this exposed coast

odm-wl4sju.name: Citrus Ridge
highlights: Soft corals in orange and yellow hues
Bumphead parrotfish, barracuda, wobbegong
hazards: Intense current: do not swim into it
odm-wl4sju.summary: A pinnacle and ridge in Raja Ampat plastered in soft coral, with schools of bumphead parrotfish, barracuda and fusiliers. Currents are moderate to strong and the dive direction follows the flow.

odm-wl9wtn.name: Los Arcos - Playa del Carmen
highlights: Two arches

odm-wmglo1.name: HMAS Perth II
odm-wmglo1.summary: A guided-missile destroyer deliberately sunk in 2001 in King George Sound near Albany as a dive wreck. It sits upright on its keel, with the upper structure shallow and the seabed near 36 m, and an interpretive trail around it.

odm-wnxq3o.name: Yellow Wall Komodo
odm-wnxq3o.depthNote: Wall from 5 m down past 30 m; best life is shallow
highlights: Sleeping turtles and cat sharks
Featherstars and sea cucumbers on the wall
odm-wnxq3o.summary: A bright wall and shallow top reef in Komodo that starts at about 5 m and falls past 30 m, though the richest life is in the upper levels. Current is usually mild; look for turtles, catsharks and plenty of featherstars.

odm-wr9t9s.name: Mazarin
highlights: Small coral garden good for macro photography

odm-wrbvju.name: Brizare Rock, Mahé
highlights: Smaller sharks and barracuda
Colourful coral and fish
hazards: Strong currents

odm-wrndzo.name: Siaba Besar
highlights: Green turtles ('Turtle City')
Macro life on sandy patches
odm-wrndzo.summary: A sheltered bay in central Komodo National Park with coral bommies and sandy patches on a gentle slope. Calm and shallow, it is known for its resident turtles and is popular for first and check-out dives.

odm-wslbvx.name: Air Wall
highlights: Wall covered in corals and sponges
Turtles, cuttlefish, batfish
odm-wslbvx.summary: A sloping reef off Gili Air that steepens into a wall around 18 m, covered in coral and sponges. Turtles are frequent and conditions are usually manageable.

odm-wvdvt8.name: Laje de Santos - Portinho
highlights: Sea turtles; sheltered side

odm-ww1kds.name: Seaquest Deep
highlights: Roatan Marine Park coral nursery (coral trees)

odm-wyovcg.name: Cayman Brac
odm-wyovcg.reason: Whole island, not a single dive site

odm-wzzymt.name: Bikini
highlights: Pipefish and garden eels
Coachman school and small cave on Bikini Ledge
odm-wzzymt.summary: Macro-friendly 2 Mile Reef dive that drops onto a ledge near 20-22 m. Expect schools of coachman, a small cave, garden eels and pipefish, and it is rated for Advanced Open Water divers.

odm-x1zrqp.name: Boarfish Reef
highlights: Caves, overhangs and swim-throughs
Blue devilfish, crayfish and boarfish
odm-x1zrqp.summary: A colourful reef between Queenscliff and Point Lonsdale, an extension of the Lonsdale Wall. It runs from about 10 m down to 22-25 m over drop-offs, caves and swim-throughs, with blue devilfish, crayfish and boarfish.

odm-x2zqxf.name: Aquarius (46)
highlights: Double reef system

odm-x5aveo.name: Ginger Steps
highlights: Step-like ledges with some of the healthiest BVI corals

odm-x5v3je.name: Batu Bolong Komodo
highlights: Soft corals, reef sharks and Napoleon wrasse
hazards: Currents can change quickly

odm-x73gpg.name: Don Quickset
highlights: Canyon-like channel through the wall
Nurse sharks, southern stingrays, tarpon, turtles

odm-x772r1.name: Friwen garden
highlights: Fusilier schools hunted by trevally
Pygmy seahorses on a gorgonian at 20 m
odm-x772r1.summary: Shallow soft and hard coral reef beside Friwen Wall; current is usually mild but can pick up into an easy drift. Fusiliers gather where the current splits, and trevally and reef sharks often hunt them.

odm-x8ny5r.name: Cenote Taak Bi Ha
odm-x8ny5r.access: Narrow staircase into a dry cenote; tanks lowered
highlights: Dense rock formations, good for photography
hazards: Fragile formations easily damaged

odm-xa9h42.name: Catherine Hill Coal Loader
highlights: Pylons grown into a reef with fish and nudibranchs
Ship chains and remains of the SS Wallarah

odm-xakznz.name: Dream Wall
highlights: Large gorgonian fans from about 10 m
Fusiliers and anthias along the wall
hazards: Deeper stretches can pick up current unpredictably
odm-xakznz.summary: A vertical wall on the north coast of Menjangan next to Coral Garden, with large fans from about 10 m down. Moderate to strong current on the deeper parts makes it an advanced dive.

odm-xfra0q.name: L'arbre Mort
highlights: Colourful sponges with morays; macro subjects
odm-xfra0q.summary: A shallow plateau just before Cap Salomon, carpeted with brightly coloured sponges that hide morays and small macro life. Easy depths make it a good choice for beginners and underwater photographers.

odm-xhi90o.name: Mandy’s Eel Garden
highlights: Garden eels on the sand near the wall base
Barracuda, rays, octopus and turtles
odm-xhi90o.summary: A calm, shallow reef and sand slope just off West Bay that suits first-timers and students. Garden eels sway on the sand near the wall base, with moray eels, rays and turtles around the coral heads.

odm-xhqo3p.name: Lipah Bay, Bali
highlights: Turtles, coral blocks with colorful fish
odm-xhqo3p.summary: Calm shore dive at Amed: walk in from a sandy beach, swim to a slope and follow a ledge past coral blocks. Good for relaxed reef exploration and critter hunting, with turtles grazing along the bottom.

odm-xktu72.name: Grande Caye de Sainte-Luce
highlights: About 50 coral species on a 200 m reef
odm-xktu72.summary: A broad coral plateau off Sainte-Luce prized for coral diversity, with some fifty species recorded on a reef about 200 m long. Open to all levels and a popular spot for introductory dives.

odm-xp91rg.name: The Crack at Pulau Babi
odm-xp91rg.depthNote: Fissure itself at roughly 18-20 m per Neptune
highlights: Earthquake fissure in the reef
Sea fans, sponges and sea squirts
odm-xp91rg.summary: A reef on Pulau Babi split open by the 1992 Flores earthquake, leaving a fissure and small cave in the wall. Divers look down into the crack rather than enter it, over walls of sea fans and sponges.

odm-xq4p9e.name: Mushroom Forest & Blue Room
odm-xq4p9e.depthNote: Most life at 12-14 m (40-50 ft) in Mushroom Forest
highlights: Mushroom-shaped hard coral formations
Giant moray eels, porcupinefish, barracuda and lobster
odm-xq4p9e.summary: Famous west-coast boat dive over mushroom-shaped hard corals, with most life at 12-14 m among large star corals. Often combined with the nearby Blue Room cave.
sources: Bluewater Dive Travel (Scuba Lodge & Ocean Suites)

odm-xs9p8u.name: Protea Banks
odm-xs9p8u.access: Boat from Shelly Beach harbour; about 35 logged dives and Advanced Open Water expected
highlights: Hammerhead, bull, tiger and ragged-tooth sharks
Northern and Southern pinnacles with caves and drop-offs
hazards: Strong Agulhas Current; negative entry and blue-water ascent
odm-xs9p8u.summary: Offshore reef system about 7.5 km from Shelly Beach, made of two pinnacles, sand channels and drop-offs in the Agulhas Current. It is a deep, fast drift dive for experienced divers, known for hammerheads and other sharks.

odm-xsuiwg.name: Alcyone, Cocos Island
highlights: Hundreds of scalloped hammerheads at cleaning stations
hazards: Strong, sweeping currents; mooring line needed to descend
odm-xsuiwg.summary: An isolated seamount off the south coast of Cocos Island whose summit sits around 27 m, home to a hammerhead cleaning station. Strong current makes the mooring line essential, so it is a dive for experienced divers.

odm-xsxatd.name: Tanjung Jepun, Padang Bai, Bali
highlights: Blue-spotted stingrays, frogfish, cuttlefish
Artificial reef and small wreck at ~17 m
odm-xsxatd.summary: Gentle Padang Bai site used for open-water training: sand and rubble from about 5 m, then a slope down to an artificial reef and small wreck near 17 m. A good macro dive for stingrays, frogfish and cuttlefish.

odm-xt5j6j.name: La Jetée, Carriacou
highlights: Over 50 fish species incl. seahorses and eels

odm-xw4fcy.name: Cenote Dos Ojos
highlights: Stalactites, fossils and sunlit openings
hazards: Silty bottom in Baticueva needs buoyancy control

odm-xwscgp.name: Playa Jeremi
highlights: Pristine coral reefs

odm-xwznfg.name: Jardines de la Reina
odm-xwznfg.reason: An archipelago and national park, not a single dive site

odm-xy6xen.name: SD Point
highlights: Coral, schooling fish and turtles
odm-xy6xen.summary: Drift dive along a sloping shelf on Nusa Penida's north coast, with coral starting about 5 m and the main reef near 20 m. Current ranges from gentle to brisk and can reverse.

odm-xz5eol.name: Lighthouse Komodo
highlights: Table, whip and soft corals on a sloping reef
White-tip reef sharks
odm-xz5eol.summary: A drift-style reef off Gili Lawa Laut in northern Komodo, with two pinnacles on a sloping reef and table corals, whip corals and white-tip sharks. Operators rate it for more experienced divers.

odm-xzhwjt.name: Laje de Santos - Piscinas
highlights: Fish schools and turtles
hazards: Frequent currents at the west-southwest turn

odm-y1w1cy.name: Historic Dive Wreck Clan Mc William
highlights: Jaws swim-through, hawksbill turtle, coral growth
odm-y1w1cy.summary: A sheltered, upright wreck in Neiafu harbour, a short boat ride out. Calm, current-free and deep enough that most dives start near 28 m, it suits experienced divers and shows masts, winches, coral growth and a resident turtle.

odm-y3h3sa.name: Haï Siang, wreck
highlights: 49 m Taiwanese lobster boat scuttled in the 1980s
hazards: Long vertical descent without a line, drift

odm-y48zm9.name: Sandy Cove
odm-y48zm9.access: Within Table Mountain National Park marine protected area; permit required

odm-y56i2l.name: Fuikbaai / Newport
odm-y56i2l.access: Newport is only dived with Ocean Encounters
highlights: Slope with star coral, brain coral and soft gorgonians
Described as pristine
sources: Bluewater Dive Travel (Scuba Lodge & Ocean Suites)

odm-y5ivxz.name: Cenote Kukulcan
highlights: Very clear water, white limestone walls
hazards: Halocline near 35 ft

odm-y5w6mz.name: Cherubs Cave
highlights: Grey nurse sharks in winter
sources: Nigel Marsh Photography (Scuba Diver magazine article)

odm-y74gl7.name: Wye Reef
highlights: Reef beside Buck Island Cove; no wreckage remains

odm-y78g93.name: Julian Rocks - Nursery
highlights: Abundant reef fish and turtles
odm-y78g93.summary: The shallow, sheltered western side of Julian Rocks, about 5-12 m, and the usual choice for beginners. Reef fish are abundant and turtles are often seen.

odm-y79c9b.name: SAS Pietermaritzburg, wreck
odm-y79c9b.summary: Former navy minesweeper scuttled as an artificial reef at Miller's Point near Simon's Town in 1994. It rests upright on sand at about 22 m, with the bow deck near 17 m, and is breaking up so the interior is less accessible than before.

odm-y7xwj9.name: Teavanui Pass
highlights: Sharks, eagle rays, mantas, napoleon wrasse
odm-y7xwj9.summary: A drift dive through Bora Bora's only channel to the open ocean, riding the current from the outer reef into the lagoon. Sharks, eagle rays, jacks and napoleon wrasse use the pass, and occasionally mantas, along coloured coral walls.

odm-y8mzcp.name: Lighthouse
highlights: Shallow sand patch beside the channel and wall

odm-y9ldif.name: Harbor Reef / Pilot Boat
highlights: Sunken tugboat on a gently sloping soft-coral reef
odm-y9ldif.summary: Small sunken tugboat off the cruise-ship port in roughly 25-30 m, set on a gently sloping reef with plenty of soft coral.

odm-yapw3y.name: A-frame Cape Town
highlights: Granite outcrops with a couple of swim-throughs
hazards: Within a marine sanctuary boundary

odm-yazdvs.name: Teonai
highlights: Eagle rays and reef sharks

odm-ye0ez9.name: Halifax Point
hazards: Very strong currents - dive at slack tide only

odm-yfty64.name: Black Hills
highlights: Barracuda, spadefish, jacks and king mackerel
hazards: Potentially strong current at depth
odm-yfty64.summary: A seamount a few miles off Utila's south shore, rising to about 35 ft and falling past 130 ft. Current brings schools of barracuda, jacks and spadefish, and strong flow means it is reserved for advanced divers.

odm-ygd1bh.name: Halik, Gili Trawangan
highlights: Gorgonian fans and massive barrel sponges
odm-ygd1bh.summary: Drift-friendly reef off Gili Trawangan that begins around 6 m with healthy coral and turns into canyons and ridges toward 40 m. A gentle current suits divers of most levels.

odm-yh72t8.name: Msumbiji
odm-yh72t8.summary: A compact reef with soft and hard corals on slopes and short walls, plus coral spires with archways and overhangs away from the main formation. Visibility can be unpredictable.

odm-yi4gvw.name: Jardin Japonais
highlights: Natural arch and dense juvenile fish nursery
odm-yi4gvw.summary: A small colourful sec just north of Pointe Malendure, dropping from the surface to about 25 m below volcanic cliffs. A natural arch and dense coral make it a fish nursery, suited to everyone from beginners to experienced divers.

odm-yi71q1.name: Cement Plant
highlights: Seahorses, frogfish, lobster under the cement pier
odm-yi71q1.summary: A shallow dive around a working cement-factory pier on Barbados's west coast, bottoming out near 30 ft. Seahorses, frogfish and lobsters make it a good macro and night dive for beginners.

odm-yj6xzo.name: Valleys - Grenada
highlights: Sandy channel with coral finger reef

odm-yswlwd.name: Man O War Shoal
highlights: Green turtles, reef sharks, stingrays, lobster
sources: Saba Conservation Foundation (Saba National Marine Park)

odm-ytki35.name: El Rincon - Acapulco
highlights: Artificial reefs and a tunnel full of fish

odm-z02qmy.name: Mikadini
highlights: Mid-size groupers, blue-spotted trevally

odm-z0qxa0.name: Faille de Poe
highlights: Turtles, several shark species, rays
odm-z0qxa0.summary: A narrow channel cut through the reef at Poé, formerly a river bed, running about 20 m deep and linking lagoon to ocean. Experienced divers meet turtles, sharks and rays here.

odm-z222sp.name: Prince Albert, wreck
highlights: Eagle rays, southern stingrays and squid pass by
odm-z222sp.summary: An upright 140 ft vessel resting in about 65 ft of water on Roatán's south shore, a few fin kicks from the CoCo View resort. It is easy to reach from shore, popular for night dives, and heavily covered in coral growth.

odm-z2atie.name: Lonsdale Wall
highlights: Overhangs and ledges covered in zoanthids and sponges
hazards: Best at slack water or as a drift dive

odm-z3jift.name: Fly Point
highlights: Sponge gardens in 17-22 m
Pineapple fish, wobbegongs, nudibranchs
odm-z3jift.summary: Easy Nelson Bay shore dive via steps and a handrail, popular for training. Ledges run along the shore with sponge gardens deeper out. Currents are strong so it is dived at slack tide.

odm-z5ilc0.name: Uepi Point
highlights: Soft corals and sea fans
Reef sharks, trevally and barracuda schools
hazards: Giant triggerfish in the channel

odm-z65dqt.name: Shangri La - Playa del Carmen
highlights: Occasional turtle, seahorses and nudibranchs

odm-z8q0lz.name: Laje de Santos - Boca da Baleia
highlights: Rock formation with fish and turtles

odm-z8raaj.name: Aquarium Gros Ilets
highlights: Thousands of fish and lobsters
odm-z8raaj.summary: A sheltered dive a few minutes' boat ride from Gustavia, nicknamed the Aquarium for its dense fish and lobsters. Shallow, clear and nearly current-free, it is a classic first dive on Saint-Barthélemy.

odm-zg902p.name: Mary’s Place
odm-zg902p.depthNote: Elbow-shaped plateau 30-60 ft; vertical walls to about 120 ft
highlights: Deep crevices and canyons cutting the plateau
Macro life in the coral canyons
hazards: Often busy with several dive groups
odm-zg902p.summary: One of Roatán's best-known dives, an elbow-shaped reef plateau on the south shore that is split by deep crevices and canyons and bordered by vertical walls. It is rich in macro life but popular, so groups can queue up.

odm-zgdh07.name: Temae
highlights: Blacktip sharks, turtles, tuna, garden eels
odm-zgdh07.summary: An easy dive off Moorea's east coast in front of Temae village: a coral shelf gives way to a gentle slope. Mild current and good visibility suit divers of all levels, with blacktip sharks, turtles and a garden-eel nursery.

odm-zh3qg6.name: La Piscine de Salomon
highlights: Bigeye jacks, parrotfish, turtles among rocky blocks
odm-zh3qg6.summary: The northern circuit at Cap Salomon, a colourful and relaxed dive weaving through rocky blocks and coral. Bigeye jacks, parrotfish and turtles are the draw, and a small cave can be entered.

odm-zikl9d.name: Ribbon Reef - 5 Mile
highlights: Ribbon eels and macro life
Blacktip reef sharks and turtles
odm-zikl9d.summary: Two small rocky outcrops on Five Mile Reef, similar to Stringer but larger and deeper at 16-19 m. A favourite with macro photographers for ribbon eels, scorpionfish and anemones, with blacktip sharks and turtles often around.

odm-zin08z.name: Urquharts Bay
highlights: Scallops, octopus
hazards: Possible low visibility
Boat channel and moorings close to shore

odm-zp8hiu.name: Mamaru
highlights: Blacktip and whitetip reef sharks, turtles

odm-zs9b2s.name: Pinnacles
highlights: Potholes, gullies and swim-throughs
Manta rays in season
odm-zs9b2s.summary: A spine of rock formations rising to about 6 m below the surface at the north end of Aliwal Shoal, cut by gullies, potholes and swim-throughs. Mantas, rays and potato bass are regular sightings and the depth tops out near 17-18 m.

odm-zvbfl0.name: Salem Express, wreck
odm-zvbfl0.penetration: Penetration frowned upon; many guides refuse as it is a maritime grave
highlights: Two giant propellers and rudder
Personal items still lie on the seabed
hazards: Currents can be strong
Memorial wreck; many guides will not dive it
odm-zvbfl0.summary: A ferry lost in 1991 near Safaga, now on her side on sand with her highest point near 7 m and her deepest about 27 to 30 m. A sombre, advanced boat dive on a grave site, where penetration is discouraged.

odm-zzveh1.name: Beacon Point
highlights: Largest pillar coral formation in the Caribbean
Drop-off with barracuda, groupers, nurse sharks and jacks
hazards: Sometimes strong current
odm-zzveh1.summary: Boat dive on Curaçao's south coast with a stunning drop-off, big pillar coral and predators such as barracuda and nurse sharks. Current can be strong, so it suits experienced divers.
sources: Bluewater Dive Travel (Scuba Lodge & Ocean Suites)

osm-n1245126314.name: HMS Maori
hazards: Sharp collapsing edges; avoid penetration
Silt reduces visibility to zero
osm-n1245126314.summary: Broken destroyer remains lying upright on sand in St Elmo Bay by the Marsamxett entrance, at about 12 to 16 m. One of Malta's few shallow wrecks, entered from shore and suitable for newer divers, though silt and sharp metal call for care.

osm-n12601944496.name: Lofthus
osm-n12601944496.access: Florida Underwater Archaeological Preserve, open free year-round; anchor in sand
hazards: Sand movement buries or exposes parts of the wreck
osm-n12601944496.summary: An 1898 iron barque wrecked and later blasted, leaving a scattered wreck site just off Manalapan near Boynton Beach in about 15 to 20 feet. It is a state archaeological preserve suited to snorkelers and new divers.

osm-n1374397322.name: Echtzer See, Tauchereinstieg am DLRG-Haus
osm-n1374397322.access: Local dive club members and their guests only

osm-n1485422409.name: Pantai Merah
osm-n1485422409.depthNote: Sources also call Pantai Merah Pink Beach.

osm-n1817672135.name: Silfra Diving
osm-n1817672135.depthNote: Park limit 18 m; fissure itself reaches 63 m (technical only)
osm-n1817672135.access: National park rules: buddy required, dry suit certificate or 10 dry suit dives, no overhead entry
hazards: Very cold water; dry suit required
osm-n1817672135.summary: A water-filled fissure between the North American and Eurasian plates in Thingvellir National Park, known for extremely clear 2-4 C water. Dives are capped at 18 m, need a dry suit and a buddy, and stay out of caves.

osm-n2171849465.name: Glenlyon
osm-n2171849465.summary: A steel package freighter wrecked on Isle Royale's Glenlyon Shoals in 1924. The cold lake has preserved the bow, engine room and cabin in shallow water, and the open-to-the-public wreck is far less visited than other park wrecks.

osm-n2366251593.name: Le France
highlights: Wheelhouse, engine rooms and billiard room intact
osm-n2366251593.summary: A lake steamer that sank in 1971 off the Impérial Palace in Annecy and lies at 42 m. Dived year-round with local clubs by experienced divers, it is well preserved, with wheelhouse, engine rooms and billiard salon.

osm-n2479149211.name: Exsurgence de Port-Miou
osm-n2479149211.reason: Underground river reserved for scientific research and exploration, closed to visitors

osm-n255316037.name: SS Thistlegorm
osm-n255316037.penetration: Holds 1 to 3 can be swum through at up to 25 m
highlights: BSA motorbikes, trucks and cars in the holds
Ship largely intact, upright on sand
hazards: Currents can be strong
osm-n255316037.summary: A British freighter bombed in 1941 and now sitting upright on sand at about 30 m in the Gulf of Suez, with her wartime cargo of vehicles and motorbikes still stowed in the holds. A deep, advanced boat dive.

osm-n2628832137.name: Laguna Reef
hazards: Strong tidal flows dictate the dive plan
osm-n2628832137.summary: A shallow hard-coral lagoon on the west of Tiran island, split in two by a coral wall into North and South Laguna, with a drift along the outer wall suited to all levels. Tidal flow controls when and how it is dived.

osm-n270804074.name: Richelieu Rock
osm-n270804074.access: Inside Surin Islands National Park; open only in the dry season
highlights: Whale sharks and mantas, Feb-Apr
Harlequin shrimp under overhangs
Schools of barracuda and mackerel
hazards: Currents can strengthen mid-dive around the horseshoe
osm-n270804074.summary: Isolated horseshoe-shaped pinnacle in Mu Ko Surin National Park, rising from about 35 m to just below the surface. Famed for purple soft corals, macro life and occasional whale sharks; currents can be strong and the park is open only in the dry season.

osm-n271181711.name: The Bells
highlights: Chimney descent lit by sun rays
Cleaner fish station at about 18 m
hazards: Narrow chimney entry; mini arch at 26 m is not the Arch
osm-n271181711.summary: A shore entry through a narrow reef chimney that exits onto a wall at about 26-28 m, then follows the wall to the saddle into the Blue Hole. Guided centres take qualified divers to 30 m.

osm-n3149301713.name: Weeki Wachee Spring
osm-n3149301713.depthNote: Cave-system maximum, not a normal open-water dive depth. Technical cave training is required.
osm-n3149301713.access: Cave entry only practical when spring discharge is unusually low (as in 2007)
highlights: Deepest known freshwater cave system in the US

osm-n3167637595.name: Troy Spring
highlights: Civil War steamboat Madison scuttled in 1863
osm-n3167637595.summary: A 70-ft-deep spring on the Suwannee River whose main draw is the steamboat Madison, scuttled in 1863 to keep it from capture. Open for swimming, snorkeling and diving.

osm-n356542710.name: Edmonds Underwater Park
osm-n356542710.access: No diving within 100 yards of ferry landing; no night diving without permit
hazards: Steel dry dock interferes with compass
Long swims from shore
osm-n356542710.summary: A city-run shore-entry underwater park beside the Edmonds ferry dock, with a sunken dry dock, boats and reef structures linked by guide ropes. Popular with newer divers, though visibility varies and swims are long.

osm-n3582426705.name: Mango Bay
highlights: Schools of fusiliers and snapper in the shallows
Whiprays under big boulders
osm-n3582426705.summary: Sheltered, sandy-bottomed bay on Ko Tao with boulders and shallow reef, reached by boat. Mostly 2-15 m with light current, so it suits training dives and beginners.

osm-n369172549.name: Shaws Cove
highlights: Lobster, sheephead, garibaldi, bat rays

osm-n371470562.name: Terlinden
osm-n371470562.depthNote: Wall starts around 33 m and continues deeper
hazards: Dark below 15 m; lamp needed

osm-n4031617721.name: Fujikawa Maru
highlights: Disassembled Zero fighters in forward hold
Bow gun on the foredeck
osm-n4031617721.summary: A Japanese cargo ship sunk in Operation Hailstone in 1944 and now among the most popular wreck dives in Chuuk Lagoon, with aircraft stowed in its forward hold and a gun on the bow.

osm-n408451459.name: Shaab Claudio
highlights: Shallow cave system with light shafts
osm-n408451459.summary: A shallow reef in the Fury Shoals with a spacious, partly open-roofed cave network, popular for sunbeams and photography. Maximum depth is about 16 m, though currents can be strong on the approach.

osm-n4159831390.name: P31 - Patrol Boat
osm-n4159831390.summary: Former Maltese patrol boat sunk in 2009 as an artificial reef off Comino's west coast, lying at about 16 to 20 m. Boat access only, and gentle enough to count as beginner level.

osm-n5760423321.name: Sebayor Kecil Dive Site
osm-n5760423321.depthNote: Catalog spelling is Sebayor; sources call the island and site Sebayur Kecil.

osm-n5767096953.name: Cystal Rock Dive Site
osm-n5767096953.depthNote: Catalog spelling is Cystal Rock; sources call the site Crystal Rock.
highlights: Barracuda schools, grey and whitetip reef sharks
hazards: Strong current; reef hook recommended
osm-n5767096953.summary: A current-swept seamount pinnacle in northern Komodo National Park, known for clear water and abundant sharks and pelagics. Best for confident divers comfortable with drifts and hooks.

osm-n663869446.name: USS Oriskany
osm-n663869446.depthNote: Island top 84 ft, flight deck ~145 ft, seafloor 212 ft
highlights: Island structure within recreational depths
Hangar bay open to tech divers
hazards: Below 135 ft requires technical training
osm-n663869446.summary: A huge decommissioned aircraft carrier sunk upright off Pensacola as an artificial reef. Recreational divers visit the island superstructure while the flight deck and hangar bay below call for advanced or technical training.
sources: Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission

osm-n663869447.name: USS Massachusetts
highlights: Turrets, cupolas and anchor chain
Goliath groupers and turtles
hazards: Strong surge and low visibility at wrong tide
osm-n663869447.summary: A pre-dreadnought battleship scuttled in very shallow water near Pensacola Pass. Its turrets sit close to the surface and attract a full reef community; timing the dive for slack high tide keeps surge and silt down.

osm-n663869451.name: San Pablo
highlights: Boilers, refrigeration coils and twisted steel
Dense toadfish population
osm-n663869451.summary: A WWII freighter destroyed in a secret 1944 weapons test, now a Florida Panhandle Shipwreck Trail dive off Pensacola. The scattered wreckage covers a wide stretch of sand, with boilers and plating that hold plenty of fish.

osm-n663869458.name: S.S. Inchulva / Delray Wreck
osm-n663869458.summary: The remains of a steamship wrecked in a 1903 hurricane lie just off Delray Beach's public beach in about 25 ft of water. The shallow depth and short distance from shore make it a popular first wreck for newer divers and snorkelers.

osm-n663869492.name: Bedfordshire (Wreck)
highlights: WWII British armed trawler lying in two sections
hazards: Unexploded depth charges near the stern
osm-n663869492.summary: A British anti-submarine trawler torpedoed off Cape Lookout in 1942, lying in about 105 ft in Gulf Stream water. The broken hull is a war grave, so divers look and do not penetrate.

osm-n663869494.name: U-701 (Wreck)
osm-n663869494.depthNote: Pin is ~3400 m deep; likely misplaced
hazards: Current swings from slight to very swift
Shifting sand changes what is exposed
osm-n663869494.summary: A WWII U-boat partly buried in sand about 20 miles off Cape Hatteras, where Gulf Stream and Labrador Current meet. Visibility and current vary widely, and the sand covers or exposes the hull year to year.

osm-n663869496.name: U-85 (Wreck)
highlights: Torpedo tubes with torpedoes still inside
Deck gun and conning tower
Sand tiger sharks
hazards: Visibility and temperature swing with shifting currents
osm-n663869496.summary: The first U-boat sunk off the US coast in WWII, lying on its side about 14 miles off Oregon Inlet. Battle damage, torpedo tubes and the conning tower are visible, but conditions change with the currents.

osm-n663869497.name: U-352 (Wreck)
highlights: Amberjacks and great barracuda around the hull
osm-n663869497.summary: A German U-boat sunk in 1942, sitting largely intact in about 110 ft of Gulf Stream water off Morehead City. It draws baitfish and big predators; penetration is not permitted.

osm-n663869498.name: Indra (Wreck)
highlights: Abundant marine life; occasional sand tigers

osm-n663869499.name: Aeolus (Wreck)
highlights: Sand tiger sharks
Multi-level dive on a broken-up hull
osm-n663869499.summary: A 409 ft former cable ship sunk as a reef in 1988 and later broken into three sections by hurricanes, giving a multi-level wreck dive. Sand tigers often shelter on it.

osm-n663869517.name: Water Witch
highlights: One of the oldest intact commercial sailing ships
hazards: Zero visibility after heavy rain (Otter Creek runoff)
Surface and bottom currents
Fragile wreck; control buoyancy
osm-n663869517.summary: A remarkably intact lake sailing vessel resting about a quarter mile south of Diamond Island on Lake Champlain, within a Vermont underwater preserve. At about 90 ft with lights required, it suits very experienced divers.

osm-n663869518.name: Phoenix
osm-n663869518.depthNote: Bow 60 ft, stern 110 ft; buoy anchor pad about 50 ft
osm-n663869518.mooring: Preserve buoy; anchor pad about 50 ft down
highlights: Fire-charred framing and massive hull
hazards: Steep wreck angle can disorient divers
Lights needed; deep open-lake site needs planning
osm-n663869518.summary: A burned 19th-century paddle steamer lying on the north side of Colchester Shoal, protected as a Vermont underwater preserve. The hull slopes from roughly 60 ft at the bow to 110 ft at the stern; it is rated advanced and calls for lights and careful planning.

osm-n663869519.name: Burlington Bay Horse Ferry
osm-n663869519.access: Free, but divers must register annually
highlights: Only known surviving turntable horse ferry
Paddle wheels with iron hubs and oak spokes
hazards: Fragile paddle wheels; do not touch
Low visibility if bottom is stirred
osm-n663869519.summary: A 63-ft horse-powered ferry, the only known surviving turntable team-boat, lying at about 50 ft in Burlington Bay. A fragile intermediate-level preserve dive; hover and avoid touching the paddle wheels.

osm-n663869520.name: Champlain II
osm-n663869520.access: Free, but divers must register annually; shoreline is private
highlights: 163 ft of the 244 ft steamboat hull remains
Massive engine mounts on either side
hazards: Silty bottom, limited visibility
Zebra mussels cut hands; wear gloves
Unstable sternpost, overhanging sections
osm-n663869520.summary: A shallow Lake Champlain preserve wreck: the remaining 163 ft of an 1868 steamboat hull lies in 15-35 ft near the New York shore north of Westport. Easy beginner dive; keep off the silty bottom.

osm-n663869521.name: O.J. Walker
osm-n663869521.access: Free, but divers must register annually
highlights: Ship's wheel and aft cabin hatch cover
Masts, boom, anchors and rigging on site
hazards: Do not penetrate the wreck
Low visibility if bottom is stirred
osm-n663869521.summary: An 86-ft schooner-rigged canal boat lost in a storm in 1895, lying at about 65 ft off the Burlington breakwater. A state preserve dive for intermediate or experienced divers, with the wheel and rigging still on the wreck.

osm-n663869522.name: General Butler
osm-n663869522.access: Free, but divers must register annually
highlights: Remarkably intact 1862 canal schooner, upright
Windlass, cleats and dead-eyes in place
hazards: Extremely fragile rudder at the stern
Poor buoyancy control damages the wreck
osm-n663869522.summary: An upright 88-ft sailing canal boat from 1862 that struck the Burlington breakwater in a gale. At about 40 ft it is a beginner dive in a state preserve, with deck hatches and sailing hardware still in place.

osm-n663869532.name: Cedarville (Wreck)
osm-n663869532.mooring: Bow and stern mooring buoys, typically late May to mid-September
osm-n663869532.penetration: Penetration not advised without proper training, experience and equipment
highlights: Huge upside-down lake freighter
hazards: Large, deep, inverted wreck with variable visibility
osm-n663869532.summary: A big lake freighter lost in a 1965 collision east of the Mackinac Bridge, now lying inverted in the Straits of Mackinac Shipwreck Preserve from about 40 to 110 ft. Moorings make it reachable, but size, depth and poor visibility demand caution.

osm-n663869534.name: Panther (Wreck)
osm-n663869534.summary: A wooden grain steamer rammed in Whitefish Bay in 1916 and found in 1975, now resting at roughly 90 to 110 ft in the Whitefish Point Underwater Preserve on Lake Superior.

osm-n663869535.name: Sweepstakes (schooner)
osm-n663869535.summary: A schooner wreck lying in only about 6 m of water at Big Tub Harbour, inside Fathom Five National Marine Park near Tobermory. Shallow and easy, it is visited by divers, snorkelers and glass-bottom tour boats.

osm-n663869549.name: UB-81
osm-n663869549.reason: Designated controlled site under Protection of Military Remains Act 1986; diving prohibited

osm-n663869563.name: Vivian Quarry
osm-n663869563.access: Operator-run site; entry fee; check current opening status
highlights: Flooded buildings, boats, van and a submarine
osm-n663869563.summary: A flooded slate quarry section at Llanberis with a platform at 6 m and a floor around 18-20 m. Divers pass old mine buildings, rails and sunken boats; entry is through the on-site dive operator.

osm-n663869622.name: SMS König
highlights: Upturned hull opened up by salvage blasting
Casemate guns lying upside down on seabed
hazards: Blast debris scattered along the hull
osm-n663869622.summary: Upturned WWI German battleship east of Cava, scuttled in 1919 and heavily broken by salvage blasting. Less impressive than her sisters but the openings reveal internal structure; the hull top is around 20 m.

osm-n663869624.name: SMS Markgraf
osm-n663869624.summary: Deepest of the three scuttled German battleships at Scapa Flow, lying upside down on its port side, with the hull rising to roughly 23 m above a seabed near 45 m. A demanding, deeper dive than its sisters.

osm-n663869630.name: SMS Cöln
osm-n663869630.summary: German light cruiser scuttled in 1919 and never raised, resting on her starboard side in Scapa Flow. Her top is about 22 m and the seabed 36 m, and she is a straightforward wreck for competent sport divers.

osm-n663869632.name: SMS Kronprinz Wilhelm
highlights: Half of the 12-inch guns still visible
Engine and boiler rooms explorable
osm-n663869632.summary: Upturned German battleship scuttled in 1919 in Scapa Flow, the shallowest of the big three. Its hull top is near 12-14 m and several main guns can be seen, making it the most approachable battleship dive.

osm-n663869681.name: Umbria
highlights: Holds still stacked with bombs and trucks
hazards: Munitions remain aboard the wreck
osm-n663869681.summary: A large Italian ship scuttled in 1940 near Wingate Reef, close to Port Sudan. It rests tilted on its port side with the top only a few metres down, still carrying its wartime cargo, and is regarded as one of the Red Sea's best wreck dives.

osm-n663869688.name: Le Liban
osm-n663869688.summary: A steam liner that sank in a collision in 1903 and now lies on its keel behind Île Maïre off Marseille. The bow is wedged in rocks near 32 m and the stern is at about 36 m; the front holds can be entered.

osm-n663869697.name: Rubis
osm-n663869697.summary: A French minelaying submarine lying upright on white sand off Cap Camarat near Ramatuelle. The deck sits around 34 m and the sand around 41 m, so it suits experienced divers, and currents and wind exposure are frequent.

osm-n663869712.name: Baron Gautsch
osm-n663869712.access: Only via dive centres with a Croatian Ministry of Culture permit
osm-n663869712.penetration: Entry allowed only through the first two decks

osm-n663869765.name: Abu Galawa Kebir
osm-n663869765.depthNote: Wreck 5-18 m; surrounding reef to about 35 m
osm-n663869765.summary: Small Chinese vessel sunk in 1943 on the Abu Galawa Kebir reef in the Fury Shoals. It lies shallow, roughly 5 to 18 m, and has long since grown into the reef, with the reef itself falling to about 35 m.

osm-n663869769.name: Hamada
highlights: Parts shallow enough to snorkel
Intact propeller
osm-n663869769.summary: A roughly 65 m cargo ship lying on its side on an inshore reef at Abu Ghosum south of Marsa Alam, in only about 14 m of water. Easy and photogenic, suitable for all experience levels.

osm-n663869779.name: Numidia
osm-n663869779.depthNote: Big Brother, bow near reef top, stern ~70-80 m
hazards: Strong current, risk of being swept off the reef
Prop lies beyond recreational depth
osm-n663869779.summary: A long steamship wreck on the Big Brother reef, reached only by liveaboard. The bow sits near 8 m while the hull falls past 80 m, so most divers see the upper sections in a current that can be fierce.

osm-n663869780.name: Aida
osm-n663869780.depthNote: Wreck at Big Brother; pin is Little Brother side area
hazards: Severe current exposure
osm-n663869780.summary: A small supply ship wrecked on the Brothers reef and now lying on a steep slope. It is a demanding, current-swept dive for experienced wreck divers, reachable only from liveaboards.

osm-n663869792.name: Shaab Sabrina
osm-n663869792.mooring: Boats moor on the southern reef side

osm-n663869809.name: Carnatic
osm-n663869809.penetration: Easy entry and exit through the open iron framework
highlights: Sea fans covering the skeletal ribs
hazards: Current can be strong and shift quickly
osm-n663869809.summary: A 19th-century iron steamship wreck on Abu Nuhas, resting on its port side with the bow far shallower than the stern. The open framework is easy to swim through and heavily covered in sea fans and coral.

osm-n663869810.name: Chrisoula K
osm-n663869810.penetration: Full penetration possible in certain areas for experienced wreck divers
highlights: Cargo of floor tiles still stacked in crates
hazards: Current can be strong and shift quickly
osm-n663869810.summary: An upright cargo freighter on Abu Nuhas whose bow almost reaches the surface and whose stern rests near 28 m. Its hold still contains stacked tiles and experienced wreck divers can enter parts of the interior.

osm-n663869811.name: Kimon M
osm-n663869811.penetration: Engineering department and holds are fairly easy to enter
highlights: Large groupers and schooling snappers
hazards: Current can be strong and shift quickly
osm-n663869811.summary: The deepest of the four Abu Nuhas wrecks, a freighter that slid off the reef to rest around 30 m. Divers can reach the engine spaces and holds, and groupers and snappers gather on the hull.

osm-n663869812.name: Giannis D
highlights: Glassfish clouds and trevally around the mast
Engine room, crew quarters and bridge to explore
hazards: Disorienting tilted interior
Current can be strong and shift quickly
osm-n663869812.summary: A large cargo ship lying on its side on Abu Nuhas reef, with the mast near the surface and the stern around 24 m. Experienced wreck divers can swim into the engine room and bridge, though the tilt is disorienting.

osm-n663869819.name: Dunraven
highlights: Inverted hull with swim-through by the boiler
Thousands of glassfish at the exit
osm-n663869819.summary: The Dunraven sank in 1876 on the Beacon Rock reef at the northwest edge of Ras Mohammed and now lies upside down in two sections, from about 15 m at the bow to 29-30 m at the stern, heavily encrusted with coral and glassfish.

osm-n663869830.name: Ras Umm Sid
osm-n663869830.depthNote: Pin id is Ras Umm Sid (Sharm); sources describe the Sharm site
highlights: Column of gorgonian fans from 14 to 28 m
Giant sea fan collections
hazards: Currents can be strong
osm-n663869830.summary: A fringing reef beneath the Ras Umm Sid lighthouse near Sharm el Sheikh, known for a band of large gorgonian sea fans along the wall and a coral garden on the plateau. Currents can pick up, so a drift suits it.

osm-n663869852.name: Kormoran
hazards: Dive only possible on very calm days
osm-n663869852.summary: A shallow cargo ship wreck lying in the Straits of Tiran since 1984, with its winch, engine and propeller all within about 12 m. Suitable for all levels but accessible only in very calm weather.

osm-n663869865.name: Ras Abu Galum
osm-n663869865.reason: Ras Abu Galum is a 400 sq km protectorate with several dive sites, not one site

osm-n663869869.name: Blue Hole
osm-n663869869.depthNote: Hole just over 100 m; Arch ceiling at 55 m
highlights: Saddle opening to the sea at about 6 m
Popular freediving venue
hazards: The Arch (ceiling 55 m) has killed many divers
Inward current through the Arch
osm-n663869869.summary: A circular sinkhole on the Gulf of Aqaba shore north of Dahab, just over 100 m deep, reached by walking in. Recreational divers keep to about 30 m on the Bells route; the Arch at 55 m is a notorious technical hazard.

osm-n663869872.name: Canyon
highlights: Open-topped canyon with glassfish and light shafts
Octopus, stonefish and scorpionfish
osm-n663869872.summary: A shore dive north of Dahab that crosses a shallow lagoon and coral garden to a deep open-topped fissure in the reef, filled with glassfish and lit by shafts of light. Intermediate level, roughly 5 to 30 m.

osm-n663869877.name: Cedar Pride
osm-n663869877.mooring: Boats tie up to a buoy about 200 m offshore
highlights: Overgrown crow's nest, much photographed
Good night dive site
osm-n663869877.summary: A Lebanese freighter deliberately sunk off Aqaba in 1985, now a coral-encrusted artificial reef lying on its port side. Its starboard side begins around 10 m, with gentle conditions that suit newer wreck divers.

osm-n663870011.name: Blausee
osm-n663870011.tempNote: mountain lake in winter diving season
osm-n663870011.access: Private lake; diving by advance booking with Hotel Blausee, November to March only

osm-n663870428.name: Die Jura (Wreck)
osm-n663870428.summary: Nineteenth-century paddle steamer rammed and sunk in Lake Constance in 1864, found again off Bottighofen in 1953. It sits nearly upright at 34 to 39 m, reached by boat, and is a well-known cold-water wreck for experienced divers.

osm-n663870469.name: Plansee - Zone 2 (Hotel Forelle)
osm-n663870469.access: Permit required; diving only in the marked dive zones

osm-n663870470.name: Plansee - Zone 1 (Schotterparkplatz Kaiserbrunnen)
osm-n663870470.access: Permit required; diving only in the marked dive zones

osm-n663870547.name: Bleibtreusee
osm-n663870547.access: Advance registration and day pass required

osm-n663870556.name: Wisseler See
osm-n663870556.access: Dive buoy mandatory (lake shared with sailors and surfers)

osm-n663870583.name: Diemelsee
osm-n663870583.reason: Whole reservoir (max depth 34 m), not a single dive site

osm-n663870585.name: Twistesee (Twistestausee)
osm-n663870585.reason: Whole reservoir, not a single dive site

osm-n663870616.name: Hohendeicher See
highlights: Diving bell and training platform
osm-n663870616.summary: A Hamburg gravel-pit lake with shore entries from the club jetty and the south beach. Divers practise around a submerged diving bell and training platform; most dives stay far shallower than the nominal 19 m depth.

osm-n6748047776.name: U-1105
osm-n6748047776.access: Maryland historic shipwreck preserve; no commercial charters operate there
hazards: Near-zero visibility and strong currents
osm-n6748047776.summary: A German Type VII submarine sunk in the Potomac after the war and now Maryland's first historic shipwreck preserve. It sits upright in deep, dark, current-swept water, so it is an advanced dive with a buoy on site in season.

osm-n7669564569.name: Pendennis Shore Dive
highlights: Remains of two WWI U-boats
Reef with gullies and sand patches
hazards: Summer boat traffic; use a surface marker
osm-n7669564569.summary: Easy Falmouth shore dive, known as Silver Steps, entered down granite steps to a gully-cut reef about 10 m deep at high tide. Pieces of two scuttled U-boats lie to the north-east.

osm-n8559506183.name: Thomas reef
highlights: Plateau with a row of large gorgonian fans
Whitetip and leopard sharks on the ledge
hazards: Strong currents at the north and south ends
Thomas Canyon runs to 90 m; technical divers only
osm-n8559506183.summary: The smallest and most colourful of the four Tiran reefs, dived as a drift along a wall of gorgonians to a plateau near 25 m, with sharks resting on the ledge. Currents can be strong at either end.

osm-n8577535117.name: סטי"ל
osm-n8577535117.depthNote: Bridge 12 m, bow 18 m, stern 21 m, sand about 24-25 m
osm-n8577535117.access: Shore entry via ramp at Village Beach, Eilat
osm-n8577535117.penetration: Semi-penetration at bow and stern; some parts sealed
highlights: Bridge covered in soft purple coral
osm-n8577535117.summary: A decommissioned Israeli Navy missile boat sunk off Eilat in 1994 as a reef. It sits upright on sand a short swim from Village Beach, with a bridge near 12 m and a deck around 20 m, and parts of the interior can be explored.

osm-n8730688077.name: D1
osm-n8730688077.access: Protected wreck; divers may visit but nothing may be removed
osm-n8730688077.summary: Early Royal Navy submarine scuttled off Dartmouth in 1918 and rediscovered by technical divers, sitting upright and largely intact. It is now protected, so you can look but must leave everything in place.

osm-n889067426.name: Fairy Cove
hazards: Occasional jet skis

osm-n9720994071.name: Shaab Rumi, Precontinent 2
highlights: Remains of Cousteau's undersea village
osm-n9720994071.summary: Remains of Cousteau's 1960s undersea habitat project on the Sha'ab Rumi reef off Sudan. Two structures were removed afterwards; the rest, including the submersible hangar and shark cages, is now a diveable relic.

osm-r11092421.name: Moucha Island
osm-r11092421.reason: A whole island with several dive sites around it, not one site

osm-r14353880.name: Brackett's Landing
osm-r14353880.depthNote: Brackett's Landing is the Edmonds Underwater Park site

osm-r168896.name: Schliersee
osm-r168896.reason: Whole lake (max depth 40.5 m), not a single dive site

osm-r20325186.name: HMS Port Napier
osm-r20325186.penetration: Possible through cut openings; take a twinset
highlights: Bow guns and kelp-covered port side
Light through cut openings in the hull
hazards: Shallow wreckage can hole a boat
Sharp metal at hull openings
osm-r20325186.summary: A minelayer lying on her starboard side in Loch Alsh off Skye, partly drying at low water. Wide range of dives from easy to penetration, reached by local charter boat from Kyle of Lochalsh or Kyleakin.

osm-w132766337.name: Dosthill Quarry
highlights: Training platforms at several depths
Plane, cars and vans on the bottom
hazards: Sudden drop-off to 24 m; needs good buoyancy
osm-w132766337.summary: A Staffordshire inland quarry with easy walk-in access, shallow training platforms and a steep drop to roughly 24-26 m. Sunken vehicles, a plane and trees add interest, and pike and sturgeon live there.

osm-w141329817.name: Eccleston Delph
highlights: Training platforms at 3-9 m
Rope lines linking underwater features
osm-w141329817.summary: A flooded Lancashire stone quarry used for training and fun diving, with platforms between 3 and 9 m, rope trails linking sunken features and a floor around 20 m. Visibility is typically 3-10 m.

osm-w23185891.name: Woodhouse Reef
osm-w23185891.mooring: No fixed moorings; drift south to north
highlights: Wall running from the surface down
Giant morays, groupers, barracuda and jacks
hazards: "Washing Machine" currents between Woodhouse and Jackson
osm-w23185891.summary: The longest reef in the Straits of Tiran, a wall dropping from the surface to about 30 m or more, dived as a south-to-north drift with a canyon midway. Currents build toward the north end where it meets Jackson Reef.

osm-w24661321.name: Friedberger Baggersee
highlights: Underwater cliffs and faults
osm-w24661321.summary: A gravel-pit lake near Augsburg popular with divers, with rocky underwater relief and unusually good clarity for a quarry lake. Depths reach roughly 12-15 m, and a paid permit is required.

osm-w24920367.name: Stoney Cove
highlights: Stanegarth tug, bus, Viscount cockpit, galleon
hazards: Deep silt can drop visibility to zero
